diff --git a/snapback4/crates/snapback4-lang/tests/wave12_semantics.rs b/snapback4/crates/snapback4-lang/tests/wave12_semantics.rs
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..a589ba9349
--- /dev/null
+++ b/snapback4/crates/snapback4-lang/tests/wave12_semantics.rs
@@ -0,0 +1,381 @@
+use snapback4_core::{Context, Engine, Value, WriteState};
+use snapback4_lang::{compile, types::Ty};
+use std::collections::BTreeMap;
+
+fn checked(source: &str) -> snapback4_lang::Bound {
+    let bound = compile(&[("schema.q".into(), source.into())]);
+    assert!(bound.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:#?}", bound.diagnostics);
+    bound
+}
+
+fn engine(source: &str) -> Engine {
+    let bound = checked(source);
+    Engine::memory(bound.schema, bound.programs.into_iter().map(|program| program.program)).unwrap()
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn global_count_is_zero_then_tracks_inserts_and_deletes() {
+    let source = r#"
+table entries:
+  public
+  insert <- allow
+  delete <- allow
+  online only
+table moderators:
+  principal: principal
+  unique principal
+  read <- .principal = viewer
+  online only
+view total: count entries
+  read <- allow
+  online only
+view privateTotal: count entries
+  read <- exists moderators[viewer]
+  online only
+mutation add(id: id):
+  return insert entries { id }
+mutation remove(id: entries):
+  delete entries[id]
+  return null
+query totalEntries():
+  return total
+query privateEntries():
+  return privateTotal
+"#;
+    let bound = checked(source);
+    let generated = snapback4_lang::emit::typescript(&bound);
+    let native = snapback4_lang::emit::rust::rust(&bound);
+    assert!(!generated.contains("$global") && !native.contains("$global"),
+        "the physical discriminator leaked into generated application types");
+    for expression in ["total first 1 by .id", "total[true]"] {
+        let bound = compile(&[("bad.q".into(), format!("{source}\nquery bad(c: cursor ?):\n  return {expression}\n"))]);
+        assert!(bound.diagnostics.iter().any(|diagnostic| diagnostic.code == "E_QUARRY_TYPE"
+            && diagnostic.message.contains("global maintained scalar")), "{expression}: {:#?}", bound.diagnostics);
+    }
+    let mut engine = engine(source);
+    let query = |engine: &mut Engine| engine.query("totalEntries", Context::new("alice", BTreeMap::new())).unwrap().data;
+    let private = |engine: &mut Engine, viewer| engine.query("privateEntries", Context::new(viewer, BTreeMap::new())).unwrap().data;
+    assert_eq!(query(&mut engine), Value::Int(0));
+    assert_eq!(private(&mut engine, "alice"), Value::Null, "an unauthorized empty global stays hidden");
+    engine.seed([("moderators".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([
+        ("id", Value::Id("mod".into())), ("principal", Value::Id("alice".into())),
+    ]))]).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(private(&mut engine, "alice"), Value::Int(0), "authorized absence is the count identity");
+    assert_eq!(private(&mut engine, "bob"), Value::Null, "a hidden absence is not zero");
+    for id in ["a", "b"] {
+        let outcome = engine.mutate("add", None, Context::new("alice", BTreeMap::from([("id".into(), Value::Id(id.into()))]))).unwrap();
+        assert!(matches!(outcome.state, WriteState::Sent { .. }), "{outcome:?}");
+    }
+    assert_eq!(query(&mut engine), Value::Int(2));
+    assert_eq!(private(&mut engine, "alice"), Value::Int(2));
+    assert_eq!(private(&mut engine, "bob"), Value::Null, "a hidden stored scalar remains null");
+    engine.mutate("remove", None, Context::new("alice", BTreeMap::from([("id".into(), Value::Id("a".into()))]))).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(query(&mut engine), Value::Int(1));
+    engine.mutate("remove", None, Context::new("alice", BTreeMap::from([("id".into(), Value::Id("b".into()))]))).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(query(&mut engine), Value::Int(0));
+    assert!(engine.store().rows("total").unwrap().is_empty(), "zero deletes the physical aggregate row");
+    assert!(engine.store().rows("privateTotal").unwrap().is_empty(), "private zero also has no physical row");
+}

+#[test]
+fn matching_role_guard_narrows_only_the_authorized_keyed_total() {
+    let source = r#"
+table entries:
+  owner: principal
+  public
+  online only
+table staff:
+  principal: principal
+  role: enum('finance')
+  unique principal, role
+  read <- .principal = viewer
+  delete <- .principal = viewer
+  online only
+view totals: count entries by .owner
+  read <- exists staff[principal = viewer, role = 'finance']
+  online only
+query raw(owner: principal):
+  return totals[owner]
+query guarded(owner: principal):
+  require exists staff[principal = viewer, role = 'finance'] else NOT_FINANCE
+  return totals[owner] + 1
+"#;
+    let bound = checked(source);
+    assert_eq!(bound.programs.iter().find(|program| program.program.name == "raw").unwrap().result, Ty::Int.optional());
+    assert_eq!(bound.programs.iter().find(|program| program.program.name == "guarded").unwrap().result, Ty::Int);
+    let mut engine = Engine::memory(bound.schema, bound.programs.into_iter().map(|program| program.program)).unwrap();
+    engine.seed([("entries".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([
+        ("id", Value::Id("one".into())), ("owner", Value::Id("bob".into())),
+    ]))]).unwrap();
+    let raw = |engine: &mut Engine, owner: &str| engine.query("raw", Context::new("alice", BTreeMap::from([
+        ("owner".into(), Value::Id(owner.into())),
+    ]))).unwrap().data;
+    assert_eq!(raw(&mut engine, "bob"), Value::Null, "a hidden stored total is not disclosed");
+    assert_eq!(raw(&mut engine, "nobody"), Value::Null, "a hidden miss is indistinguishable from a hidden hit");
+    engine.seed([("staff".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([
+        ("id", Value::Id("finance".into())), ("principal", Value::Id("alice".into())),
+        ("role", Value::String("finance".into())),
+    ]))]).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(raw(&mut engine, "bob"), Value::Int(1));
+    assert_eq!(raw(&mut engine, "nobody"), Value::Int(0), "an authorized keyed miss has the count identity");
+    assert_eq!(engine.query("guarded", Context::new("alice", BTreeMap::from([
+        ("owner".into(), Value::Id("nobody".into())),
+    ]))).unwrap().data, Value::Int(1));
+
+    let stale = compile(&[("schema.q".into(), format!(r#"{source}
+mutation stale(owner: principal, grant: staff):
+  require exists staff[principal = viewer, role = 'finance'] else NOT_FINANCE
+  delete staff[grant]
+  return totals[owner] + 1
+"#))]);
+    assert!(stale.diagnostics.iter().any(|diagnostic| diagnostic.code == "E_QUARRY_TYPE"
+        && diagnostic.message.contains("int ?")), "a write must invalidate the role proof: {:#?}", stale.diagnostics);
+}

+        let error = engine.query("echo", Context::new("alice", BTreeMap::from([("email".into(), Value::String(email.into()))]))).unwrap_err();

+    }
+}

+#[test]
+fn rounded_division_is_exact_signed_and_keeps_numeric_types() {
+    let source = r#"
+query rounded():
+  return [
+    divide(5, 2, 'toward-zero'), divide(5, 2, 'away-from-zero'),
+    divide(5, 2, 'floor'), divide(5, 2, 'ceiling'),
+    divide(5, 2, 'half-away-from-zero'), divide(5, 2, 'half-even'),
+    divide(7, 2, 'half-even'), divide(-5, 2, 'half-away-from-zero'),
+    divide(-5, 2, 'floor'), divide(-5, 2, 'ceiling'),
+    divide(5, -2, 'floor'), divide(5, -2, 'ceiling'),
+    divide(7, 3, 'half-even'), divide(8, 3, 'half-even')
+  ]
+query decimalValue(value: decimal 2):
+  return divide(value, 2, 'half-even')
+query moneyValue(value: money USD 2):
+  return divide(value, 2, 'half-even')
+query scaled(numerator: int, denominator: int):
+  return [
+    divide(numerator, denominator, 2, 'half-even'),
+    divide(numerator, denominator, 2, 'half-away-from-zero')
+  ]
+query wide(numerator: int, denominator: int):
+  return divide(numerator, denominator, 12, 'half-even')
+query scaleZero(numerator: int, denominator: int):
+  return divide(numerator, denominator, 0, 'half-even')
+query scaledOverflow():
+  return divide(9007199254740991, 1, 1, 'half-even')
+query zero():
+  return divide(1, 0, 'half-even')
+"#;
+    let bound = checked(source);
+    assert_eq!(bound.programs.iter().find(|p| p.program.name == "decimalValue").unwrap().result, Ty::Decimal(2));
+    assert_eq!(bound.programs.iter().find(|p| p.program.name == "moneyValue").unwrap().result, Ty::Money("USD".into(), 2));
+    let mut engine = Engine::memory(bound.schema, bound.programs.into_iter().map(|p| p.program)).unwrap();
+    let values = engine.query("rounded", Context::new("alice", BTreeMap::new())).unwrap().data;
+    assert_eq!(values, Value::Array([2, 3, 2, 3, 3, 2, 4, -3, -3, -2, -3, -2, 2, 3].into_iter().map(Value::Int).collect()));
+    for name in ["decimalValue", "moneyValue"] {
+        let value = engine.query(name, Context::new("alice", BTreeMap::from([("value".into(), Value::Int(5))]))).unwrap().data;
+        assert_eq!(value, Value::Int(2), "{name}");
+    }
+    let scaled = |engine: &mut Engine, numerator, denominator| engine.query("scaled", Context::new("alice", BTreeMap::from([
+        ("numerator".into(), Value::Int(numerator)), ("denominator".into(), Value::Int(denominator)),
+    ]))).unwrap().data;
+    assert_eq!(scaled(&mut engine, 101, 2), Value::Array(vec![Value::Int(5050), Value::Int(5050)]));
+    assert_eq!(scaled(&mut engine, -101, 2), Value::Array(vec![Value::Int(-5050), Value::Int(-5050)]));
+    assert_eq!(scaled(&mut engine, 1, 8), Value::Array(vec![Value::Int(12), Value::Int(13)]));
+    assert_eq!(scaled(&mut engine, -1, 8), Value::Array(vec![Value::Int(-12), Value::Int(-13)]));
+    assert_eq!(engine.query("wide", Context::new("alice", BTreeMap::from([
+        ("numerator".into(), Value::Int(snapback4_core::value::I53_MAX)),
+        ("denominator".into(), Value::Int(snapback4_core::value::I53_MAX)),
+    ]))).unwrap().data, Value::Int(1_000_000_000_000), "the wide scaled intermediate is not restricted to i53");
+    assert_eq!(engine.query("scaleZero", Context::new("alice", BTreeMap::from([
+        ("numerator".into(), Value::Int(5)), ("denominator".into(), Value::Int(2)),
+    ]))).unwrap().data, Value::Int(2));
+    assert_eq!(engine.query("scaledOverflow", Context::new("alice", BTreeMap::new())).unwrap_err().code, "E_OVERFLOW");
+    assert_eq!(engine.query("zero", Context::new("alice", BTreeMap::new())).unwrap_err().code, "E_DIV_ZERO");
+
+    use snapback4_core::ir::{Builtin, Expr, Program, ProgramKind, Rounding, Stmt};
+    let overflow = Program {
+        name: "overflow".into(), kind: ProgramKind::Query, args: BTreeMap::new(),
+        read_time_granularity_ms: None, native: false, returned_shapes: BTreeMap::new(),
+        body: vec![Stmt::Return(Expr::Builtin { builtin: Builtin::Divide { rounding: Rounding::TowardZero, scale: None },
+            args: vec![Expr::Literal(Value::Int(i64::MIN)), Expr::Literal(Value::Int(-1))] })],
+    };
+    let mut raw = Engine::memory(Default::default(), [overflow]).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(raw.query("overflow", Context::new("alice", BTreeMap::new())).unwrap_err().code, "E_OVERFLOW");
+
+    for bad in ["divide(1, 2, 'nearest')", "divide(1, 2, mode)", "divide(1, divisor, 'half-even')",
+        "divide(1, 2, 13, 'half-even')", "divide(1, 2, scale, 'half-even')"] {
+        let source = if bad.contains("mode") { format!("query bad(mode: enum('half-even')):\n  return {bad}\n") }
+            else if bad.contains("scale") { format!("query bad(scale: int):\n  return {bad}\n") }
+            else if bad.contains("divisor") { format!("query bad(divisor: decimal 2):\n  return {bad}\n") }
+            else { format!("query bad():\n  return {bad}\n") };
+        let bound = compile(&[("bad.q".into(), source)]);
+        assert!(bound.diagnostics.iter().any(|d| d.code == "E_QUARRY_TYPE"), "{bad}: {:#?}", bound.diagnostics);
+    }
+}

   143	    /// Streams the ids of the live rows referencing `id` through `r` to
   144	    /// `visit`, through its index, until `visit` answers false. A capped walk
   145	    /// (cascade, set null) reads `PAGE` rows per seek and holds at most the
   146	    /// reference's cap; a restrict probe reads one row per seek, so it examines
   147	    /// nothing past its witness. Images are dropped before `visit` runs. Seeks
   148	    /// start at the live suffix, so an expired backlog is never visited.
   149	    fn each_child(&mut self, r: &Referencing<'_>, id: &Value, capped: bool, visit: &mut dyn FnMut(&mut Self, Value) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   150	        let schema = self.schema;
   151	        let index = schema.reference_index(r.child, r.column).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("{}.{} has no reference index", r.child, r.column)))?.to_owned();

   156	            vec![(vec![id.clone(), Value::Null], None), (vec![id.clone()], Some(Value::Int(now)))]
   157	        } else {
   158	            vec![(vec![id.clone()], None)]
   159	        };
   160	        let mut live = 0_u64;
   161	        for (prefix, gt) in ranges {
   162	            let mut bounds = Bounds { gt, ..Default::default() };
   163	            loop {
   164	                let page = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.scan(allowance, r.child, &index, &prefix, &bounds, Dir::Asc, page_rows))?;
   165	                let more = page.len() == page_rows;
   166	                if let Some((_, key)) = page.last() { bounds.after = crate::key::decode(key).map(|v| v.into_iter().skip(prefix.len()).collect()); }
   167	                let mut ids = Vec::with_capacity(page.len());

   169	                    if self.device {
   170	                        // @ref LLP 3000.039#6.4 — a device predicts only over current rows: retained history queues the delete, and only a live, current (or own provisional) row is a witness.
   171	                        // A retained, no longer current row is work the reservation does not
   172	                        // price and a witness the device cannot judge: the delete queues.
   173	                        if self.tx.retained_row(r.child, &row)? && !self.tx.current_row(r.child, &row)? {
   174	                            return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction(format!("deleting meets retained {} history that references it; queued without a local delete", r.child)));

   182	                    // is a store that broke its own invariant, never a hidden-row count.
   183	                    if live > cap { return Err(RuntimeError::Schema(format!("{}.{} holds more rows than its cap for one {} row", r.child, r.column, r.column))); }

   188	                }

   191	        }

   193	    }

   195	    /// A device predicts only over a referencing group it holds completely.
   196	    // @ref LLP 3000.039#6.4 — the held-group proof of LLP 3000.007 §20.5, per closure row and reference.
   197	    fn prove_reference_held(&mut self, r: &Referencing<'_>, id: &Value) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {

   201	        // unacquired range is unknown even when the rule admits the viewer).

   206	    /// The engine's own write of a `set null` reference: no rule, every constraint.
   207	    fn clear_reference(&mut self, table: &str, column: &str, old: Value) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   208	        let mut new = old.clone();
   209	        if let Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) = &mut new { fields.insert(column.to_owned(), Value::Null); }
   210	        let patch = crate::value::object([(column, Value::Null)]);
   211	        let outer = std::mem::replace(&mut self.engine_action, true);
   212	        let result = self.target_attempt(table, |runner| {
   213	            runner.reserve_maintains(table, &runner.schema.tables[table])?;
   214	            runner.replace_authorized(table, old, new, true, &patch, 0)
   215	        });
   216	        self.engine_action = outer;
   217	        result
   218	    }
   219	
   220	    /// The engine's own delete of a closure row: no rule, its constraints, its
   221	    /// `read through` children's probe, maintains and partition events.
   222	    fn delete_reached(&mut self, table_name: &str, old: Value) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   223	        self.target_attempt(table_name, |runner| {
   224	            runner.refuse_engine_owned(table_name, Effect::Delete)?;
   225	            let table = &runner.schema.tables[table_name];
   226	            runner.reserve_maintains(table_name, table)?;
   227	            runner.delete_row(table_name, old)
   228	        })
   229	    }
   230	}

   232	/// Rows a child scan holds per seek: the reservation's transient `4 × row`
   233	/// (LLP 3000.039 §5.1, `Schema::delete_reservation`).
   234	const PAGE: usize = crate::schema::references::REFERENCE_PAGE;

   236	fn through_reference(r: &Referencing<'_>) -> bool {
   237	    r.table.through.as_ref().is_some_and(|t| t.reference == r.column)
   238	}
   239	
   240	/// The closure's rows, children before parents: a table goes first when no
   241	/// other reached table must be removed before it (the cascade and `read
   242	/// through` edges are acyclic by `check`), and within a table, later
   243	/// discoveries first.
   244	fn deletion_order(schema: &crate::schema::Schema, reached: &[(String, String)]) -> Vec<(String, String)> {
   245	    let tables: Vec<&str> = {
   246	        let mut seen = Vec::new();
   247	        for (table, _) in reached { if !seen.contains(&table.as_str()) { seen.push(table.as_str()); } }
   248	        seen
   249	    };
   250	    // edges: child table -> the reached tables it must be removed before
   251	    // (its cascade parents and its `read through` parent; LLP 3000.039 §3).
   252	    let mut edges: Vec<(&str, &str)> = Vec::new();
   253	    for &child in &tables {
   254	        for &parent in &tables {
   255	            if child != parent && schema.deletion_precedes(child, parent) { edges.push((child, parent)); }
   256	        }
   257	    }
   258	    let mut order: Vec<&str> = Vec::new();
   259	    let mut remaining = tables.clone();
   260	    while !remaining.is_empty() {
   261	        // A table no remaining table references can go now (its referencers are gone).
   262	        let position = remaining.iter().position(|t| !remaining.iter().any(|other| other != t && edges.contains(&(*other, *t))))
   263	            .unwrap_or(remaining.len() - 1);
   264	        order.push(remaining.remove(position));
   265	    }
   266	    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(reached.len());
   267	    for table in order {
   268	        out.extend(reached.iter().rev().filter(|(t, _)| t == table).cloned());
   269	    }
   270	    out
   271	}

   228	pub(super) fn capture_matches(through: &Through, expected: &Value, row: &Value) -> bool {
   229	    through.fields.keys().map(String::as_str).chain([PARENT_DEADLINE])
   230	        .all(|field| row.field(field).ok() == expected.field(field).ok())
   231	}

   233	pub(super) fn stamp(
   234	    parent: &Table,
   235	    through: &Through,
   236	    image: &Value,
   237	    row: &mut Value,
   238	) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   239	    let image = crate::schema::row_image(image, parent);
   240	    if let Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) = row {
   241	        for (capture, source) in &through.fields {
   242	            fields.insert(capture.clone(), image.field(source)?.clone());
   243	        }
   244	        fields.insert(
   245	            PARENT_DEADLINE.into(),
   246	            parent
   247	                .deadline(&image)
   248	                .map(Value::Int)
   249	                .unwrap_or(Value::Null),
   250	        );
   251	    }
   252	    Ok(())

   139	pub trait Presence: std::fmt::Debug + Send + Sync {
   140	    /// How many connections `principal` holds open now.
   141	    fn connections(&self, principal: &str) -> u64;
   142	    /// A single observation: (live connections, grace deadline in engine time).
   143	    fn effect_presence(&self, principal: &str) -> (u64, Option<i64>) { (self.connections(principal), None) }

   145	    fn effect_presence_at(&self, principal: &str, now: i64) -> (u64, Option<i64>) {
   146	        let (live, deadline) = self.effect_presence(principal);

   148	        )
   149	    }

    13	/// Rotate a sweep's table order after the last table that consumed a bounded
    14	/// visit. Per-table row cursors alone can starve every later table when an
    15	/// earlier table contains a permanently restricted due row.
    16	pub(crate) fn resume_expiry_tables(
    17	    mut tables: Vec<String>,
    18	    cursors: &BTreeMap<String, Vec<Value>>,
    19	) -> Vec<String> {
    20	    let after = cursors
    21	        .get(EXPIRY_TABLE_CURSOR)
    22	        .and_then(|cursor| cursor.first())
    23	        .and_then(|value| value.as_str().ok());
    24	    if let Some(index) = after.and_then(|after| tables.iter().position(|table| table == after)) {
    25	        let next = (index + 1) % tables.len().max(1);
    26	        tables.rotate_left(next);
    27	    }
    28	    tables
    29	}

    35	/// Only inherited batches need staging. Preserve the streaming path for
    36	/// existing schemas, including large fixture imports.
    37	pub(crate) fn ancestor_order<'a, I>(
    38	    schema: &Schema,
    39	    rows: I,
    40	) -> Box<dyn Iterator<Item = (String, Value)> + 'a>
    41	where
    42	    I: IntoIterator<Item = (String, Value)>,
    43	    I::IntoIter: 'a,
    44	{
    45	    if schema.tables.values().all(|t| t.through.is_none()) {
    46	        return Box::new(rows.into_iter());
    47	    }
    48	    let order = schema.through_order();
    49	    let mut rows: Vec<_> = rows.into_iter().collect();
    50	    rows.sort_by_key(|(name, _)| order.iter().position(|n| n == name).unwrap_or(usize::MAX));
    51	    Box::new(rows.into_iter())
    52	}

    64	fn sample(samples: &mut Vec<String>, row: &Value, reference: &str, parent: &str) {
    65	    fn bounded(text: &str) -> &str {
    66	        let mut end = text.len().min(256);
    67	        while !text.is_char_boundary(end) {
    68	            end -= 1;
    69	        }
    70	        &text[..end]
    71	    }
    72	    if samples.len() < 5 {
    73	        let id = row
    74	            .field("id")
    75	            .ok()
    76	            .and_then(|v| v.as_str().ok())
    77	            .unwrap_or("<missing>");
    78	        let value = row
    79	            .field(reference)
    80	            .ok()
    81	            .and_then(|v| v.as_str().ok())
    82	            .unwrap_or("<missing>");
    83	        samples.push(format!(
    84	            "{}: {reference} -> {parent}[{}]",
    85	            bounded(id),
    86	            bounded(value)
    87	        ));
    88	    }
    89	}

    91	fn rows(
    92	    tx: &dyn Rows,
    93	    name: &str,
    94	    mut visit: impl FnMut(Value) -> Result<(), RuntimeError>,
    95	) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    96	    let mut bounds = Bounds::default();
    97	    loop {
    98	        let page = tx.scan(name, "byId", &[], &bounds, Dir::Asc, 256)?;
    99	        if page.is_empty() {
   100	            return Ok(());
   101	        }
   102	        for (row, key) in page {
   103	            bounds.after = crate::key::decode(&key);
   104	            visit(row)?;
   105	        }
   106	    }
   107	}

   109	fn correspondence(
   110	    child: &RuleExpr,
   111	    parent: &RuleExpr,
   112	) -> Option<std::collections::BTreeMap<String, String>> {
   113	    if child.is_uniformly_readable() && parent.is_uniformly_readable() {
   114	        return Some(Default::default());
   115	    }
   116	    fn walk(
   117	        a: &serde_json::Value,
   118	        b: &serde_json::Value,
   119	        map: &mut std::collections::BTreeMap<String, String>,
   120	    ) -> bool {
   121	        use serde_json::Value::*;
   122	        match (a, b) {
   123	            (Object(a), Object(b)) if a.len() == b.len() => {
   124	                if let (Some(String(a)), Some(String(b))) = (a.get("Field"), b.get("Field")) {
   125	                    if map.get(a).is_some_and(|old| old != b)
   126	                        || map.iter().any(|(old, v)| v == b && old != a)
   127	                    {
   128	                        return false;
   129	                    }
   130	                    map.insert(a.clone(), b.clone());
   131	                    true
   132	                } else {
   133	                    a.iter()
   134	                        .all(|(k, a)| b.get(k).is_some_and(|b| walk(a, b, map)))
   135	                }
   136	            }
   137	            (Array(a), Array(b)) if a.len() == b.len() => {
   138	                a.iter().zip(b).all(|(a, b)| walk(a, b, map))
   139	            }
   140	            _ => a == b,
   141	        }
   142	    }
   143	    let mut map = Default::default();
   144	    walk(
   145	        &serde_json::to_value(child).ok()?,
   146	        &serde_json::to_value(parent).ok()?,
   147	        &mut map,
   148	    )
   149	    .then_some(map)
   150	}

   152	/// The retirement phase shared by activation and its read-only occupancy
   153	/// preview. Selection and the predecessor deadline predicate live here once;
   154	/// checking a candidate must not count a row this phase would remove.
   155	pub(crate) struct Retirement<'a> {
   156	    affected: Vec<(String, &'a Table)>,
   157	    now: i64,
   158	}
   159	
   160	impl<'a> Retirement<'a> {
   161	    pub(crate) fn new(next: &Schema, previous: &'a Schema, now: i64) -> Self {
   162	        let affected = next
   163	            .through_order()
   164	            .into_iter()
   165	            .filter_map(|name| {
   166	                let next = &next.tables[&name];
   167	                let old = previous.table(&name)?;
   168	                Self::changes_lifetime(next,old).then_some((name, old))
   169	            })
   170	            .collect();
   171	        Self { affected, now }
   172	    }
   173	
   174	    fn changes_lifetime(next:&Table,old:&Table) -> bool {
   175	        next.through != old.through || next.through.is_some() && (next.expire != old.expire || next.expire.as_ref().is_some_and(|field|old.defaults.get(field)!=next.defaults.get(field)))
   176	    }
   177	
   178	    pub(crate) fn retires_image(next:&Table,old:&Table,row:&Value,now:i64) -> bool {
   179	        (next.through!=old.through || next.expire!=old.expire || old.expire.as_ref().is_some_and(|field|old.defaults.get(field)!=next.defaults.get(field))) && old.expired(row,now)
   180	    }
   181	
   182	    pub(crate) fn affects(&self, name: &str) -> bool {
   183	        self.affected.iter().any(|(table, _)| table == name)
   184	    }
   185	
   186	    pub(crate) fn retires(&self, name: &str, row: &Value) -> bool {
   187	        self.affected
   188	            .iter()
   189	            .find(|(table, _)| table == name)
   190	            .is_some_and(|(_, old)| old.expired(row, self.now))
   191	    }
   192	}

   348	                .field(&t.reference)
   349	                .ok()
   350	                .and_then(|v| v.as_str().ok())
   351	                .map(|id| tx.get(&t.parent, id))
   352	                .transpose()?
   353	                .flatten();
   354	            let matches = found.as_ref().is_some_and(|p| {
   355	                (!parent.expired(p, now) || table.expired(&row, now)) && {
   356	                    let p = crate::schema::row_image(p, parent);
   357	                    t.fields
   358	                        .iter()
   359	                        .all(|(field, source)| row.field(field).ok() == p.field(source).ok())
   360	                        && row.field(PARENT_DEADLINE).ok()
   361	                            == Some(&parent.deadline(&p).map(Value::Int).unwrap_or(Value::Null))
   362	                }
   363	            });
   364	            if !matches {
   365	                invalid += 1;
   366	                sample(&mut samples, &row, &t.reference, &t.parent);
   367	            }
   368	            Ok(())
   369	        })?;
   370	        if invalid > 0 {
   371	            return Err(refusal(
   372	                &name,
   373	                invalid,
   374	                "restored captures do not match a live parent",
   375	                &samples,
   376	            ));
   377	        }
   378	    }
   379	    Ok(())
   380	}
   381	
   382	pub fn validate_indexes(tx: &dyn Rows, schema: &Schema) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   383	    for (name, table) in &schema.tables {
   384	        let mut checks: Vec<_> = table
   385	            .indexes
   386	            .iter()
   387	            .filter(|(_, i)| i.unique)
   388	            .map(|(name, i)| (name, i.components.len(), 1, true))
   389	            .collect();
   390	        for constraint in &table.constraints {
   391	            if let crate::schema::Constraint::Cap { by, max } = constraint {
   392	                let (index, _) = table
   393	                    .indexes
   394	                    .iter()
   395	                    .find(|(_, i)| i.columns().starts_with(by))
   396	                    .ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("{name} cap has no index")))?;
   397	                checks.push((index, by.len(), u64::from(*max), false));
   398	            }
   399	        }
   400	        for (index, width, max, nulls_distinct) in checks {
   401	            let mut bounds = Bounds::default();
   402	            let mut previous = None;
   403	            let mut count = 0;
   404	            loop {
   405	                let page = tx.scan(name, index, &[], &bounds, Dir::Asc, 256)?;
   406	                if page.is_empty() {
   407	                    break;
   408	                }
   409	                for (_, key) in page {
   410	                    let full = crate::key::decode(&key)
   411	                        .ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Store("invalid activation index".into()))?;
   412	                    let group = full[..width].to_vec();
   413	                    bounds.after = Some(full);
   414	                    if nulls_distinct && group.contains(&Value::Null) {
   415	                        continue;
   416	                    }
   417	                    if previous.as_ref() == Some(&group) {
   418	                        count += 1;
   419	                    } else {
   420	                        previous = Some(group);
   421	                        count = 1;
   422	                    }
   423	                    if count > max {
   424	                        return Err(RuntimeError::Constraint(format!(
   425	                            "cannot activate {name}.{index}: existing group exceeds {max}"
   426	                        )));
   427	                    }
   428	                }
   429	            }
   430	        }
   431	    }
   432	    Ok(())
   433	}

   435	impl super::runner::Runner<'_> {
   436	    /// Authoritative adapters feed an ancestor-ordered batch to the ordinary
   437	    /// insert/update path; captures always resolve inside this transaction.
   438	    pub fn seed_server_rows(
   439	        &mut self,
   440	        rows: impl IntoIterator<Item = (String, Value)>,
   441	    ) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
   442	        if !self.context.is_system() || self.device {
   443	            return Err(RuntimeError::Input(
   444	                "server seed requires system authority".into(),
   445	            ));
   446	        }
   447	        let order = self.schema.through_order();
   448	        let mut rows: Vec<_> = rows.into_iter().collect();
   449	        rows.sort_by_key(|(n, _)| order.iter().position(|x| x == n));
   450	        let count = rows.len() as u64;
   451	        for (name, row) in rows {
   452	            super::timeline::check_import(self.schema, &name)?;
   453	            // Adoption rewrites are system imports of stored images (LLP 3000.015 §1).
   454	            self.upsert(
   455	                &name,
   456	                &row.field("id")?.clone(),
   457	                row.import_input(&super::ImportInput(())),
   458	            )?;
   459	        }
   460	        self.check_final_exists()?;
   461	        Ok(count)
   462	    }
   463	
   464	    /// A bounded child-first sweep on the common Rows interface.
   465	    pub fn sweep_server_rows(&mut self, limit: usize, expiry_after: &mut BTreeMap<String, Vec<Value>>) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
   466	        if !self.context.is_system() || self.device {
   467	            return Err(RuntimeError::Input(
   468	                "server sweep requires system authority".into(),
   469	            ));
   470	        }
   471	        let now = self
   472	            .context
   473	            .now
   474	            .ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Input("sweep clock is not pinned".into()))?;
   475	        let mut count = 0;
   476	        let mut visited = 0;
   477	        let tables = resume_expiry_tables(self.schema.through_order().into_iter().rev().collect(), expiry_after);
   478	        for name in tables {
   479	            let Some((index, _)) = self.schema.tables[&name].expiry_index() else {
   480	                continue;
   481	            };
   482	            let due = Bounds { gte: Some(Value::Int(i64::MIN)), lte: Some(Value::Int(now)), ..Default::default() };
   483	            let mut bounds = due.clone();
   484	            bounds.after = expiry_after.get(&name).cloned();
   485	            let mut wrapped = bounds.after.is_none();
   486	            while visited < limit {
   487	                let batch = (limit - visited).min(256);
   488	                let page = self.metered_scan(|runner, scope| {
   489	                    runner
   490	                        .tx
   491	                        .scan(scope, &name, index, &[], &bounds, Dir::Asc, batch)
   492	                })?;
   493	                if page.is_empty() {
   494	                    expiry_after.remove(&name);
   495	                    if !wrapped && visited < limit {
   496	                        bounds = due.clone();
   497	                        wrapped = true;
   498	                        continue;
   499	                    }
   500	                    break;
   501	                }
   502	                let page_len = page.len();
   503	                for (row, key) in page {
   504	                    bounds.after = crate::key::decode(&key);
   505	                    if let Some(after) = &bounds.after { expiry_after.insert(name.clone(), after.clone()); }
   506	                    visited += 1;
   507	                    mark_expiry_table(expiry_after, &name);
   508	                    match self.retire_expired_row(&name, &row) {
   509	                        Ok(true) => count += 1,
   510	                        Ok(false) => {},
   511	                        Err(RuntimeError::Structural { code: "E_REFERENCED" | "E_PARENT_HAS_CHILDREN", .. }) => {},
   512	                        Err(error) => return Err(error),
   513	                    }
   514	                }
   515	                if page_len < batch {
   516	                    expiry_after.remove(&name);
   517	                    if !wrapped && visited < limit {
   518	                        bounds = due.clone();
   519	                        wrapped = true;
   520	                        continue;
   521	                    }
   522	                    break;
   523	                }
   524	            }
   525	        }
   526	        Ok(count)
   527	    }
   528	}

   265	        self.refuse_receipt_fields(table_name, &patch, false)?;
   266	        self.refuse_recorded(table_name, &patch)?;
   267	        super::sequences::refuse_fields(&self.schema.tables[table_name], table_name, &patch)?;
   268	        if patch.as_object()?.contains_key("id") {
   269	            return Err(RuntimeError::Input(format!("{table_name} update patch cannot change id")));
   270	        }
   271	        let id = key.as_str()?;
   272	        self.reserve_target_resolution(table_name, self.schema.table(table_name).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("missing table {table_name}")))?, &patch, false)?;
   273	        let Some(old) = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| {
   274	            runner.fetch_write_target(allowance, table_name, id)
   275	        })? else {
   276	            return Err(self.write_miss(table_name, "byId", &[key.clone()]));
   277	        };
   278	        if self.device && self.schema.tables[table_name].sync.is_none() { return Err(self.write_miss(table_name, "byId", &[key.clone()])); }
   279	        let readable = !self.inactive_write_target(table_name, &old)?
   280	            && self.check_rule(table_name, Effect::Read, None, &old)?;
   281	        let patch = self.ignore_hidden_immutable_patch(table_name, patch, readable)?;
   282	        let (new, copy) = self.merge_patch(table_name, &old, &patch, readable)?;
   283	        self.replace(table_name, old, new, readable, &patch, copy)
   284	    }
   285	
   286	    pub(super) fn upsert(&mut self, table_name: &str, key: &Value, row: Supplied) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   287	        if self.device && self.schema.tables[table_name].not_before.is_some() {
   288	            return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction(
   289	                "a mutation touching a `not before` table runs on the server".into(),
   290	            ));
   291	        }
   292	        self.target_attempt(table_name, |runner| {
   293	            runner.upsert_attempt(table_name, key, row)
   294	        })
   295	    }
   296	
   297	    fn upsert_attempt(&mut self, table_name: &str, key: &Value, row: Supplied) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   298	        self.refuse_upsert_owned(table_name)?;
   299	        self.refuse_receipt_fields(table_name, &row, false)?;
   300	        self.refuse_recorded(table_name, &row)?;
   301	        super::sequences::refuse_fields(&self.schema.tables[table_name], table_name, &row)?;
   302	        let id = key.as_str()?;
   303	        if row.field("id")?.as_str()? != id {
   304	            return Err(RuntimeError::Input(format!("{table_name} upsert row id must equal its key")));
   305	        }
   306	        self.reserve_target_resolution(table_name, self.schema.table(table_name).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("missing table {table_name}")))?, &row, true)?;
   307	        match self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| {
   308	            runner.fetch_write_target(allowance, table_name, id)
   309	        })? {
   310	            Some(old) => {
   311	                let readable = !self.inactive_write_target(table_name, &old)?
   312	                    && self.check_rule(table_name, Effect::Read, None, &old)?;
   313	                let row = self.ignore_hidden_immutable_patch(table_name, row, readable)?;
   314	                // @ref LLP 3000.007#5.4 — an existing row receives a patch; omitted columns keep their values.
   315	                let (new, copy) = self.merge_patch(table_name, &old, &row, readable)?;
   316	                self.replace(table_name, old, new, readable, &row, copy)
   317	            }
   318	            None if self.device && !self.upsert_absence_proven(table_name, "byId", &[key.clone()])? =>
   319	            {
   320	                Err(self.write_miss(table_name, "byId", &[key.clone()]))
   321	            }
   322	            None => self.insert_upsert(table_name, "byId", row),
   323	        }
   324	    }
   325	
   326	    pub(super) fn insert_upsert(&mut self, table_name: &str, addressed_index: &str, row: Supplied) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   327	        self.refuse_upsert_owned(table_name)?;
   328	        // @ref LLP 3000.036.002#5 — trusted fixture imports preserve the constraint layer.
   329	        if self.context.is_system() {
   330	            return self.insert_attempt(table_name, row, false, Some(addressed_index)).map(|_| ()).map_err(|error| match error {
   331	                RuntimeError::Input(message) => RuntimeError::Constraint(message),
   332	                other => other,
   333	            });
   334	        }
   335	        if self.schema.tables[table_name].through.is_some() {
   336	            // A read-through child's insert arm keeps the hidden-target word for every authority refusal.
   337	            return self.insert_attempt(table_name, row, false, Some(addressed_index)).map(|_| ()).map_err(|e| match e {
   338	                RuntimeError::Rule {..} | RuntimeError::Input(_) => self.no_write_target(), other => other,
   339	            });
   340	        }
   341	        match self.insert_attempt(table_name, row, false, Some(addressed_index)).map(|_| ()) {
   342	            Err(RuntimeError::Input(_)) => Err(self.no_write_target()),
   343	            result => result,
   344	        }
   345	    }
   346	
   347	    fn replace(&mut self, table_name: &str, old: Value, new: Value, readable: bool, patch: &Value, copy: u64) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   348	        self.authorize_update_fields(table_name, &old, &new, patch, readable)?;
   349	        self.replace_authorized(table_name, old, new, readable, patch, copy)
   350	    }
   351	
   352	    /// `copy` is the merged image's lawful price, charged again for an engine slot copy.
   353	    pub(super) fn replace_authorized(&mut self, table_name: &str, old: Value, new: Value, readable: bool, patch: &Value, copy: u64) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   354	        self.refuse_engine_owned(table_name, Effect::Update)?;
   355	        self.refuse_receipt_fields(table_name, patch, false)?;
   356	        self.refuse_recorded(table_name, patch)?;
   357	        super::sequences::refuse_fields(&self.schema.tables[table_name], table_name, patch)?;
   358	        self.authorize_fields(table_name, &old, patch)?;
   359	        let definition = &self.schema.tables[table_name];
   360	        for path in definition.columns.keys().filter(|field| {
   361	            definition.engine_field(field) && field.as_str() != crate::schema::through::DEADLINE
   362	        }) {
   363	            if old.field(path).ok() != new.field(path).ok() {
   364	                return Err(if readable { RuntimeError::Structural { code: "E_RECORDED_FIELD", message: format!("engine replacement changed stored attribution at {table_name}.{path} (guide maintains)") } } else { self.no_write_target() });
   365	            }
   366	        }
   367	        let mut new = new;
   368	        self.schema.tables[table_name].recompute_deadline(&mut new)?;
   369	        // @ref LLP 3000.017#2.2 — extending life re-admits the new image.
   370	        if self.schema.tables[table_name].stamp_ephemeral(&mut new, self.context.now.unwrap_or(0))?
   371	            && !self.check_rule(table_name, Effect::Insert, None, &new)? {
   372	            return Err(if readable { RuntimeError::Rule { table: table_name.into(), effect: Effect::Update } } else { self.no_write_target() });
   373	        }
   374	        let new = self.with_asset_facts(table_name, new, Some(&old), (!readable).then_some(patch))?;
   375	        if let Err(error) = super::validate::validate_projection(self.schema, table_name, &new, self.device.then_some(self.context.viewer.as_str())) { return Err(if readable { error } else { self.no_write_target() }); }
   376	        self.check_constraints(table_name, Some(&old), &new, Effect::Update)?;
   377	        let new = self.prepare_event_slots(table_name, Some(&old), new, copy)?;
   378	        // A predicting device keeps another owner's omitted private field as an omission.
   379	        super::validate::validate_projection(self.schema, table_name, &new, self.device.then_some(self.context.viewer.as_str()))?;
   380	        let table = self.schema.table(table_name).expect("validated");
   381	        let entries = self.maintain_scratch(self.contribution_heap(table), |runner| {
   382	            runner.tx.put(table_name, table, &new, Some(&old))
   383	        })?;
   384	        self.charge_source_indexes(table, Some(&old), Some(&new), entries)?;
   385	        self.row_changed(table_name, Some(&old), Some(&new), Origin::Source)
   386	    }
   387	
   388	    pub(super) fn delete(&mut self, table_name: &str, id: &str) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   389	        if self.device && self.schema.tables[table_name].not_before.is_some() {
   390	            return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction(
   391	                "a mutation touching a `not before` table runs on the server".into(),
   392	            ));
   393	        }
   394	        self.target_attempt(table_name, |runner| runner.delete_attempt(table_name, id))
   395	    }
   396	
   397	    fn delete_attempt(&mut self, table_name: &str, id: &str) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   398	        self.refuse_engine_owned(table_name, Effect::Delete)?;
   399	        self.refuse_receipt_scope_delete(table_name)?;
   400	        let table = self.schema.table(table_name).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("missing table {table_name}")))?;
   401	        self.reserve_write_rules(table, &[Effect::Read, Effect::Delete])?;
   402	        // @ref LLP 3000.007#20.9 — delete prepays hidden contribution work before fetching its old image, with the same attempt lifetime as update.
   403	        self.reserve_maintains(table_name, table)?;
   404	        let Some(old) = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| {
   405	            runner.fetch_write_target(allowance, table_name, id)
   406	        })? else {
   407	            return Err(RuntimeError::Require { site: Some(self.statement_site.clone()), code: "NOT_FOUND".to_owned(), message: None });
   408	        };
   409	        // @ref LLP 3000.039#3 — a delete that consults referencing rows needs read authority on its row first.
   410	        let readable =
   411	            !self.inactive_write_target(table_name, &old)? && self.check_rule(table_name, Effect::Read, None, &old)?;
   412	        if (self.schema.children(table_name).next().is_some() || self.schema.is_referenced(table_name)) && !readable
   413	        {
   414	            self.refusing_clause(table_name, "read rule");
   415	            return Err(self.no_write_target());
   416	        }
   417	        if !self.check_rule(table_name, Effect::Delete, None, &old)? {
   418	            return Err(if readable {
   419	                RuntimeError::Rule { table: table_name.to_owned(), effect: Effect::Delete }
   420	            } else { self.no_write_target() });
   421	        }
   422	        self.delete_authorized(table_name, old)
   423	    }
   424	
   425	    pub(super) fn delete_authorized(&mut self, table_name: &str, old: Value) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   426	        let old = if self.schema.is_referenced(table_name) {
   427	            self.apply_reference_actions(table_name, &old)?;
   428	            // @ref LLP 3000.039#3 — the actions may have changed the root (a maintained column mirrored from its children): remove its current image.
   429	            let id = old.field("id")?.as_str()?.to_owned();
   430	            self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.get(allowance, table_name, &id))?.unwrap_or(old)
   431	        } else { old };
   432	        self.delete_row(table_name, old)
   433	    }
   434	
   435	    /// A delete's own removal of one row, its rules already decided: receipt
   436	    /// membership, the read-through child probe, constraints, maintains and
   437	    /// the partition event. A referential cascade removes each row this way.
   438	    pub(super) fn delete_row(&mut self, table_name: &str, old: Value) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   439	        let table = &self.schema.tables[table_name];
   440	        self.receipt_member_removed(table_name, &old)?;
   441	        self.refuse_live_children(table_name,old.field("id")?)?;
   442	        self.check_constraints(table_name, Some(&old), &old, Effect::Delete)?;
   443	        let entries = self.maintain_scratch(self.contribution_heap(table), |runner| {
   444	            runner.tx.delete(table_name, table, &old)
   445	        })?;
   446	        self.charge_source_indexes(table, Some(&old), None, entries)?;
   447	        self.row_changed(table_name, Some(&old), None, Origin::Source)
   448	    }
   449	
   450	    /// Remove a row the engine itself retires (an expired one): no rule and
   451	    /// no constraint stands between the engine and its own sweep, while
   452	    /// aggregates and partition events apply as for any delete.
   453	    pub(super) fn remove(&mut self, table_name: &str, old: &Value) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   454	        self.refuse_engine_owned(table_name, Effect::Delete)?;
   455	        let table = self.schema.table(table_name).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("missing table {table_name}")))?;
   456	        let entries = self.maintain_scratch(self.contribution_heap(table), |runner| {
   457	            runner.tx.delete(table_name, table, old)
   458	        })?;
   459	        self.charge_source_indexes(table, Some(old), None, entries)?;
   460	        self.row_changed(table_name, Some(old), None, Origin::Source)
   461	    }
   462	
   463	    /// Physically retire one row whose upper lifetime ended. Expiry bypasses
   464	    /// the root's authored delete rule and constraints, but it does not bypass
   465	    /// the schema's declared effects on rows that reference the root. A
   466	    /// read-through child still retains the expired parent physically.
   467	    // @ref LLP 3000.039#3 — expiry cleanup runs the same closure/restrict/set-null actions as an authored delete.
   468	    pub(super) fn retire_expired_row(&mut self, table_name: &str, old: &Value) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
   469	        if self.physical_children(table_name, old.field("id")?)? { return Ok(false); }
   470	        let current = if self.schema.is_referenced(table_name) {
   471	            self.apply_reference_actions(table_name, old)?;
   472	            // A cascade may maintain a column on the root; delete its current
   473	            // physical image so index and cap entries match what is stored.
   474	            let id = old.field("id")?.as_str()?;
   475	            self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.get(allowance, table_name, id))?
   476	                .unwrap_or_else(|| old.clone())
   477	        } else {
   478	            old.clone()
   479	        };
   480	        self.remove(table_name, &current)?;
   481	        Ok(true)
   482	    }
   483	
   484	    /// At a program commit's end, retire every source row the commit changed
   485	    /// or inserted whose lifetime has already ended: its final
   486	    /// image was never live at a commit boundary, so it leaves no row for a
   487	    /// later sweep to announce. Inside the commit the
   488	    /// row existed as written (an insert-then-update still works). Engine
   489	    /// bookkeeping, unmetered: the device's prediction does not do it, and
   490	    /// the program's metering is already recorded. Its work, returned, stays
   491	    /// linear in the rows retired: each aggregate row takes one net change
   492	    /// and each audience key is scanned for a live row once. Seeds and loads
   493	    /// ordinarily keep their rows for the sweep; row-keyed view sources use
   494	    /// `retire_seeded_view_sources` to preserve their count-basis contract.
   495	    // @ref LLP 3000#7-decisions-during-execution — a row whose lifetime ended by its own commit's end never exists at a commit boundary.
   496	    #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
   497	    pub(crate) fn retire_expired_births(&mut self) -> Result<crate::meter::Metered, RuntimeError> {
   498	        let Some(now) = self.context.now else { return Ok(Default::default());
   499	        };
   500	        // @ref LLP 3000.036.000.000#3 — an expired final image never grants a new recipient the row's id.
   501	        // The tracker covers synced and unsynced source tables alike. Each
   502	        // distinct entry prepaid its tree node, strings and this vector slot;
   503	        // the rows-written ceiling bounds the commit-end walk.
   504	        // A row that existed before the commit and ends it already expired is
   505	        // retired too: accounted from the partitions it was in at the commit's
   506	        // start, it revokes there and announces nothing to a partition it only
   507	        // entered with its expiring image.
   508	        let mut changed: Vec<(String, String)> = std::mem::take(&mut self.expiry_rows).into_iter().collect();
   509	        if changed.is_empty() {
   510	            return Ok(Default::default());
   511	        }
   512	        // The log's order must not depend on a map's iteration order.
   513	        let order = self.schema.through_order();
   514	        changed.sort_by_key(|(name,id)| {
   515	            (std::cmp::Reverse(order.iter().position(|n| n == name)),id.clone(),
   516	            )
   517	        });
   518	        let meter = std::mem::replace(&mut self.meter, crate::meter::Meter::new(crate::meter::Ceilings::unbounded(), crate::meter::Cut::Abort));
   519	        self.retiring = Some(Default::default());
   520	        let retired = changed.iter().try_for_each(|(table_name, id)| {
   521	            let Some(row) = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.get(allowance, table_name, id))? else { return Ok(());
   522	            };
   523	            let table = self.schema.table(table_name).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("missing table {table_name}")))?;
   524	            if table.expired(&row, now) { self.retire_expired_row(table_name, &row).map(|_| ()) } else { Ok(()) }
   525	        });
   526	        let aggregates = self.retiring.take().map(|retiring| retiring.aggregates).unwrap_or_default();
   527	        let retired = retired.and_then(|()| self.apply_retired_aggregates(aggregates));
   528	        let work = std::mem::replace(&mut self.meter, meter).used;
   529	        retired.map(|()| work)
   530	    }
   531	
   532	    /// Seed writes historically retire only already-expired sources of
   533	    /// row-keyed views. Keep that narrow boundary while routing their removal
   534	    /// through the common action and net-maintenance path.
   535	    // @ref LLP 3000.039#6.5 — ordinary expired fixtures remain stored; derived row-view sources cannot revive after clock rollback.
   536	    #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
   537	    pub(crate) fn retire_seeded_view_sources(&mut self) -> Result<crate::meter::Metered, RuntimeError> {
   538	        let schema = self.schema;
   539	        self.expiry_rows.retain(|(table, _)| schema.maintains.iter()
   540	            .any(|maintain| maintain.source == table.as_str() && maintain.row_key.is_some()));
   541	        self.retire_expired_births()
   542	    }
   543	
   544	    /// A column with a declared default takes it when the written row leaves
   545	    /// it out, before validation and before the asset facts, so the row the
   546	    /// rules and the constraints see is the complete one.
   547	    // @ref LLP 3000.007#5.4 — omitted defaults use the clock and viewer of the host running the insert.
   548	    pub(super) fn with_defaults(&mut self, table_name: &str, row: Supplied) -> Result<Supplied, RuntimeError> {
   549	        let table = self.schema.table(table_name).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("missing table {table_name}")))?;
   550	        if !table.defaults.keys().any(|name| {
   551	            row.as_object().is_ok_and(|fields| !fields.contains_key(name))
   552	        }) {
   553	            return Ok(row);
   554	        }
   555	        let row = row.defaults(table,self.context.now.ok_or_else(||RuntimeError::Input("write clock is not pinned".into()))?,&self.context.viewer)?;
   556	        self.meter.heap(row.heap_bytes())?;
   557	        Ok(row)
   558	    }
   559	
   560	    /// An `image`/`video` column names an upload by id; the row carries the
   561	    /// facts the server established about it (type, bytes, dimensions,
   562	    /// duration), never the client's word for them. The upload must be the
   563	    /// writer's own and of the column's kind and size. The system principal
   564	    /// may name an asset that was never uploaded: a fixture's placeholder,
   565	    /// metadata only, never served.
   566	    // Web stores hold received asset facts, never the authoritative upload ledger.
   567	    #[cfg(not(feature = "sqlite"))]
   568	    fn with_asset_facts(&mut self, _table_name: &str, row: Value, _old: Option<&Value>, _hidden_patch: Option<&Value>) -> Result<Value, RuntimeError> {
   569	        Ok(row)
   570	    }
   571	
   572	    pub(super) fn refuse_upsert_owned(&self, table: &str) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   573	        self.refuse_engine_owned(table, Effect::Insert)?;
   574	        self.refuse_engine_owned(table, Effect::Update)
   575	    }
   576	
   577	    /// Programs never write a maintained target; the engine does.
   578	    pub(super) fn refuse_engine_owned(&self, table: &str, effect: Effect) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   579	        // @ref LLP 3000.022#14.3 — pending member changes cannot rewrite settled requirements.
   580	        if self.device && effect != Effect::Insert && self.schema.receipts.iter().any(|f| f.members == table || f.runs == table) {
   581	            return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction("receipt membership changes and progress queue until settlement".into()));
   582	        }
   583	        self.refuse_receipt_table(table)?;
   584	        self.refuse_condition_write()?;
   585	        self.refuse_timeline_write(table, effect)?;
   586	        self.schema.refuse_private(table)?;
   587	        if self.schema.maintain_for(table).is_some() {
   588	            return Err(RuntimeError::Schema(format!("{table} is a maintained aggregate; write its source rows instead")));
   589	        }
   590	        Ok(())
   591	    }
   592	
   593	    fn check_constraints(&mut self, table_name: &str, old: Option<&Value>, new: &Value, effect: Effect) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   594	        let table = self.schema.table(table_name).expect("validated");
   595	        let id = new.field("id")?.as_str()?.to_owned();
   596	        // @ref LLP 3000.039#4.1 — an action's own write consults no rule: probing the child's read rule would draw the shared allowance only where a child exists.
   597	        let readable = match old { Some(old) if effect == Effect::Update && !self.engine_action => {
   598	                !self.inactive_write_target(table_name, old)?
   599	                    && self.check_rule(table_name, Effect::Read, None, old)?
   600	            }
   601	            _ => true };
   602	        if effect != Effect::Delete {
   603	            for (name, index) in table.indexes.iter().filter(|(_, index)| index.unique) {
   604	                // byId can only return this id (already checked on insert).
   605	                // An unchanged admitted unique key cannot acquire a collision.
   606	                if name == "byId" { continue; }
   607	                let key = index_values(index, new);
   608	                if old.is_some_and(|old| index_values(index, old) == key) { continue; }
   609	                if key.iter().any(|value| *value == Value::Null) {
   610	                    continue;
   611	                }
   612	                // @ref LLP 3000.007#20.5 — holding the target does not cover a different unique population.
   613	                if self.device && effect == Effect::Update && !self.device_work(|runner| {
   614	                        runner.upsert_absence_proven(table_name, name, &key)
   615	                    })? {
   616	                    return Err(self.write_miss(table_name, name, &key));
   617	                }
   618	                if let Some(existing) = self.collision_lookup(table_name, name, index, &key, Some(&id), effect)
   619	                    .map_err(|error| {
   620	                        if !readable && matches!(error, RuntimeError::Rule { .. }) { self.no_write_target() } else { error
   621	                        }
   622	                    })?
   623	                    && existing.field("id")?.as_str()? != id
   624	                {
   625	                    self.observe_sequence_columns(table_name, new, &index.columns(), effect == Effect::Insert)?;
   626	                    if effect == Effect::Update && !readable {
   627	                        #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
   628	                        self.refusing_clause(table_name, &format!("unique {}", index.columns().join(", ")));
   629	                        return Err(self.no_write_target());
   630	                    }
   631	                    // @ref LLP 3000.036#13.9 — the dev log names the `unique` line that refused (wave 3 I3).
   632	                    self.refusing_clause(table_name, &format!("unique {}", index.columns().join(", ")));
   633	                    let declared=index.components.iter().map(|part| match part {
   634	                        crate::schema::IndexComponent::Calendar(k) if k.function=="bucket" => format!("bucket({}, {}{})",k.column,k.millis,if k.offset==0 {String::new()} else {format!(", {}",k.offset)}),

   771	    fn collision_lookup(&mut self, table: &str, name: &str, index: &crate::schema::Index, key: &[Value], except: Option<&str>, effect: Effect) -> Result<Option<Value>, RuntimeError> {
   772	        let probes = super::rules::rule_probes(&self.schema.tables[table].rules.read);

   775	                runner.lookup_write_occupant(table, name, index, key)?

   778	            };
   779	            if let Some(row) = &found && Some(row.field("id")?.as_str()?) != except {
   780	                runner.observe_sequence_columns(table, row, &index.columns(), effect == Effect::Insert)?;
   781	                runner.visible_collision(table, row, effect, &format!("unique {}", index.columns().join(", ")))?;
   782	            }

   804	    /// `after insert <- exists t[...]` holds for every row inserted this
   805	    /// transaction; checked once the program has run.
   806	    pub(super) fn check_final_exists(&mut self) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {

   811	                let Constraint::FinalExistsOnInsert { table: target, index, key } = constraint else { continue;
   812	                };
   813	                let refusal = || {
   814	                    RuntimeError::Constraint(format!("inserting into {table_name} requires a matching row in {target} by the end of the mutation"))
   815	                };
   816	                let has_references = key.iter().any(|term| term.reference_source().is_some());
   817	                let key: Vec<Value> = if has_references {
   818	                    // Preserve the structural target probe, but authorize each
   819	                    // live row supplying its key before it can confer authority.
   820	                    let rule = crate::schema::RuleExpr::Exists { table: target.clone(), index: index.clone(), key: key.clone(), equalities: vec![], provenance: crate::ir::KeyProvenance::Shape };
   821	                    for term in key { if let crate::schema::RuleTerm::Field(field) = term { self.provisional_sequence_read |= self.device && table.sequences.contains_key(field); } }

   823	                } else { key
   824	                    .iter()
   825	                    .map(|term| match term {
   826	                        crate::schema::RuleTerm::Field(field) | crate::schema::RuleTerm::NextField(field) => {
   827	                            // This inserted image owns a provisional ordinal even if no expression read it.
   828	                            self.provisional_sequence_read |= self.device && table.sequences.contains_key(field);
   829	                            row.field(field).cloned().unwrap_or(Value::Null)
   830	                        }
   831	                            crate::schema::RuleTerm::Viewer => {
   832	                                Value::Id(self.context.viewer.clone())
   833	                            }
   834	                            crate::schema::RuleTerm::Literal(value) => value.clone(),
   835	                        crate::schema::RuleTerm::OldField(_) | crate::schema::RuleTerm::Reference { .. } | crate::schema::RuleTerm::ReferenceChain { .. } => Value::Null,
   836	                    })
   837	                    .collect() };
   838	                self.read_tables.insert(target.clone());
   839	                self.observe_sequence_selection(target, index, &key)?;

   855	                    let proven = self.device && match self.upsert_absence_proven(target, index, &key) {

   875	    fn contribution_heap(&self, table: &Table) -> u64 {
   876	        table.indexes.values().fold(0, |bytes: u64, index| match index.components.first() {
   877	            Some(crate::schema::IndexComponent::Contribution(maintain)) => bytes.saturating_add(
   878	                super::write_target::row_copy_ceiling(&self.schema.tables[&maintain.target]).saturating_mul(16)),
   879	            _ => bytes,
   880	        })
   881	    }
   882	
   883	    fn charge_source_indexes(&mut self, table: &Table, old: Option<&Value>, new: Option<&Value>, mut entries: u64) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   884	        for index in table.indexes.values() {
   885	            if let Some(crate::schema::IndexComponent::Contribution(maintain)) = index.components.first() {
   886	                self.charge_maintain(MeterKind::Steps, maintain.evaluation_steps() * (u64::from(old.is_some()) + u64::from(new.is_some())))?;
   887	            }
   888	        }
   889	        if self.maintain_prepaid {
   890	            let id = old.or(new).expect("source image").field("id")?.as_str()?;
   891	            for index in table.indexes.values() {
   892	                if matches!(index.components.first(), Some(crate::schema::IndexComponent::Contribution(_))) {
   893	                    let before = old.map(|row| crate::rows::stored_index_keys(table, index, row, id)).unwrap_or_default();
   894	                    let after = new.map(|row| crate::rows::stored_index_keys(table, index, row, id)).unwrap_or_default();
   895	                    let changed = before.iter().filter(|key| !after.contains(key)).count() + after.iter().filter(|key| !before.contains(key)).count();
   896	                    entries = entries.saturating_sub(changed as u64);
   897	                }
   898	            }
   899	        }
   900	        self.meter.charge(MeterKind::IndexEntries, entries)?;
   901	        Ok(())
   902	    }

   904	    /// The shared tail of every physical row change: creation facts, the
   905	    /// write meter, maintained aggregates, and the partition events.
   906	    pub(super) fn row_changed(&mut self, table_name: &str, old: Option<&Value>, new: Option<&Value>, origin: Origin) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   907	        if old.is_some() && new.is_none() { self.timeline_purge_charge(table_name)?; }
   908	        if self.schema.visible(table_name) { self.written_tables.insert(table_name.to_owned()); }
   909	        if origin == Origin::Source {
   910	            for m in self.schema.maintains.iter().filter(|m|m.row_key.as_ref().is_some_and(|k|k.table == table_name)) {
   911	                self.written_tables.insert(m.target.clone());
   912	            }
   913	            for m in self.schema.maintains.iter().filter(|m|m.source == table_name) {
   914	                if let Some(owner) = &m.private { self.written_tables.insert(owner.table.clone()); }
   915	                if m.row_key.is_some() { self.written_tables.insert(m.target.clone()); }
   916	            }
   917	        }
   918	        self.rows_written += 1;
   919	        if origin == Origin::Maintained { self.charge_maintain(MeterKind::RowsWritten, 1)?; }
   920	        else { self.meter.charge(MeterKind::RowsWritten, 1)?; }
   921	        let table = self.schema.table(table_name).expect("validated");
   922	        // Final-exists obligations retain immutable successful-insert images.
   923	        // Current creation facts have separate per-row ownership, so updates
   924	        // and deletes remove only that row's contributions in O(index count).
   925	        let id = old.or(new).expect("a row change has an image").field("id")?.as_str()?;
   926	        let owner = (table_name.to_owned(), id.to_owned());
   927	        if origin == Origin::Source && new.is_some() && table.is_expiring() && !self.expiry_rows.contains(&owner) {
   928	            self.meter.step(1)?;
   929	            self.meter.heap(crate::rows::word_heap::text(table_name)
   930	                + crate::rows::word_heap::text(id)
   931	                + crate::rows::word_heap::insertion::<(String, String), ()>(self.expiry_rows.len())
   932	                + crate::rows::word_heap::slots::<(String, String)>(1))?;
   933	            self.expiry_rows.insert(owner.clone());
   934	        }
   935	        if self.device && new.is_some() { self.provisional_rows.insert(owner.clone()); }
   936	        let previous = self.created_rows.remove(&owner);
   937	        let was_created = previous.is_some() || old.is_none();
   938	        if let Some(keys) = previous {
   939	            for key in keys {
   940	                if let Some(count) = self.created.get_mut(&key) {
   941	                    *count -= 1;
   942	                    if *count == 0 { self.created.remove(&key); }
   943	                }
   944	            }
   945	        }
   946	        if old.is_none() {
   947	            if let Some(row) = new { self.inserted.push((table_name.to_owned(), row.clone())); }
   948	        }
   949	        if was_created {
   950	            if let Some(row) = new {
   951	                let keys: Vec<_> = table.indexes.iter().map(|(name, index)| {
   952	                        (table_name.to_owned(), name.clone(), canonical_json(&index_values(index, row)),
   953	                        )
   954	                    }).collect();
   955	                for key in &keys { *self.created.entry(key.clone()).or_default() += 1; }
   956	                self.created_rows.insert(owner, keys);
   957	            }
   958	        }
   959	        #[cfg(all(feature = "sqlite", not(feature = "web-device-check")))]
   960	        if !self.event_free { partition::row_changed(self, table_name, old, new, origin)?; }
   961	        #[cfg(not(feature = "sqlite"))]
   962	        if !self.event_free { partition::account_row_change::<false>(self, table_name, old, new, origin)?; }
   963	        #[cfg(all(feature = "sqlite", feature = "web-device-check"))]
   964	        if self.device { if !self.event_free { partition::account_row_change::<false>(self, table_name, old, new, origin)?; } }
   965	        else if !self.event_free { partition::row_changed(self, table_name, old, new, origin)?; }
   966	        if origin == Origin::Source {
   967	            // @ref LLP 3000.039#3 — even a derived source that ends expired reaches commit-end retirement and its reference actions.
   968	            if old.is_some() || new.is_some() {
   969	                #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
   970	                self.place_assets(table_name, table, old, new)?;
   971	                self.maintain(table_name, old, new)?;
   972	                if self.schema.timelines.iter().any(|t| t.maps(table_name)) { self.timeline_transition(table_name, old, new)?; }
   973	            }
   974	        }
   975	        self.tx.track_time_audience(
   976	            table_name,
   977	            table,
   978	            id,
   979	            new,
   980	            self.context.now.unwrap_or(i64::MIN),

   484	    /// At a program commit's end, retire every source row the commit changed
   485	    /// or inserted whose lifetime has already ended: its final
   486	    /// image was never live at a commit boundary, so it leaves no row for a
   487	    /// later sweep to announce. Inside the commit the
   488	    /// row existed as written (an insert-then-update still works). Engine
   489	    /// bookkeeping, unmetered: the device's prediction does not do it, and
   490	    /// the program's metering is already recorded. Its work, returned, stays
   491	    /// linear in the rows retired: each aggregate row takes one net change
   492	    /// and each audience key is scanned for a live row once. Seeds and loads
   493	    /// ordinarily keep their rows for the sweep; row-keyed view sources use
   494	    /// `retire_seeded_view_sources` to preserve their count-basis contract.
   495	    // @ref LLP 3000#7-decisions-during-execution — a row whose lifetime ended by its own commit's end never exists at a commit boundary.
   496	    #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
   497	    pub(crate) fn retire_expired_births(&mut self) -> Result<crate::meter::Metered, RuntimeError> {
   498	        let Some(now) = self.context.now else { return Ok(Default::default());
   499	        };
   500	        // @ref LLP 3000.036.000.000#3 — an expired final image never grants a new recipient the row's id.
   501	        // The tracker covers synced and unsynced source tables alike. Each
   502	        // distinct entry prepaid its tree node, strings and this vector slot;
   503	        // the rows-written ceiling bounds the commit-end walk.
   504	        // A row that existed before the commit and ends it already expired is
   505	        // retired too: accounted from the partitions it was in at the commit's
   506	        // start, it revokes there and announces nothing to a partition it only
   507	        // entered with its expiring image.
   508	        let mut changed: Vec<(String, String)> = std::mem::take(&mut self.expiry_rows).into_iter().collect();
   509	        if changed.is_empty() {
   510	            return Ok(Default::default());
   511	        }
   512	        // The log's order must not depend on a map's iteration order.
   513	        let order = self.schema.through_order();
   514	        changed.sort_by_key(|(name,id)| {
   515	            (std::cmp::Reverse(order.iter().position(|n| n == name)),id.clone(),
   516	            )
   517	        });
   518	        let meter = std::mem::replace(&mut self.meter, crate::meter::Meter::new(crate::meter::Ceilings::unbounded(), crate::meter::Cut::Abort));
   519	        self.retiring = Some(Default::default());
   520	        let retired = changed.iter().try_for_each(|(table_name, id)| {
   521	            let Some(row) = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.get(allowance, table_name, id))? else { return Ok(());
   522	            };
   523	            let table = self.schema.table(table_name).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("missing table {table_name}")))?;
   524	            if table.expired(&row, now) { self.retire_expired_row(table_name, &row).map(|_| ()) } else { Ok(()) }
   525	        });
   526	        let aggregates = self.retiring.take().map(|retiring| retiring.aggregates).unwrap_or_default();
   527	        let retired = retired.and_then(|()| self.apply_retired_aggregates(aggregates));
   528	        let work = std::mem::replace(&mut self.meter, meter).used;
   529	        retired.map(|()| work)
   530	    }

   593	    fn check_constraints(&mut self, table_name: &str, old: Option<&Value>, new: &Value, effect: Effect) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   594	        let table = self.schema.table(table_name).expect("validated");
   595	        let id = new.field("id")?.as_str()?.to_owned();
   596	        // @ref LLP 3000.039#4.1 — an action's own write consults no rule: probing the child's read rule would draw the shared allowance only where a child exists.
   597	        let readable = match old { Some(old) if effect == Effect::Update && !self.engine_action => {
   598	                !self.inactive_write_target(table_name, old)?
   599	                    && self.check_rule(table_name, Effect::Read, None, old)?
   600	            }

   603	            for (name, index) in table.indexes.iter().filter(|(_, index)| index.unique) {
   604	                // byId can only return this id (already checked on insert).
   605	                // An unchanged admitted unique key cannot acquire a collision.
   606	                if name == "byId" { continue; }

   608	                if old.is_some_and(|old| index_values(index, old) == key) { continue; }

   611	                }

   621	                        }
   622	                    })?
   623	                    && existing.field("id")?.as_str()? != id
