    62	        // A plain loop into a vector: iterator adapters monomorphize per call site on the web device.
    63	        let mut out = Vec::new();
    64	        for (child, table) in &self.tables {
    65	            for (column, action) in &table.on_delete {
    66	                if action.acts() && matches!(table.columns.get(column).map(ColumnType::required), Some(ColumnType::Ref { table: target }) if target == parent) {
    67	                    out.push(Referencing { child, table, column, action: *action });
    68	                }
    69	            }
    70	        }
    71	        out
    72	    }
    73	
    74	    /// A delete of a `parent` row consults its referencing rows, so it needs
    75	    /// read authority on that row (LLP 3000.039 §3 step 1).
    76	    pub fn is_referenced(&self, parent: &str) -> bool { !self.referencing(parent).is_empty() }
    77	
    78	    /// The index a reference is probed through: its column first, then the
    79	    /// child's deadline column when the child can expire, so one seek skips an
    80	    /// expired backlog. A `read through` reference uses its child index.
    81	    pub fn reference_index(&self, child: &str, column: &str) -> Option<&str> {
    82	        let table = self.table(child)?;
    83	        if table.through.as_ref().is_some_and(|t| t.reference == column) {
    84	            return table.indexes.contains_key(through::CHILDREN).then_some(through::CHILDREN);
    85	        }
    86	        // The effective deadline: a read-through child's `$deadline`, else `expire at`.
    87	        let deadline = table.expiry_column();
    88	        table.indexes.iter().find(|(_, index)| {
    89	            let columns = index.columns();
    90	            index.is_plain() && columns.first().map(String::as_str) == Some(column)
    91	                && deadline.is_none_or(|deadline| columns.get(1).map(String::as_str) == Some(deadline))
    92	        }).map(|(name, _)| name.as_str())
    93	    }
    94	
    95	    /// The cap bounding a reference's children: `cap N by <column>` exactly,
    96	    /// or one when the reference itself is a plain unique key. A nullable
    97	    /// reference may have many nulls, but a parent delete probes one non-null
    98	    /// parent id, whose unique group still has at most one row.
    99	    pub fn reference_cap(&self, child: &str, column: &str) -> Option<u32> {
   100	        let table = self.table(child)?;
   101	        let declared = table.constraints.iter().find_map(|c| match c {
   102	            Constraint::Cap { by, max } if by.len() == 1 && by[0] == column => Some(*max),
   103	            _ => None,
   104	        });
   105	        let unique = table.indexes.values().any(|index| index.unique && index.is_plain() && index.columns() == [column]).then_some(1);
   106	        declared.into_iter().chain(unique).min()
   107	    }
   108	
   109	    /// Whether `cap` on `table` skips a group whose reference is null: only a
   110	    /// `set null` reference's own cap does (a null reference has no parent).
   111	    pub fn cap_skips_null(&self, table: &Table, by: &[String], group: &[Value]) -> bool {
   112	        by.iter().zip(group).any(|(column, value)| *value == Value::Null && table.on_delete.get(column) == Some(&OnDelete::SetNull))
   113	    }
   114	
   115	    /// The tables a delete of a `parent` row may write through its writing
   116	    /// actions, and the tables its actions read. A function of the schema, so
   117	    /// a commit's touched set never says which of them a delete reached.
   118	    pub fn action_tables(&self, parent: &str) -> ActionTables {
   119	        let mut out = ActionTables::default();
   120	        let mut queue = vec![parent.to_owned()];
   121	        let mut visited = BTreeSet::new();
   122	        while let Some(table) = queue.pop() {
   123	            if !visited.insert(table.clone()) { continue; }
   124	            for r in self.referencing(&table) {
   125	                out.read.insert(r.child.to_owned());
   126	                if r.action.writes() { out.written.insert(r.child.to_owned()); }
   127	                if r.action == OnDelete::Cascade { queue.push(r.child.to_owned()); }
   128	            }
   129	        }
   130	        // What a write of each of those tables writes in turn: the derived
   131	        // destinations `row_changed` names (aggregate targets, maintained-column
   132	        // owners, row-keyed views).
   133	        let derived: Vec<String> = self.maintains.iter().filter(|m| out.written.contains(&m.source) || m.row_key.as_ref().is_some_and(|k| out.written.contains(&k.table)))
   134	            .flat_map(|m| [Some(m.target.clone()), m.private.as_ref().map(|owner| owner.table.clone())]).flatten().collect();
   135	        out.written.extend(derived);
   136	        out.written.retain(|name| self.visible(name));
   137	        // Private derivations disappear from the device's projection; their
   138	        // event envelope is exported with each direct source's write price.
   139	        let sources: Vec<String> = out.written.iter().cloned().collect();
   140	        for source in sources {
   141	            if let Some(events) = self.write_reservation(&source).and_then(|plan| plan.action_events) { out.written.extend(events.tables); }
   142	        }
   143	        out
   144	    }
   145	
   146	    /// The order a delete's closure is removed in: a row before any table it
   147	    /// must not outlive — its cascade parent, and its `read through` parent.
   148	    /// A cycle through those edges has no valid order and is refused.
   149	    pub fn deletion_precedes(&self, child: &str, parent: &str) -> bool {
   150	        self.table(child).is_some_and(|t| t.through.as_ref().is_some_and(|through| through.parent == parent))
   151	            || self.referencing(parent).into_iter().any(|r| r.child == child && r.action == OnDelete::Cascade)
   152	    }
   153	
   154	    /// A table that reaches itself through cascade and `read through` edges.
   155	    pub fn deletion_cycle(&self) -> Option<String> {
   156	        fn visit<'a>(schema: &'a Schema, name: &'a str, path: &mut Vec<&'a str>, done: &mut BTreeSet<&'a str>) -> Option<String> {
   157	            if path.contains(&name) { return Some(name.to_owned()); }
   158	            if !done.insert(name) { return None; }
   159	            path.push(name);
   160	            for (child, _) in &schema.tables {
   161	                if schema.deletion_precedes(child, name) && let Some(cycle) = visit(schema, child, path, done) { return Some(cycle); }
   162	            }
   163	            path.pop();
   164	            None
   165	        }
   166	        let mut done = BTreeSet::new();
   167	        self.tables.keys().find_map(|name| if self.tables[name].on_delete.values().any(|a| *a == OnDelete::Cascade) || self.is_referenced(name) {
   168	            let mut path = Vec::new();
   169	            visit(self, name, &mut path, &mut done)
   170	        } else { None })
   171	    }
   172	
   173	    /// Whether `name` is a table a timeline orders the writes of.
   174	    pub fn timeline_member(&self, name: &str) -> bool {
   175	        self.timelines.iter().any(|t| t.owns(name) || t.maps(name) || t.authors.first().is_some_and(|a| a == name))
   176	    }
   177	
   178	    /// The most rows of each table one delete of a `parent` row can reach
   179	    /// through its cascades (its closure), the root included: each cascade
   180	    /// edge multiplies by its cap, and edges into a table add up. `None` when
   181	    /// the cascade graph from `parent` is cyclic or a cascade lacks its cap.
   182	    pub fn closure_bounds(&self, parent: &str) -> Option<Vec<(String, u64)>> {
   183	        // Vectors, not maps: the web device pays for every new collection type.
   184	        let mut reach: Vec<String> = vec![parent.to_owned()];
   185	        let mut edges: Vec<(usize, usize, u64)> = Vec::new();
   186	        let mut at = 0;
   187	        while at < reach.len() {
   188	            let table = reach[at].clone();
   189	            for r in self.referencing(&table) {
   190	                if r.action != OnDelete::Cascade { continue; }
   191	                let cap = u64::from(self.reference_cap(r.child, r.column)?);
   192	                let child = reach.iter().position(|t| t == r.child).unwrap_or_else(|| { reach.push(r.child.to_owned()); reach.len() - 1 });
   193	                edges.push((at, child, cap));
   194	            }
   195	            at += 1;
   196	        }
   197	        // Kahn's order over the reached cascade subgraph; a leftover table is a cycle.
   198	        let mut indegree = vec![0_usize; reach.len()];
   199	        for &(_, child, _) in &edges { indegree[child] += 1; }
   200	        let mut bounds = vec![0_u64; reach.len()];
   201	        bounds[0] = 1;
   202	        let mut ready: Vec<usize> = (0..reach.len()).filter(|&t| indegree[t] == 0).collect();
   203	        let mut done = 0;
   204	        while let Some(table) = ready.pop() {
   205	            done += 1;
   206	            for &(from, child, cap) in edges.iter().filter(|(from, _, _)| *from == table) {
   207	                bounds[child] = bounds[child].saturating_add(bounds[from].saturating_mul(cap));
   208	                indegree[child] -= 1;
   209	                if indegree[child] == 0 { ready.push(child); }
   210	            }
   211	        }
   212	        (done == reach.len()).then(|| reach.into_iter().zip(bounds).collect())
   213	    }
   214	
   215	    /// The fixed charge a delete of a `parent` row reserves before it probes,
   216	    /// cascades or clears any row, over every meter: the closure's rows and
   217	    /// their identities, every restrict probe (one seek per closure row, plus
   218	    /// the closure rows it skips), every set-null row, and one engine write of
   219	    /// each, priced from the source-write plan the engine already exports. A
   220	    /// function of the schema only — caps, the reference graph, each table's
   221	    /// indexes and row size, and the exported plans — so a meter, an `E_BOUND`
   222	    /// abort or the physical allowance never depends on how many (hidden) rows
   223	    /// exist, and every host charges alike: a device's projection keeps every
   224	    /// table that can carry an action and every exported price. `None` when the
   225	    /// closure is unbounded (a cycle or a missing cap) or a written table has no
   226	    /// fixed write price. Heap is the closure's identity scratch plus the largest
   227	    /// single row's transient work, plus event images retained until commit.
   228	    // @ref LLP 3000.039#5.1 — the reservation is schema-fixed; LLP 3000.015 §2's law for work shaped by hidden rows.
   229	    pub fn delete_reservation(&self, parent: &str) -> Option<Price> {
   230	        let bounds = self.closure_bounds(parent)?;
   231	        let mut price = [0_u64; 7];
   232	        let mut heap = 0_u64;
   233	        let mut identities = 0_u64;
   234	        let mut gathered = 0_u64;
   235	        let rows_of = |name: &str| bounds.iter().find(|(t, _)| t == name).map_or(0, |(_, n)| *n);
   236	        for (table, n) in &bounds {
   237	            let n = *n;
   238	            if table != parent {
   239	                // Fetched by the closure walk and again, current, before its delete.
   240	                let unit = self.unit_write(table)?;
   241	                heap = heap.max(unit[4]);
   242	                add(&mut price, [unit[0], unit[1], unit[2] + 1, unit[3], 0, unit[5], unit[6]].map(|v| v.saturating_mul(n)));
   243	                identities = identities.saturating_add(n);
   244	                // Before any set-null write, each reached cascade row proves
   245	                // that no physically retained read-through child lies outside
   246	                // the closure. Each child table can skip every reached
   247	                // identity from that table and then inspect one outside
   248	                // witness. Execution performs
   249	                // these probes under reference_prepaid, so their complete
   250	                // schema bound belongs in this outer admission reservation.
   251	                let through_children: Vec<_> = self.children(table).collect();
   252	                let probes_per_row = through_children.iter()
   253	                    .map(|(child, _, _)| rows_of(child).saturating_add(1))
   254	                    .fold(0_u64, u64::saturating_add);
   255	                let probes = n.saturating_mul(probes_per_row);
   256	                add(&mut price, [probes, 0, probes, 0, 0, 0, 0]);
   257	                let outside_heap = through_children.iter()
   258	                    .map(|(name, child, _)| crate::engine::row_copy_ceiling(child).saturating_mul(rows_of(name).saturating_add(1)))
   259	                    .fold(0_u64, u64::saturating_add);
   260	                heap = heap.max(outside_heap);
   261	            }
   262	            for r in self.referencing(table) {
   263	                // A capped walk holds one page of child images per seek.
   264	                let row = crate::engine::row_copy_ceiling(r.table);
   265	                heap = heap.max(row.saturating_mul(REFERENCE_PAGE as u64));
   266	                let seeks = if r.table.expiry_column().is_some() && r.table.through.as_ref().is_none_or(|t| t.reference != r.column) { 2 } else { 1 };
   267	                // A walk over a capped group: a seek per page, and a last, short page per range.
   268	                let walk = |cap: u64| seeks * n + cap.saturating_mul(n) / REFERENCE_PAGE as u64;
   269	                // Every reached row runs the lifetime hook for every through
   270	                // child, including children the closure already cascaded away.
   271	                let through = r.table.through.as_ref().is_some_and(|t| t.reference == r.column);
   272	                if through && table != parent { add(&mut price, [3_u64, 0, 3, 0, 0, 0, 0].map(|v| v.saturating_mul(n))); }
   273	                match r.action {
   274	                    // A read-through child's probe: three seeks per closure row (LLP 3000.014 §6).
   275	                    OnDelete::Restrict if through => {},
   276	                    // One probe per closure row, a row per seek: it may skip the closure
   277	                    // rows that name it (each names one target per reference), then stops
   278	                    // at its first outside witness.
   279	                    OnDelete::Restrict => {
   280	                        let probe = seeks * n + rows_of(r.child) + n;
   281	                        add(&mut price, [2 * probe, probe, seeks * n + rows_of(r.child) + n, 0, 0, 0, 0]);
   282	                    }
   283	                    OnDelete::Cascade => {
   284	                        let pages = walk(u64::from(self.reference_cap(r.child, r.column)?));
   285	                        add(&mut price, [2 * pages, pages, seeks * n, 0, 0, 0, 0]);
   286	                    }
   287	                    OnDelete::SetNull => {
   288	                        let cap = u64::from(self.reference_cap(r.child, r.column)?);
   289	                        gathered = gathered.max(cap);
   290	                        let cleared = cap.saturating_mul(n);
   291	                        let unit = self.unit_write(r.child)?;
   292	                        heap = heap.max(unit[4]);
   293	                        let pages = walk(cap);
   294	                        add(&mut price, [2 * pages, pages, seeks * n, 0, 0, 0, 0]);
   295	                        add(&mut price, [unit[0], unit[1], unit[2] + 1, unit[3], 0, unit[5], unit[6]].map(|v| v.saturating_mul(cleared)));
   296	                    }
   297	                    OnDelete::Keep => {}
   298	                }
   299	            }
   300	        }
   301	        // The root is read again, current, before its own removal.
   302	        price[2] = price[2].saturating_add(1);
   303	        // The closure's identities (table and id) are held until the last
   304	        // delete, with the root's and one page of child ids.
   305	        // A set-null group is gathered whole (at most its cap) before it is cleared.
   306	        price[4] = heap.saturating_add(identities.saturating_add(1 + REFERENCE_PAGE as u64 + gathered).saturating_mul(CLOSURE_IDENTITY_BYTES));
   307	        let mut receiver_steps = 0;
   308	        for (table, _) in &bounds {
   309	            for reference in self.referencing(table) {
   310	                if reference.action.writes() { receiver_steps = receiver_steps.max(self.write_reservation(reference.child)?.action_events?.steps_per_write); }
   311	            }
   312	        }
   313	        price[0] = price[0].saturating_add(price[3].saturating_mul(receiver_steps));
   314	        price[4] = price[4].saturating_add(self.retained_action_heap(parent, price[3])?);
   315	        Some(price)
   316	    }
   317	
   318	    /// Diagnostic recipe price: action work plus the root's ordinary write.
   319	    /// Execution retains its existing separate charges for these two terms.
   320	    pub fn delete_total_reservation(&self, parent: &str) -> Option<Price> {
   321	        let mut total = self.delete_reservation(parent)?;
   322	        add(&mut total, self.unit_write(parent)?);
   323	        Some(total)
   324	    }
   325	
   326	    /// Event images remain live until commit, after action scratch is released.
   327	    pub fn delete_event_heap(&self, parent: &str) -> Option<u64> {
   328	        self.retained_action_heap(parent, self.delete_reservation(parent)?[3])
   329	    }
   330	
   331	    // @ref LLP 3000.039#5.1 — two event images per priced row write, plus bounded keys and audience transitions, retained for the request lifetime.
   332	    fn retained_action_heap(&self, parent: &str, writes: u64) -> Option<u64> {
   333	        let mut per_write = 0;
   334	        for (table, _) in self.closure_bounds(parent)? {
   335	            for reference in self.referencing(&table) {
   336	                if reference.action.writes() {
   337	                    let events = self.write_reservation(reference.child)?.action_events?;
   338	                    per_write = per_write.max(events.heap_per_write);
   339	                }
   340	            }
   341	        }
   342	        Some(writes.saturating_mul(per_write))
   343	    }
   344	
   345	    /// One engine write (delete or set-null update) of a `table` row: fetch and
   346	    /// write it, its index entries (a `words(..)` index at its token bound), a
   347	    /// row copy, and the source-write price the engine exports for the table.
   348	    fn unit_write(&self, name: &str) -> Option<Price> {
   349	        let table = self.table(name)?;
   350	        let plan = self.write_reservation(name)?;
   351	        if plan.server_only { return None; }
   352	        let entries = table.indexes.values().map(|index| match index.word_component() {
   353	            Some((_, fields)) => fields.iter().filter_map(|f| table.columns.get(f)).map(|kind| match kind.required() {
   354	                ColumnType::Text { max } => u64::from(*max), _ => 0,
   355	            }).sum::<u64>().min(crate::words::MAX_TOKENS_PER_ROW as u64),
   356	            None => 1,
   357	        }).fold(0_u64, u64::saturating_add);
   358	        let row = crate::engine::row_copy_ceiling(table);
   359	        // The row copy and every phase's heap are held together until the
   360	        // write's attempt ends (an asset phase beside a column recount): a sum.
   361	        let mut unit = [4 + 2 * entries, 2 * entries, 1, 1, row.saturating_mul(4), 0, 0];
   362	        for phase in 0..=reservations::VIEW_READ {
   363	            add(&mut unit, plan.price(phase));
   364	        }
   365	        // The lifetime hook reserves all child-table witnesses while source
   366	        // phases are still held. Device verification additionally holds the
   367	        // parent and a child scratch image; every host prices the same peak.
   368	        let mut lifetime = 0_u64;
   369	        let mut child_peak = 0_u64;
   370	        for (_, child, _) in self.children(name) {
   371	            let scratch = crate::engine::row_copy_ceiling(child).saturating_mul(3);
   372	            lifetime = lifetime.saturating_add(scratch);
   373	            child_peak = child_peak.max(scratch);
   374	        }
   375	        if lifetime > 0 { unit[4] = unit[4].saturating_add(lifetime).saturating_add(child_peak).saturating_add(row); }
   376	        Some(unit)
   377	    }
   378	}
   379	
   380	/// The tables a delete's actions may write or read (`Schema::action_tables`).
   381	#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
   382	pub struct ActionTables {
   383	    pub written: BTreeSet<String>,
   384	    pub read: BTreeSet<String>,
   385	}
   386	
   387	/// Whether any rule of any table, or the child's own sync, reads `column` of
   388	/// `child` — directly, as a probe key or equality on `child`, or as a hop.
   389	fn carries_authority(schema: &Schema, child: &str, column: &str) -> bool {
   390	    fn term_reads(term: &RuleTerm, own: bool, child: &str, column: &str) -> bool {
   391	        match term {
   392	            RuleTerm::Field(f) | RuleTerm::OldField(f) | RuleTerm::NextField(f) => own && f == column,
   393	            RuleTerm::Reference { .. } | RuleTerm::ReferenceChain { .. } => {
   394	                (own && term.reference_source().is_some_and(|(c, _)| c == column))
   395	                    || term.references().any(|(table, field)| table == child && field == column)
   396	            }
   397	            RuleTerm::Viewer | RuleTerm::Literal(_) => false,
   398	        }
   399	    }
   400	    fn rule_reads(schema: &Schema, rule: &RuleExpr, own: bool, child: &str, column: &str) -> bool {
   401	        match rule {
   402	            RuleExpr::Public { .. } | RuleExpr::Allow | RuleExpr::Deny => false,
   403	            RuleExpr::Eq(a, b) | RuleExpr::Ne(a, b) | RuleExpr::Compare(_, a, b) => term_reads(a, own, child, column) || term_reads(b, own, child, column),
   404	            RuleExpr::And(items) | RuleExpr::Or(items) => items.iter().any(|item| rule_reads(schema, item, own, child, column)),
   405	            RuleExpr::Not(inner) => rule_reads(schema, inner, own, child, column),
   406	            RuleExpr::Exists { table, index, key, equalities, .. } | RuleExpr::Created { table, index, key, equalities, .. } => {
   407	                let probes_column = table == child && (equalities.iter().any(|(field, _)| field == column)
   408	                    || schema.table(child).and_then(|t| t.index(index)).is_some_and(|i| i.columns().iter().take(key.len()).any(|c| c == column)));
   409	                probes_column || key.iter().chain(equalities.iter().map(|(_, t)| t)).any(|term| term_reads(term, own, child, column))
   410	            }
   411	        }
   412	    }
   413	    schema.tables.iter().any(|(name, table)| {
   414	        let own = name == child;
   415	        [&table.rules.read, &table.rules.insert, &table.rules.update, &table.rules.delete].iter().any(|rule| rule_reads(schema, rule, own, child, column))
   416	            || table.constraints.iter().any(|c| matches!(c, Constraint::FinalExistsOnInsert { table: target, index, key }
   417	                if (target == child && schema.table(child).and_then(|t| t.index(index)).is_some_and(|i| i.columns().iter().take(key.len()).any(|c| c == column)))
   418	                    || key.iter().any(|term| term_reads(term, own, child, column))))
   419	    })
   420	}
   421	
   422	/// Why `column` cannot be cleared by its parent's delete, if it cannot: a
   423	/// value that carries authority or meaning beyond "which parent this row has".
   424	// @ref LLP 3000.039#2.2 — set null never changes any rule's verdict, moves a row between audiences, or rewrites a fact resolved through the reference.
   425	pub fn set_null_refusal(schema: &Schema, name: &str, table: &Table, column: &str) -> Option<String> {
   426	    let audience = table.sync.as_ref().is_some_and(|sync| std::iter::once((&sync.audience, sync.horizon.as_ref()))
   427	        .chain(sync.also.iter().map(|arm| (&arm.audience, arm.horizon.as_ref())))
   428	        .any(|(audience, horizon)| match audience {
   429	        Audience::Public => false,
   430	        Audience::Column(c) => c == column,
   431	        Audience::Target { prefix, .. } => prefix.iter().any(|c| c == column),
   432	    } || horizon.is_some_and(|h| table.index(&h.by).is_some_and(|i| i.uses_column(column)))));
   433	    let maintained = schema.maintains.iter().any(|m| m.source == name && m.by.iter().any(|by| by.trim_start_matches('.').starts_with(&format!("{column}."))));
   434	    if !table.columns.get(column).is_some_and(ColumnType::is_optional) { Some("the reference is required; declare it optional (`?`) or choose cascade".into()) }
   435	    else if table.through.as_ref().is_some_and(|t| t.reference == column) { Some("a read-through reference is required and immutable".into()) }
   436	    else if table.immutable_fields().any(|f| f == column) { Some("the column is immutable".into()) }
   437	    else if table.written_by.contains_key(column) { Some("the column is written by its field owner".into()) }
   438	    else if table.sequences.values().any(|p| p == column) { Some("a sequence counts within it".into()) }

   446	/// Why rows of `name` cannot be deleted or cleared by another row's delete.
   447	pub fn write_target_refusal(schema: &Schema, name: &str) -> Option<String> {
   448	    let table = schema.table(name)?;
   449	    if table.constraints.iter().any(|c| matches!(c, Constraint::AppendOnly)) { Some(format!("{name} is append only")) }
   450	    else if !table.written_by.is_empty() { Some(format!("{name} has field-owned (`written by`) columns, whose owners the schema singled out")) }
   451	    else if schema.maintains.iter().filter(|m| m.source == name || m.row_key.as_ref().is_some_and(|k| k.table == name))
   452	        .flat_map(|m| [Some(m.target.as_str()), m.private.as_ref().map(|owner| owner.table.as_str())]).flatten()
   453	        .any(|destination| schema.table(destination).is_some_and(|t| t.sync.is_some() && t.written_by.values().any(|authority| !authority.audience))) {
   454	        Some(format!("{name}'s derived writes deliver private fields, whose recipient authorization has no fixed action price"))
   455	    }
   456	    else if schema.timeline_member(name) { Some(format!("a timeline orders {name}'s writes")) }
   457	    else if schema.maintains.iter().any(|m| m.row_key.as_ref().is_some_and(|k| k.table == name)) { Some(format!("{name} is a row-keyed view's member table, whose writes may recount a group outside any fixed price")) }
   458	    else if schema.maintains.iter().any(|m| m.source == name && matches!(m.kind, MaintainKind::Sum { .. })) { Some(format!("{name} feeds a maintained sum: system work can delete rows despite `delete <- deny`, and a cascade from another parent can reach them; a hidden contribution could push the sum out of range, so whether the delete commits would depend on rows the deleter cannot see")) }
   459	    else if schema.write_reservation(name).is_none_or(|plan| plan.server_only) { Some(format!("{name}'s writes have no fixed price, so a cascade into it cannot be reserved")) }
   460	    else { None }
   461	}
   462	
   463	fn add(to: &mut Price, price: Price) {
   464	    for (to, price) in to.iter_mut().zip(price) { *to = to.saturating_add(price); }
   465	}
   466	
   467	/// Structural admission of `on_delete` (the compiler states each refusal first).
   468	pub fn validate(schema: &Schema) -> Vec<SchemaIssue> {
   469	    let mut issues = Vec::new();
   470	    for (name, table) in &schema.tables {
   471	        for (column, action) in &table.on_delete {
   472	            let path = format!("tables.{name}.onDelete.{column}");
   473	            let mut fail = |message: String| issues.push(SchemaIssue { path: path.clone(), message });
   474	            let Some(ColumnType::Ref { table: parent }) = table.columns.get(column).map(ColumnType::required) else {
   475	                fail(format!("on delete names {column}, which is not a reference column")); continue;
   476	            };
   477	            if table.written_by.contains_key(column) {
   478	                fail(format!("{name}.{column} is field-owned; a private value carries no delete action"));
   479	                continue;
   480	            }
   481	            if !schema.actionable(name) || !schema.actionable(parent) {
   482	                fail(format!("{name}.{column} -> {parent} cannot carry a delete action: ephemeral, engine-owned and receipt or timeline bookkeeping tables keep their own lifetimes"));
   483	                continue;
   484	            }
   485	            let through = table.through.as_ref().is_some_and(|t| &t.reference == column);
   486	            if action.acts() && schema.reference_index(name, column).is_none() {
   487	                fail(format!("{name}.{column} needs its reference index (leading with {column})"));
   488	            }
   489	            if action.writes() {
   490	                if schema.reference_cap(name, column).is_none() {
   491	                    fail(format!("E_CASCADE_BOUND: {} on {name}.{column} needs `cap N by {column}`", action.words()));
   492	                }
   493	                if let Some(reason) = write_target_refusal(schema, name) {
   494	                    fail(format!("{} on {name}.{column}: {reason}", action.words()));
   495	                }
   496	            }
   497	            match action {
   498	                OnDelete::Keep if through => fail(format!("on delete keep on read-through {name}.{column}: a read-through child lives within its parent")),
   499	                OnDelete::SetNull => if let Some(reason) = set_null_refusal(schema, name, table, column) { fail(format!("on delete set null on {name}.{column}: {reason}")); },
   500	                OnDelete::Cascade if through && table.is_expiring() => fail(format!("on delete cascade on read-through {name}.{column} needs a child that never expires")),
   501	                _ => {}
   502	            }
   503	        }
   504	    }
   505	    if let Some(table) = schema.deletion_cycle() {
   506	        issues.push(SchemaIssue { path: format!("tables.{table}"), message: format!("{table} reaches itself through on delete cascade and read through: no order can delete those rows") });
   507	    }
   508	    for name in schema.tables.keys() {
   509	        if schema.is_referenced(name) && schema.delete_reservation(name).is_none()
   510	            && schema.action_tables(name).written.iter().all(|t| write_target_refusal(schema, t).is_none())
   511	            && schema.referencing(name).into_iter().all(|r| !r.action.writes() || schema.reference_cap(r.child, r.column).is_some()) {
   512	            issues.push(SchemaIssue { path: format!("tables.{name}"), message: format!("on delete cascade from {name} reaches {name} again; a cascade cannot be cyclic") });
   513	        }
   514	    }
   515	    issues
   516	}

     1	//! Atomic adoption of the maintained-row address function in the evaluation
     2	//! adapter. The marker and generation publish in the same writer transaction
     3	//! as the target rebuild, so no writer can observe mixed legacy/digest ids.
     4	use super::*;
     5	
     6	pub(super) fn install(
     7	    tx: &store::Tx<'_>,
     8	    schema: &Schema,
     9	    creating: bool,
    10	    generation: u64,
    11	) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
    12	    let current = tx.query(
    13	        "SELECT maintained_identity_version FROM _backend WHERE singleton",
    14	        &[],
    15	    )?[0].get::<_, Option<&str>>(0).map(str::to_owned);
    16	    if current.as_deref() == Some(crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_VERSION) {
    17	        return Ok(generation);
    18	    }
    19	
    20	    let aggregates: Vec<_> = schema.maintains.iter()
    21	        .filter(|maintain| maintain.private.is_none() && maintain.row_key.is_none())
    22	        .cloned()
    23	        .collect();
    24	    if !creating && !aggregates.is_empty() {
    25	        let mut runner = Runner::new(
    26	            tx,
    27	            schema,
    28	            Context::system().at(crate::now_ms()),
    29	            Meter::new(Ceilings::unbounded(), Cut::Abort),
    30	            tx.next_seq()?,
    31	        );
    32	        runner.event_free = true;
    33	        runner.rewrite_legacy_maintained_references(&aggregates)?;
    34	        for maintain in &aggregates {
    35	            runner.rebuild_maintain(maintain)?;
    36	        }
    37	    }
    38	
    39	    let generation = if creating || aggregates.is_empty() {
    40	        generation
    41	    } else {
    42	        generation.checked_add(1)
    43	            .ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Generation("generation overflow".into()))?
    44	    };
    45	    tx.execute(
    46	        "UPDATE _backend SET maintained_identity_version=$1, generation=$2 WHERE singleton",
    47	        &[&crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_VERSION, &store::signed(generation)?],
    48	    )?;
    49	    Ok(generation)
    50	}

    39	    ids: &BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>>,
    40	) -> bool {
    41	    match (kind, value) {
    42	        (crate::schema::ColumnType::Ref { table }, Value::Id(id)) => {
    43	            let Some(next) = ids.get(table).and_then(|ids| ids.get(id)) else { return false };
    44	            *id = next.clone();
    45	            true
    46	        }
    47	        (crate::schema::ColumnType::Optional(inner), value) => rewrite_legacy_maintained_reference(inner, value, ids),
    48	        (crate::schema::ColumnType::List { of, .. } | crate::schema::ColumnType::ListRange { of, .. }, Value::Array(values)) =>
    49	            values.iter_mut().fold(false, |changed, value| rewrite_legacy_maintained_reference(of, value, ids) || changed),
    50	        _ => false,
    51	    }
    52	}

    54	impl Runner<'_> {
    55	    // @ref LLP 3000.022#14.3 — no predicted delta enters receipt-derived state.
    56	    pub(super) fn defer_receipt_maintain(&self, m: &Maintain) -> bool {
    57	        self.device && self.schema.receipt_dependencies.contains_key(&m.target)
    58	    }
    59	
    60	    // Cache ordinary group keys once per target/query. Predicates and receipt
    61	    // fields are never evaluated; unknown/computed keys conservatively freeze
    62	    // the target. An unpinned read is incomplete if any group is dirty, while
    63	    // each returned row still decides independently whether to recount.
    64	    #[inline(never)]
    65	    pub(super) fn receipt_maintain_pending(&mut self, m: &Maintain, group: Option<&[Value]>) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
    66	        if !self.defer_receipt_maintain(m) { return Ok(false); }
    67	        if !self.receipt_pending_groups.contains_key(&m.target) {
    68	            let fields = if let Some(k) = &m.row_key { vec![k.source_key.clone()] }
    69	                else { m.by.iter().map(|f| m.aliases.get(f).unwrap_or(f).clone()).collect() };
    70	            let mut groups = self.receipt_overlay_groups(&m.source, &fields, !m.computed.is_empty())?;
    71	            if let Some(k) = &m.row_key {
    72	                let member = self.receipt_overlay_groups(&k.table, std::slice::from_ref(&k.member_key), false)?;
    73	                groups = groups.zip(member).map(|(mut source, member)| { source.extend(member); source });
    74	            }
    75	            self.receipt_pending_groups.insert(m.target.clone(), groups);
    76	        }
    77	        let dirty = self.receipt_pending_groups[&m.target].as_ref().is_none_or(|keys|
    78	            group.map_or(!keys.is_empty(), |group| keys.iter().any(|key| key == group)));
    79	        if dirty {
    80	            self.value_source_incomplete = true;
    81	            self.components.note(|frame| frame.pending = true);
    82	        }
    83	        Ok(dirty)
    84	    }
    85	
    86	    fn receipt_overlay_groups(&self, table: &str, fields: &[String], computed: bool) -> Result<Option<Vec<Vec<Value>>>, RuntimeError> {
    87	        if !self.tx.has_provisional(table)? { return Ok(Some(Vec::new())); }
    88	        if computed || fields.iter().any(|f| self.schema.receipt_dependencies.get(table).is_some_and(|owned| owned.contains(f))) {
    89	            return Ok(None);
    90	        }
    91	        self.tx.provisional_groups(table, fields)
    92	    }
    93	
    94	    // Recover a read's parent/group from the pinned index. A member point uses
    95	    // one ordinary-key lookup; a scan without the parent stays conservative.
    96	    pub(super) fn receipt_read_group(&mut self, m: &Maintain, index: &str, key: &[Value]) -> Result<Option<Vec<Value>>, RuntimeError> {
    97	        if !self.defer_receipt_maintain(m) { return Ok(None); }
    98	        let columns = self.schema.tables[&m.target].indexes[index].columns();
    99	        let pinned = |field: &str| columns.iter().position(|c| c == field).and_then(|i| key.get(i)).cloned();
   100	        if let Some(k) = &m.row_key {
   101	            if let Some(parent) = pinned(&k.member_key) { return Ok(Some(vec![parent])); }
   102	            if let Some(id) = pinned("member").or_else(|| pinned("id")) {
   103	                let row = self.metered_scan(|r, scope| r.tx.get(scope, &k.table, id.as_str()?))?;
   104	                return Ok(row.and_then(|row| row.field(&k.member_key).ok().cloned()).map(|v| vec![v]));
   105	            }
   106	            return Ok(None);
   107	        }
   108	        Ok(m.by.iter().map(|f| pinned(f)).collect())
   109	    }
   110	
   111	    pub(super) fn maintain(&mut self, source: &str, old: Option<&Value>, new: Option<&Value>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   112	        self.receipt_pending_groups.clear();
   113	        // Inserts ordinarily charge their actual aggregate work. A deferred
   114	        // predicate cannot select that work on a device, so use the same public
   115	        // worst-case reservation as update/delete before skipping it. Already
   116	        // prepaid writes must not pay twice.
   117	        if self.device && !self.maintain_prepaid && self.schema.maintains.iter().any(|m|
   118	            m.source == source && m.private.is_none() && m.row_key.is_none() && (self.schema.receipt_dependencies.contains_key(&m.target) || self.schema.tables[&m.target].sync.is_none())) {
   119	            self.reserve_maintains(source, &self.schema.tables[source])?;
   120	        }
   121	        self.maintain_row_views(source, old, new)?;
   122	        let maintains = self.schema.maintains.iter().filter(|maintain| maintain.source == source && maintain.row_key.is_none());
   123	        for maintain in maintains {
   124	            if self.defer_receipt_maintain(maintain) || (self.device && self.schema.tables[&maintain.target].sync.is_none()) { continue; }
   125	            let source_bytes = super::write_target::row_copy_ceiling(&self.schema.tables[&maintain.source]);
   126	            let target = &self.schema.tables[&maintain.target];
   127	            let bytes = source_bytes.saturating_mul(2).saturating_add(super::write_target::row_copy_ceiling(target).saturating_mul(16 + 4 * target.indexes.len() as u64));
   128	            let prepaid = self.maintain_prepaid;
   129	            if maintain.private.is_some() && self.column_prepaid { self.maintain_prepaid = true; }
   130	            let result = self.maintain_scratch(bytes, |runner| runner.maintain_one(maintain, old, new));
   131	            self.maintain_prepaid = prepaid;
   132	            result?;
   133	        }
   134	        Ok(())
   135	    }
   136	
   137	    // @ref LLP 3000.007#20.9 — reserve interpreted images, both keys, targets and index buffers before allocation; release transient ownership on every exit.
   138	    pub(super) fn maintain_scratch<T>(&mut self, bytes: u64, work: impl FnOnce(&mut Self) -> Result<T, RuntimeError>) -> Result<T, RuntimeError> {
   139	        if self.maintain_prepaid { return work(self); }
   140	        self.meter.heap(bytes)?;
   141	        let result = work(self);
   142	        self.meter.used.heap_bytes = self.meter.used.heap_bytes.saturating_sub(bytes);
   143	        result
   144	    }
   145	
   146	    fn maintain_one(&mut self, maintain: &Maintain, old: Option<&Value>, new: Option<&Value>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   147	        let table = self.schema.table(&maintain.source).expect("validated");
   148	        let mut changes: Vec<(Vec<Value>, i128)> = Vec::new();
   149	        for (image, direction) in [(old, -1), (new, 1)] {
   150	            let Some(image) = image else { continue };
   151	            self.charge_maintain(MeterKind::Steps, maintain.evaluation_steps())?;
   152	            let image = crate::schema::row_image(image, table);
   153	            if !maintain.selected(&image) { continue; }
   154	            let key = maintain.source_key(&image);
   155	            let change = delta(maintain, &image, direction)?;
   156	            if let Some(existing) = changes.iter_mut().find(|(k, _)| *k == key) { existing.1 += change; }
   157	            else { changes.push((key, change)); }
   158	        }
   159	        for (key, change) in changes {
   160	            #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
   161	            if let Some(retiring) = self.retiring.as_mut() {
   162	                let entry = retiring.aggregates.entry((maintain.target.clone(), canonical_json(&key))).or_insert_with(|| (key, 0));
   163	                entry.1 = entry.1.checked_add(change).ok_or_else(|| aggregate_overflow(maintain))?;
   164	                continue;
   165	            }
   166	            if change != 0 || self.live_sum(maintain) {
   167	                self.apply_aggregate(maintain, key, change, None)?;
   168	            }
   169	        }
   170	        Ok(())
   171	    }
   172	
   173	    /// Apply a retirement's net aggregate changes, one per target row, in
   174	    /// key order. Only a total the commit really ends with can overflow.
   175	    #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
   176	    pub(super) fn apply_retired_aggregates(&mut self, changes: BTreeMap<(String, String), (Vec<Value>, i128)>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   177	        let schema = self.schema;
   178	        for ((target, _), (key, change)) in changes {
   179	            let maintain = schema.maintain_for(&target).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("missing maintain for {target}")))?;
   180	            if change != 0 || self.live_sum(maintain) {
   181	                self.apply_aggregate(maintain, key, change, None)?;
   182	            }
   183	        }
   184	        Ok(())
   185	    }

   187	    #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
   188	    pub(crate) fn rebuild_maintain_reported(&mut self, maintain: &Maintain, report: &mut crate::store::adoption_report::AdoptionReport) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   189	        let started = std::time::Instant::now();
   190	        self.rebuilt_source_rows = 0;
   191	        self.rebuild_maintain(maintain)?;
   192	        let rows = self.rebuilt_source_rows;
   193	        report.views.push(crate::store::adoption_report::ViewBuild { name: maintain.label(), rows, elapsed: started.elapsed() });
   194	        Ok(())
   195	    }

   197	    /// Derive every legacy-to-digest aggregate id map to a fixed point, then
   198	    /// rewrite typed references before rebuilding the target rows. The fixed
   199	    /// point matters when one aggregate groups by a reference to another.
   200	    /// Every pass is inside the adoption writer transaction, so no reader can
   201	    /// observe a dangling intermediate reference.
   202	    #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
   203	    pub(crate) fn rewrite_legacy_maintained_references(&mut self, maintains: &[Maintain]) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
   204	        let mut legacy = Vec::new();
   205	        for maintain in maintains.iter().filter(|maintain| maintain.private.is_none() && maintain.row_key.is_none()) {
   206	            let target = self.schema.tables[&maintain.target].clone();
   207	            let fields: Vec<_> = maintain.group_fields().into_iter().map(|field| {
   208	                let kind = target.columns.get(&field).expect("validated maintain group").clone();
   209	                (field, kind)
   210	            }).collect();
   211	            let mut rows = Vec::new();
   212	            let mut bounds = Bounds::default();
   213	            loop {
   214	                let page = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.scan(allowance, &maintain.target, "byId", &[], &bounds, Dir::Asc, 256))?;
   215	                if page.is_empty() { break; }
   216	                for (row, encoded) in page {
   217	                    bounds.after = crate::key::decode(&encoded);
   218	                    let old = row.field("id")?.as_str()?.to_owned();
   219	                    let key = fields.iter().map(|(field, kind)| Ok((kind.clone(), row.field(field)?.clone())))
   220	                        .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, RuntimeError>>()?;
   221	                    rows.push((old, key));
   222	                }
   223	            }
   224	            legacy.push((maintain.target.clone(), rows));
   225	        }
   226	
   227	        let mut ids: BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>> = BTreeMap::new();
   228	        let mut settled = false;
   229	        // One dependency edge can settle per pass.  Count identities rather
   230	        // than target tables: one aggregate target may contain an arbitrary
   231	        // acyclic chain of references to other rows in that same target.
   232	        let identity_count = legacy.iter().map(|(_, rows)| rows.len()).sum::<usize>();
   233	        // The first pass also materializes empty target maps, so retain one
   234	        // additional observation pass even when every target is empty.
   235	        for _ in 0..=identity_count.saturating_add(1) {
   236	            let mut next_ids: BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>> = BTreeMap::new();
   237	            for (target, rows) in &legacy {
   238	                let target_ids = next_ids.entry(target.clone()).or_default();
   239	                for (old, key) in rows {
   240	                    let key: Vec<_> = key.iter().map(|(kind, value)| {
   241	                        let mut value = value.clone();
   242	                        rewrite_legacy_maintained_reference(kind, &mut value, &ids);
   243	                        value
   244	                    }).collect();
   245	                    let next = maintained_id(&key);
   246	                    if old != &next { target_ids.insert(old.clone(), next); }
   247	                }
   248	            }
   249	            if next_ids == ids {
   250	                ids = next_ids;
   251	                settled = true;
   252	                break;
   253	            }
   254	            ids = next_ids;
   255	        }
   256	        if !settled {
   257	            return Err(RuntimeError::Schema("legacy aggregate identity references form a cycle".into()));
   258	        }
   259	
   260	        let references: Vec<_> = self.schema.tables.iter().filter_map(|(name, table)| {
   261	            let columns: Vec<_> = table.columns.iter().filter_map(|(column, kind)|
   262	                has_legacy_maintained_reference(kind, &ids).then(|| (column.clone(), kind.clone())))
   263	                .collect();
   264	            (!columns.is_empty()).then(|| (name.clone(), table.clone(), columns))
   265	        }).collect();
   266	        let mut rewritten = 0_u64;
   267	        for (name, table, columns) in references {
   268	            let mut bounds = Bounds::default();
   269	            loop {
   270	                let page = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.scan(allowance, &name, "byId", &[], &bounds, Dir::Asc, 256))?;
   271	                if page.is_empty() { break; }
   272	                for (old, encoded) in page {
   273	                    bounds.after = crate::key::decode(&encoded);
   274	                    let mut next = old.clone();
   275	                    let mut changed = false;
   276	                    if let Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) = &mut next {
   277	                        for (column, kind) in &columns {
   278	                            let Some(value) = fields.get_mut(column) else { continue };
   279	                            changed |= rewrite_legacy_maintained_reference(kind, value, &ids);
   280	                        }
  1743	    } else {
  1744	        // The rule is exactly the probe the sync inverts: a second disjunct
  1745	        // would admit viewers the partition never delivers to; a conjunct
  1746	        // or a literal in the key would deliver rows the rule denies.
  1747	        let exact = format!("sync to {target_name}[{spelled_prefix}] is only sound when the read rule is exactly `exists {target_name}[{spelled_want}]`; it reads under `{}`", table.rules.read.quarry());
  1748	        // @ref LLP 3000.036.000.000#2.2 — a union's group arm inverts its own whole disjunct.
  1749	        let probe = if sync.is_union() {
  1750	            audience_rule.disjuncts().into_iter().find(|disjunct| matches!(disjunct, RuleExpr::Exists { .. })).ok_or_else(|| exact.clone())?
  1751	        } else { audience_rule.as_ref() };
  1752	        let RuleExpr::Exists { table: probed, index, key, equalities, .. } = probe else { return Err(exact) };
  1753	        if probed != target_name || *key != want || !equalities.is_empty() {
  1754	            return Err(exact);
  1755	        }
  1756	        let index_def = target.index(index).ok_or_else(|| format!("the read rule probes unknown index {target_name}.{index}"))?;
  1757	        let index_columns = index_def.columns();
  1758	        if !index_def.is_plain() || index_columns.len() != want.len() {
  1759	            return Err(format!("the read rule's probe uses {target_name}.{index}, which does not cover exactly `{spelled_want}`"));
  1760	        }
  1761	        let probe_principal = &index_columns[prefix.len()];
  1762	        if probe_principal != principal {
  1763	            return Err(format!("sync to {target_name}[{spelled_prefix}] by .{principal} reads recipients from {target_name}.{principal}, but the read rule binds viewer to {target_name}.{probe_principal}; say `by .{probe_principal}`"));
  1764	        }
  1765	        index_columns[..prefix.len()].to_vec()
  1766	    };
  1767	    for column in prefix {
  1768	        if table.columns.get(column).is_some_and(ColumnType::is_optional) && !table.through.as_ref().is_some_and(|t| t.fields.contains_key(column)) {
  1769	            return Err(format!("sync to {target_name}[{spelled_prefix}] needs required group keys; {table_name}.{column} is optional. Make every content group column required so online rules and device partitions name the same group"));
  1770	        }
  1771	    }
  1772	    for column in &columns {
  1773	        if target.columns.get(column).is_some_and(ColumnType::is_optional) {
  1774	            return Err(format!("sync to {target_name}[{spelled_prefix}] needs required group keys; {target_name}.{column} is optional. Make every audience group column required so membership discovery, revocation and content delivery name the same group"));
  1775	        }
  1776	    }
  1777	    let mut by_group = columns.clone();
  1778	    by_group.push(principal.clone());
  1779	    let (group_index, group_def) = target.indexes.iter().find(|(_, index)| index.is_plain() && index.columns() == by_group).ok_or_else(|| format!("sync to {target_name}[{spelled_prefix}] needs an index on {target_name} over {}", by_group.join(", ")))?;
  1780	    if !group_def.unique {
  1781	        return Err(format!("the audience index {target_name}.{group_index} must be unique: with two rows for one group and principal, deleting one would revoke a group the other still grants"));
  1782	    }
  1783	    let mut by_principal = vec![principal.clone()];
  1784	    by_principal.extend(columns.iter().cloned());
  1785	    let principal_index = target.indexes.iter().find(|(_, index)| index.is_plain() && index.columns().starts_with(&by_principal)).map(|(name, _)| name.clone()).ok_or_else(|| format!("sync to {target_name}[{spelled_prefix}] needs an index on {target_name} whose leading columns are {} so a device can find its groups", by_principal.join(", ")))?;
  1786	    Ok(AudienceBinding { group_index: group_index.clone(), columns, principal: principal.clone(), principal_index })
  1787	}

  1789	/// The maintained target's row address for a source image: the `by` values.
  1790	pub fn maintained_key(source: &Value, by: &[String]) -> Vec<Value> {
  1791	    by.iter().map(|field| source.field(field).cloned().unwrap_or(Value::Null)).collect()
  1792	}

  1794	/// Activation marker for the maintained-row address function. A missing or
  1795	/// older marker rebuilds every aggregate target before the generation opens.
  1796	pub const MAINTAINED_ID_META: &str = "maintained_id_version";
  1797	pub const MAINTAINED_ID_VERSION: &str = "sha256-v1";
  1798	
  1799	/// The id of a maintained row is a fixed-size digest of its typed group key.
  1800	/// Programs address aggregates by their group index, never by this internal
  1801	/// id. Domain separation makes future encodings explicit migrations.
  1802	// @ref LLP 3000.007.003#30-aggregate-target-identity-and-migration — every aggregate writer, synthetic check row and adoption rebuild shares this bounded identity.
  1803	pub fn maintained_id(key: &[Value]) -> String {
  1804	    crate::value::digest(&("snapback4-maintained-id/sha256-v1", key))
  1805	}
  1806	
  1807	#[test]
  1808	fn maintained_identity_is_fixed_size_and_domain_separated() {
  1809	    let short = maintained_id(&[Value::String("x".into())]);
  1810	    let long = maintained_id(&[Value::String("x".repeat(100_000))]);
  1811	    assert_eq!(short.len(), 64);
  1812	    assert_eq!(long.len(), 64);
  1813	    assert_ne!(short, long);
  1814	    assert_ne!(short, crate::value::digest(&[Value::String("x".into())]));
  1815	}

  1817	/// Whether a value is (or contains) the reserved system principal.
  1818	pub fn contains_system_principal(value: &Value) -> bool {
  1819	    match value {
  1820	        Value::Id(id) => id == crate::SYSTEM_PRINCIPAL,
  1821	        Value::Array(items) => items.iter().any(contains_system_principal),
  1822	        Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) => fields.values().any(contains_system_principal),
  1823	        _ => false,
  1824	    }
  1825	}
  1826	
  1827	/// Missing optional columns read as null; missing required columns with a
  1828	/// literal default read that value. Contextual defaults belong to inserts.
  1829	pub fn materialize_optional_fields(row: &mut Value, table: &Table) {
  1830	    let fields = match row {
  1831	        Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) => fields,
  1832	        _ => return,
  1833	    };
  1834	    for (name, kind) in &table.columns {
  1835	        if !fields.contains_key(name) {
  1836	            if table.maintained.contains_key(name) {
  1837	                fields.insert(name.clone(), Value::Int(0));
  1838	            } else if kind.is_optional() {
  1839	                fields.insert(name.clone(), Value::Null);
  1840	            } else if let Some(ColumnDefault::Literal(value)) = table.defaults.get(name) {
  1841	                fields.insert(name.clone(), value.clone());
  1842	            }
  1843	        }
  1844	    }
  1845	}
  1846	
  1847	/// Borrow complete images; materialize old images only when needed.
  1848	pub fn row_image<'a>(row: &'a Value, table: &Table) -> std::borrow::Cow<'a, Value> {
  1849	    if table.columns.keys().all(|column| row.field(column).is_ok()) { return std::borrow::Cow::Borrowed(row); }
  1850	    let mut image = row.clone();
  1851	    materialize_optional_fields(&mut image, table);
  1852	    std::borrow::Cow::Owned(image)
  1853	}

  1856	mod tests;
  1857	/// The type an argument declares as a column type, for value validation.
  1858	pub fn arg_as_column(kind: &ArgType) -> Option<ColumnType> {
  1859	    Some(match kind {
  1860	        ArgType::Cursor | ArgType::Scalar => return None,
  1861	        ArgType::Id => ColumnType::Id,
  1862	        ArgType::Principal => ColumnType::Principal,
  1863	        ArgType::Ref { table } => ColumnType::Ref { table: table.clone() },
  1864	        ArgType::Text { max, .. } => ColumnType::Text { max: *max },
  1865	        ArgType::Bytes { max } => ColumnType::Bytes { max: *max },
  1866	        ArgType::Image { max } => ColumnType::Image { max: *max, once: false },
  1867	        ArgType::Video { max } => ColumnType::Video { max: *max },
  1868	        ArgType::File { max, types } => ColumnType::File { max: *max, types: types.clone() },
  1869	        ArgType::Int => ColumnType::Int,
  1870	        ArgType::IntRange { min, max } => ColumnType::IntRange { min: *min, max: *max },
  1871	        ArgType::Bool => ColumnType::Bool,
  1872	        ArgType::Time => ColumnType::Time,
  1873	        ArgType::Json { max_bytes } => ColumnType::Json { max_bytes: *max_bytes },
  1874	        ArgType::Optional(inner) => ColumnType::Optional(Box::new(arg_as_column(inner)?)),
  1875	        ArgType::List { of, max } => ColumnType::List { of: Box::new(of.as_deref().map(arg_as_column).flatten().unwrap_or(ColumnType::Json { max_bytes: 4096 })), max: *max },
  1876	        ArgType::ListRange { of, min, max } => ColumnType::ListRange { of: Box::new(of.as_deref().and_then(arg_as_column).unwrap_or(ColumnType::Json { max_bytes: 4096 })), min: *min, max: *max },
  1877	        ArgType::Enum { variants } => ColumnType::Enum { variants: variants.clone() },

   292	    /// Build one aggregate from the rows in the store: the target's rows go,
   293	    /// then every source row contributes once. A schema change that adds or
   294	    /// redefines a `maintain` calls this, so a count over existing rows is

   299	        let saved = self.column_rebuild;
   300	        self.column_rebuild |= maintain.private.is_some();

   302	        self.column_rebuild = saved;
   303	        self.meter.used.heap_bytes = heap;
   304	        result

   318	                bounds.after = crate::key::decode(&key);

   321	                self.charge_maintain(MeterKind::IndexEntries, entries)?;

   368	    fn live_sum(&self, maintain: &Maintain) -> bool {
   369	        matches!(maintain.kind, MaintainKind::Sum { .. }) && self.schema.table(&maintain.source).is_some_and(|source| source.is_expiring())

   372	    /// A zero sum is still a group while source rows remain: one signed
   373	    /// contribution may expire before the other. Keep its candidate row so
   374	    /// a scan, snapshot and offline replica can discover the later live sum.
   375	    fn aggregate_source_present(&mut self, maintain: &Maintain, key: &[Value]) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {

   393	    fn aggregate_source_complete(&mut self, maintain: &Maintain, key: &[Value]) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {

   405	    fn apply_aggregate(&mut self, maintain: &Maintain, key: Vec<Value>, change: i128, source_present: Option<bool>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {

   408	        }
   409	        let id = maintained_id(&key);
   410	        let target = self.schema.table(&maintain.target).expect("validated");
   411	        self.charge_maintain(MeterKind::Examined, 1)?;
   412	        let existing = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.get(allowance, &maintain.target, &id))?;
   413	        let target_key = target_group_key(maintain, &key);
   414	        if self.device && existing.is_none() && !self.upsert_absence_proven(&maintain.target, "byGroup", &target_key)? {
   415	            self.unknown_fact(&maintain.target, "byGroup", &target_key, "aggregate base");
   416	            return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction("the affected aggregate value or its absence is not known locally; queued without a predicted row".into()));
   417	        }
   418	        let old_value = existing.as_ref().and_then(|row| row.field("value").ok()).map(Value::as_int).transpose()?.unwrap_or(0);

   420	        if !(I53_MIN as i128..=I53_MAX as i128).contains(&next) {
   421	            return Err(aggregate_overflow(maintain));
   422	        }

   424	            Some(present) => present,
   425	            None => self.aggregate_source_present(maintain, &key)?,
   426	        };
   427	        if next == 0 && !keep_zero {
   428	            if let Some(existing) = existing {
   429	                self.refuse_timeline_write(&maintain.target, crate::schema::Effect::Delete)?;
   430	                let entries = self.tx.delete(&maintain.target, target, &existing)?;
   431	                self.charge_maintain(MeterKind::IndexEntries, entries)?;
   432	                self.row_changed(&maintain.target, Some(&existing), None, Origin::Maintained)?;
   433	            }
   434	            self.mirror_column(maintain, &key, 0)?;
   435	            return Ok(());
   436	        }
   437	        let mut row = crate::small_map::collect([("id".to_owned(), Value::Id(id.clone())), ("value".to_owned(), Value::Int(next as i64))]);

   446	        self.charge_maintain(MeterKind::IndexEntries, entries)?;
   447	        self.row_changed(&maintain.target, existing.as_ref(), Some(&row), Origin::Maintained)?;

   452	pub(super) fn delta(maintain: &Maintain, source: &Value, direction: i64) -> Result<i128, RuntimeError> {
   453	    Ok(match &maintain.kind {
   454	        MaintainKind::Count => i128::from(direction),
   455	        MaintainKind::Sum { of } => i128::from(direction).checked_mul(i128::from(source.field(of)?.as_int()?)).ok_or_else(|| aggregate_overflow(maintain))?,
   456	    })
   457	}

   111	fn int_range(kind: &ColumnType) -> bool {
   112	    match kind {
   113	        ColumnType::IntRange { .. } => true,
   114	        ColumnType::Optional(inner) | ColumnType::List { of: inner, .. } | ColumnType::ListRange { of: inner, .. } => int_range(inner),
   115	        _ => false,
   116	    }
   117	}
   118	
   119	fn ordered_units(table: &Table, rule: &RuleExpr) -> bool {
   120	    let units = |term: &RuleTerm| matches!(term, RuleTerm::Field(f) if matches!(table.columns.get(f), Some(ColumnType::Decimal { .. } | ColumnType::Money { .. })));
   121	    match rule {
   122	        RuleExpr::Compare(_, l, r) => units(l) || units(r),
   123	        RuleExpr::And(items) | RuleExpr::Or(items) => items.iter().any(|item| ordered_units(table, item)),
   124	        RuleExpr::Not(inner) => ordered_units(table, inner),
   125	        _ => false,
   126	    }
   127	}
   128	
   129	fn ordered(rule: &RuleExpr) -> bool {
   130	    match rule {
   131	        RuleExpr::Compare(..) => true,
   132	        RuleExpr::And(items) | RuleExpr::Or(items) => items.iter().any(ordered),
   133	        RuleExpr::Not(inner) => ordered(inner),
   134	        _ => false,
   135	    }
   136	}
   137	
   138	impl Schema {
   139	    pub fn supported_capabilities() -> Vec<String> { CAPABILITIES.iter().map(|(name, _)| (*name).into()).collect() }
   140	    fn has_receipt_columns(&self) -> bool {
   141	        self.tables.iter().any(|(name, table)| table.maintained.keys().any(|field|
   142	            self.receipt_dependencies.get(name).is_some_and(|fields| fields.contains(field))))
   143	    }
   144	    pub fn required_capabilities(&self) -> BTreeSet<String> {
   145	        CAPABILITIES.iter().filter(|(_, needs)| needs(self)).map(|(name, _)| (*name).into()).collect()
   146	    }
   147	}
   148	
   149	impl Serialize for Schema {
   150	    fn serialize<S: Serializer>(&self, serializer: S) -> Result<S::Ok, S::Error> {
   151	        let required = self.required_capabilities();
   152	        // The derive's field order, omissions and bytes are unchanged for
   153	        // ordinary schemas, including the serialized conformance corpus.
   154	        if required.is_empty() { return Wire::serialize(self, serializer); }
   155	        let mut wire = self.clone();
   156	        for table in wire.tables.values_mut() {
   157	            table.constraints.retain(|c| !matches!(c, Constraint::Recorded));
   158	        }
   159	        let mut carrier = wire.tables.first_entry().ok_or_else(||
   160	            serde::ser::Error::custom("E_SCHEMA_CAPABILITY: required capabilities need a table carrier"))?;
   161	        carrier.get_mut().constraints.push(Constraint::Capabilities(required));
   162	        Wire::serialize(&wire, serializer)
   163	    }
   164	}
   165	
   166	impl<'de> Deserialize<'de> for Schema {
   167	    fn deserialize<D: Deserializer<'de>>(deserializer: D) -> Result<Self, D::Error> {
   168	        // The private remote derive uses the ordinary
   169	        // streaming serde codec. No JSON-value or content-buffer replay.
   170	        let mut schema = Wire::deserialize(deserializer)?;
   171	        let mut declared = BTreeSet::new();
   172	        let mut carriers = 0;
   173	        let mut legacy = false;
   174	        for table in schema.tables.values_mut() {
   175	            let mut recorded = 0;
   176	            table.constraints.retain(|constraint| {
   177	                if let Constraint::Capabilities(names) = constraint {
   178	                    carriers += 1;
   179	                    declared.extend(names.iter().cloned());
   180	                    false
   181	                } else if matches!(constraint, Constraint::Recorded) {
   182	                    recorded += 1;
   183	                    false
   184	                } else { true }
   185	            });
   186	            if recorded > 1 || (recorded != 0 && table.recorded.is_empty()) {
   187	                return Err(serde::de::Error::custom("E_SCHEMA_CAPABILITY: invalid legacy Recorded marker"));
   188	            }
   189	            if recorded != 0 { legacy = true; declared.insert("recorded-attribution".into()); }
   190	        }
   191	        for name in &declared {
   192	            if !CAPABILITIES.iter().any(|(known, _)| name == known) {
   193	                return Err(serde::de::Error::custom(format!("E_SCHEMA_CAPABILITY: unsupported engine capability {name}; upgrade the engine/device")));
   194	            }
   195	        }
   196	        let mut required = schema.required_capabilities();
   197	        // @ref LLP 3000.022#14.3 — RY already serialized the dependency closure.
   198	        // RP stamps every emitted schema so old devices refuse its new prediction
   199	        // facts, but an RP reader must still open RY's kept backend/database.
   200	        // All other capabilities and the carrier shape remain exact.
   201	        let legacy_receipt_prediction = !declared.contains("receipt-derived-prediction-v1")
   202	            && required.remove("receipt-derived-prediction-v1");
   203	        // The price carrier can be absent in an old projection. Missing prices
   204	        // are fenced per program, rather than bricking a kept store.
   205	        for cap in ["source-write-reservations-v1", "source-write-reservations-v2"] {
   206	            if declared.contains(cap) { required.insert(cap.into()); }
   207	            else { required.remove(cap); }
   208	        }
   209	        // Stores written before the digest migration have no carrier for this
   210	        // capability. Admit that persisted schema for server-side rebuilding;
   211	        // its next serialization stamps the capability, so old devices refuse.
   212	        let mut legacy_semantic_capabilities = BTreeSet::new();
   213	        if !declared.contains("maintained-id-sha256-v1")
   214	            && required.remove("maintained-id-sha256-v1") {
   215	            legacy_semantic_capabilities.insert("maintained-id-sha256-v1".into());
   216	        }
   217	        // Kept pre-Wave-12 schemas need the server's new expiry action path,
   218	        // then stamp the device fence on their next published projection.
   219	        if !declared.contains("expiry-reference-actions-v1")
   220	            && required.remove("expiry-reference-actions-v1") {
   221	            legacy_semantic_capabilities.insert("expiry-reference-actions-v1".into());
   222	        }
   223	        // Before the shared fence, the binder emitted Recorded on F2 tables
   224	        // even when the same schema also declared timelines. Only that legacy
   225	        // representation infers its full requirements; modern carriers remain
   226	        // exact, including when mixed with a legacy marker.
   227	        if legacy && carriers == 0 {
   228	            // A legacy marker only covers the capabilities that predate the fence.
   229	            // New semantics must never inherit permission from this escape hatch.
   230	            declared = required.iter().filter(|name| matches!(name.as_str(),
   231	                "maintained-column" | "recorded-attribution" | "timeline" | "timeline-v2")).cloned().collect();
   232	        }
   233	        if declared != required || carriers + usize::from(legacy) != usize::from(!required.is_empty()) {
   234	            return Err(serde::de::Error::custom(format!("E_SCHEMA_CAPABILITY: schema requires {required:?}, but declares {declared:?} in {carriers} carriers")));
   235	        }
   236	        let had_prices = !schema.source_reservations.is_empty();
   237	        schema.prepare_receipt_dependencies();
   238	        // Opening an old blob preserves its wire shape. Complete visible
   239	        // declarations can still price a write on demand; hidden ones cannot.
   240	        if !had_prices { schema.source_reservations.clear(); }
   241	        schema.legacy_receipt_prediction = legacy_receipt_prediction
   242	            || (!declared.contains("source-write-reservations-v1") && !schema.receipts.is_empty());
   243	        schema.legacy_semantic_capabilities = legacy_semantic_capabilities.into();
   244	        Ok(schema)
   245	    }
   246	}

diff --git a/snapback4/crates/snapback4-core/src/engine/postgres/maintained_identity_upgrade.rs b/snapback4/crates/snapback4-core/src/engine/postgres/maintained_identity_upgrade.rs

--- /dev/null

@@ -0,0 +1,49 @@
+//! Atomic adoption of the maintained-row address function in the evaluation
+//! adapter. The marker and generation publish in the same writer transaction
+//! as the target rebuild, so no writer can observe mixed legacy/digest ids.
+use super::*;
+
+pub(super) fn install(
+    tx: &store::Tx<'_>,
+    schema: &Schema,
+    creating: bool,
+    generation: u64,
+) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
+    let current = tx.query(
+        "SELECT maintained_identity_version FROM _backend WHERE singleton",
+        &[],
+    )?[0].get::<_, Option<&str>>(0).map(str::to_owned);
+    if current.as_deref() == Some(crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_VERSION) {
+        return Ok(generation);
+    }
+
+    let aggregates: Vec<_> = schema.maintains.iter()
+        .filter(|maintain| maintain.private.is_none() && maintain.row_key.is_none())
+        .cloned()
+        .collect();
+    if !creating && !aggregates.is_empty() {
+        let mut runner = Runner::new(
+            tx,
+            schema,
+            Context::system().at(crate::now_ms()),
+            Meter::new(Ceilings::unbounded(), Cut::Abort),
+            tx.next_seq()?,
+        );
+        runner.event_free = true;
+        for maintain in &aggregates {
+            runner.rebuild_maintain(maintain)?;
+        }
+    }
+
+    let generation = if creating || aggregates.is_empty() {
+        generation
+    } else {
+        generation.checked_add(1)
+            .ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Generation("generation overflow".into()))?
+    };
+    tx.execute(
+        "UPDATE _backend SET maintained_identity_version=$1, generation=$2 WHERE singleton",
+        &[&crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_VERSION, &store::signed(generation)?],
+    )?;
+    Ok(generation)
+}

+#[test]
+#[ignore = "requires isolated local Postgres; scripts/test-postgres.sh"]
+fn reopening_legacy_maintained_ids_rebuilds_before_publishing_the_generation() {
+    let bound = snapback4_lang::compile(&[("schema.q".into(), r#"
+table entries:
+  bucket: int
+  public
+view totals: count entries by .bucket
+  public
+"#.into())]);
+    assert!(bound.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:?}", bound.diagnostics);
+    let schema: Schema = serde_json::from_str(&serde_json::to_string(&bound.schema).unwrap()).unwrap();
+    let programs = bound.programs.into_iter().map(|p| p.program).collect::<Vec<_>>();
+    let url = std::env::var("SNAPBACK4_EVAL_POSTGRES").expect("private test-postgres.sh database");
+    let name = format!("sb4_eval_maintained_id_{:x}", crate::ids::seed());
+    let mut engine = PostgresEngine::create(Client::connect(&url, postgres::NoTls).unwrap(), &name, schema, programs).unwrap();
+    engine.load([("entries".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("entry".into())), ("bucket", Value::Int(7))]))]).unwrap();
+    let digest = crate::schema::maintained_id(&[Value::Int(7)]);
+    let legacy = crate::value::canonical_json(&[Value::Int(7)]);
+    let target = engine.schema.tables["totals"].clone();
+    let generation = engine.generation();
+    let tx = engine.store.transaction(Some(WriteMode::Serialized)).unwrap();
+    let old = tx.get("totals", &digest).unwrap().expect("current aggregate");
+    tx.delete("totals", &target, &old).unwrap();
+    let mut old = old;
+    if let Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) = &mut old {
+        fields.insert("id".into(), Value::Id(legacy.clone()));
+    }
+    tx.put("totals", &target, &old, None).unwrap();
+    tx.execute("UPDATE _backend SET maintained_identity_version=NULL WHERE singleton", &[]).unwrap();
+    tx.commit().unwrap();
+    drop(engine);
+
+    let mut reopened = PostgresEngine::open(Client::connect(&url, postgres::NoTls).unwrap(), &name).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(reopened.generation(), generation + 1);
+    let tx = reopened.store.transaction(None).unwrap();
+    assert!(tx.get("totals", &legacy).unwrap().is_none());
+    let rebuilt = tx.get("totals", &digest).unwrap().expect("digest aggregate");
+    assert_eq!(rebuilt.field("value").unwrap(), &Value::Int(1));
+    tx.rollback().unwrap();
+}

 };
 use std::collections::BTreeMap;
 
+const EXPIRY_TABLE_CURSOR: &str = "$expiry-table";
+
+/// Rotate a sweep's table order after the last table that consumed a bounded
+/// visit. Per-table row cursors alone can starve every later table when an
+/// earlier table contains a permanently restricted due row.
+pub(crate) fn resume_expiry_tables(
+    mut tables: Vec<String>,
+    cursors: &BTreeMap<String, Vec<Value>>,
+) -> Vec<String> {
+    let after = cursors
+        .get(EXPIRY_TABLE_CURSOR)
+        .and_then(|cursor| cursor.first())
+        .and_then(|value| value.as_str().ok());
+    if let Some(index) = after.and_then(|after| tables.iter().position(|table| table == after)) {
+        let next = (index + 1) % tables.len().max(1);
+        tables.rotate_left(next);
+    }
+    tables
+}
+
+pub(crate) fn mark_expiry_table(cursors: &mut BTreeMap<String, Vec<Value>>, table: &str) {
+    cursors.insert(EXPIRY_TABLE_CURSOR.into(), vec![Value::String(table.into())]);
+}

+/// The copied corpus is a frozen image of the pre-digest store. Translate
+/// maintained target identities at the adapter boundary so its logical values
+/// remain an oracle for the current address function. Other row ids retain
+/// their exact frozen spelling.
+fn legacy_maintained_ids(schema: &Schema, rows: &[ReceiptRow]) -> Result<BTreeMap<String, String>, String> {
+    let mut ids = BTreeMap::new();
+    for receipt in rows {
+        let Some(maintain) = schema.maintains.iter().find(|maintain| maintain.target == receipt.table && maintain.row_key.is_none()) else { continue };
+        let old = match receipt.row.field("id") {
+            Ok(Value::Id(id)) => id,
+            Ok(_) => return Err(format!("{}.id is not an id", receipt.table)),
+            Err(error) => return Err(format!("{}.id: {error}", receipt.table)),
+        };
+        let key = maintain.by.iter().map(|field| receipt.row.field(field).cloned().map_err(|error| format!("{}.{}: {error}", receipt.table, field))).collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()?;
+        let new = snapback4_core::schema::maintained_id(&key);
+        if let Some(prior) = ids.insert(old.clone(), new.clone())
+            && prior != new
+        {
+            return Err(format!("legacy id {old} names more than one maintained group"));
+        }
+    }
+    Ok(ids)
+}
+
+fn translate_legacy_maintained_row(schema: &Schema, table: &str, row: &mut Value, ids: &BTreeMap<String, String>) {
+    if !schema.maintains.iter().any(|maintain| maintain.target == table && maintain.row_key.is_none()) { return; }
+    let (Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields)) = row else { return };
+    let Some(Value::Id(id)) = fields.get_mut("id") else { return };
+    if let Some(replacement) = ids.get(id) {
+        *id = replacement.clone();
+    }
+}
+
+fn translate_legacy_maintained_expected(expected: &mut Expected, ids: &BTreeMap<String, String>) -> Result<(), String> {
+    if ids.is_empty() || expected.error_code.is_some() { return Ok(()); }
+    let Some(canonical) = &expected.canonical_result else { return Ok(()) };
+    let mut value: Value = serde_json::from_str(canonical).map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;
+    translate_legacy_maintained_result(&mut value, ids);
+    expected.canonical_result = Some(snapback4_core::value::canonical_json(&value));
+    Ok(())
+}
+
+fn translate_legacy_maintained_result(value: &mut Value, ids: &BTreeMap<String, String>) {
+    match value {
+        Value::Id(id) => {
+            if let Some(replacement) = ids.get(id) {
+                *id = replacement.clone();
+            }
+        }
+        Value::Array(values) => values.iter_mut().for_each(|value| translate_legacy_maintained_result(value, ids)),
+        Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) => fields.values_mut().for_each(|value| translate_legacy_maintained_result(value, ids)),
+        _ => {}
+    }
+}

+Seed commits preserve ordinary expired fixture images for the later sweep,
+but sources of row-keyed views keep the established count-basis exception.
+After normal maintenance, the seed filters its commit-end expiry tracker to
+those sources and retires them through this same common action path. The
+retirement uses the engine-owned, unbounded meter after the authored seed
+work has been charged; applies `restrict`, `cascade`, and `set null`; and
+defers the resulting maintained deltas until the retirement pass completes.
+This prevents a born-expired source from reviving under a later clock
+rollback without broadening retirement to unrelated fixture or raw-load
+rows. The SQLite and evaluation Postgres seed adapters share this ordering;
+the wasm interpreter has no server seed API or physical expiry-retirement
+path.
+
