+
+#[test]
+fn seeded_expired_row_view_sources_do_not_revive_on_clock_rollback() {
+    let mut e = Engine::memory(compile(false), vec![]).unwrap();
+    e.seed_at([("members".into(), member(0, 0, 0))], 1).unwrap();
+    e.seed_at([("messages".into(), message(0, 1, 99, false, Some(100)))], 1).unwrap();
+
+    // Updating a live source into an expired final image and seeding a new
+    // born-expired source both retire through the common action path.
+    e.seed_at([
+        ("messages".into(), message(0, 1, 99, false, Some(5))),
+        ("messages".into(), message(1, 1, 99, false, Some(5))),
+    ], 10).unwrap();
+    assert!(e.store().rows("messages").unwrap().is_empty());
+
+    // Ordinary expired fixture images keep the seed contract.
+    let grant = with_deadline(object([
+        ("id", id("expired-grant")),
+        ("conversationId", id("room")),
+        ("principal", id("reader")),
+    ]), Some(5));
+    e.seed_at([("access".into(), grant)], 10).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("access").unwrap().len(), 1);
+
+    // A later rollback cannot resurrect either retired source into the live
+    // acquisition, even though both deadlines would otherwise be live at 2.
+    let views = e.store().rows("unread").unwrap();
+    let schema = e.schema().clone();
+    let tx = e.store_mut().transaction().unwrap();
+    let mut runner = Runner::new(&tx, &schema, Context::new("reader", Default::default()).at(2),
+        Meter::new(Ceilings::unbounded(), Cut::Abort), 0);
+    let acquired = runner.live_acquisition_batch("unread", &views).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(acquired.len(), 1);
+    assert_eq!(acquired[0].as_ref().map(|row| field(row, "value")), Some(0));
+}

@@ -120,6 +120,60 @@ fn a_refused_reseed_leaves_the_store_untouched() {
     assert_eq!(count(&mut engine, "L1"), Value::Int(1));
 }
 
+const EXPIRY_RESET: &str = "table aFree:
+  until: time
+  expire at .until
+  public
+table zBlocked:
+  until: time
+  expire at .until
+  public
+table zReferences:
+  root: zBlocked on delete restrict
+  public
+";
+
+fn expiry_engine() -> Engine {
+    let bound = snapback4_lang::compile(&[("expiry-reset.q".into(), EXPIRY_RESET.into())]);
+    assert!(bound.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:?}", bound.diagnostics);
+    Engine::new_at(Store::memory().unwrap(), bound.schema, bound.programs.into_iter().map(|p| p.program), 0).unwrap()
+}
+
+fn expiring(table: &str, id: &str) -> (String, Value) {
+    (table.into(), object([("id", Value::Id(id.into())), ("until", Value::Int(10))]))
+}
+
+/// A successful reset creates a fresh store identity and therefore a fresh
+/// bounded expiry walk. A refused reset leaves both the store and its walk
+/// continuation untouched.
+#[test]
+fn reset_restarts_the_expiry_walk_only_after_commit() {
+    let blocked_seed = || [
+        expiring("aFree", "a"),
+        expiring("zBlocked", "z"),
+        ("zReferences".into(), object([
+            ("id", Value::Id("w".into())),
+            ("root", Value::Id("z".into())),
+        ])),
+    ];
+
+    let mut refused = expiry_engine();
+    refused.seed_at(blocked_seed(), 0).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(refused.sweep_expired(10, 1).unwrap(), 0, "the reverse table walk first retains zBlocked");
+    assert!(refused.dev_reset_at(vec![("aFree".into(), Value::Null)], 0).is_err());
+    assert_eq!(refused.sweep_expired(10, 1).unwrap(), 1, "a refused reset preserves the cursor that rotates next to aFree");
+    assert!(refused.store().rows("aFree").unwrap().is_empty());
+    assert_eq!(refused.store().rows("zBlocked").unwrap().len(), 1);
+
+    let mut committed = expiry_engine();
+    committed.seed_at(blocked_seed(), 0).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(committed.sweep_expired(10, 1).unwrap(), 0);
+    committed.dev_reset_at(vec![expiring("aFree", "a"), expiring("zBlocked", "z")], 0).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(committed.sweep_expired(10, 1).unwrap(), 1);
+    assert_eq!(committed.store().rows("aFree").unwrap().len(), 1, "the fresh reverse walk has not reached aFree");
+    assert!(committed.store().rows("zBlocked").unwrap().is_empty(), "the fresh reverse walk starts at zBlocked");
+}
+
 /// A reset empties every table together, so no referential action runs and
 /// no reference is left naming a removed row (LLP 3000.039 §6.5); the reseed
 /// rebuilds the reference indexes, so the next delete cascades and restricts

 table snapshot after each retirement; this is extensionally the same sequential
 store update while avoiding an exponential functional-update expression tree.
+The formal sweep carries the same in-engine, across-call continuation as the server: the
+last visited table rotates the next call even after a complete scan, and a
+call stopped at its visited-row bound retains each table's last
+`(selected index components,id)` key until the following call scans its tail
+and wrapped head.
 The Lean difftest generator preserves
 seeded expiry values and requested prelude/final sweeps, advances the formal
 store with each engine sweep, then compares the following program outcome.

     3	/-!
     4	# Rows, stores, rules and visibility
     5	
     6	A store maps each table name to its rows. Rules are evaluated against the
     7	whole store: an `exists t[..]` probe is an exact-key existence test that does
     8	not consult `t`'s own read rule (OPEN R1). A row is *visible* to a viewer
     9	when its table's read rule holds for it; every read the evaluator performs
    10	goes through `visibleRows`, so the read semantics in `Eval.lean` never sees
    11	a hidden row (`Disclosure.lean`).
    12	-/

    14	namespace Quarry

    21	def Row.get (r : Row) (c : String) : Scalar :=
    22	  if c = "id" then .id r.id else (r.cols.lookup c).getD .null
    23	
    24	def Row.toValue (r : Row) : Value :=
    25	  .row (("id", .s (.id r.id)) :: r.cols.map fun p => (p.1, .s p.2))
    26	
    27	/-- The store: the rows of each table. -/
    28	abbrev Store := String → List Row
    29	
    30	def Store.empty : Store := fun _ => []
    31	
    32	def Store.set (s : Store) (t : String) (rs : List Row) : Store :=
    33	  fun t' => if t' = t then rs else s t'
    34	
    35	def Store.insertRow (s : Store) (t : String) (r : Row) : Store := s.set t (s t ++ [r])

    42	structure Imgs where

    81	/-- Rule evaluation against the whole store `s`, for viewer `v`. -/

   209	-- @ref LLP 3000.036.003#3-semantics — lower read lifetimes filter every logical read at the server clock.
   210	def opened (td : TableDecl) (now : Int) (r : Row) : Bool :=
   211	  match td.notBefore with
   212	  | none => true
   213	  | some c => match r.get c with
   214	    | .null => true
   215	    | .int opens => opens <= now
   216	    | _ => false
   217	
   218	/-- Whether a row remains before its table's upper read lifetime. Null has no
   219	upper bound; the checked schema guarantees that a non-null value is a time. -/
   220	-- @ref LLP 3000.036.003#3-semantics — upper read lifetimes filter every logical read before physical cleanup.
   221	def unexpired (td : TableDecl) (now : Int) (r : Row) : Bool :=
   222	  match td.expire with
   223	  | none => true
   224	  | some c => match r.get c with
   225	    | .null => true
   226	    | .int closes => now < closes
   227	    | _ => false
   228	
   229	def live (td : TableDecl) (now : Int) (r : Row) : Bool := opened td now r && unexpired td now r
   230	
   231	/-- Referential actions ignore expired child images but still govern a child
   232	whose lower read lifetime has not opened yet, matching the physical engine. -/
   233	def unexpiredStore (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (now : Int) : Store := fun t =>
   234	  match sch.table? t with
   235	  | some td => (s t).filter (unexpired td now)
   236	  | none => []
   237	
   238	/-- The physical store with rows outside their logical lifetime removed. Rule
   239	probes use this store too, so a future or expired row cannot authorize work. -/
   240	def openedStore (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (now : Int) : Store := fun t =>
   241	  match sch.table? t with
   242	  | some td => (s t).filter (live td now)
   243	  | none => []
   244	
   245	/-- Read-rule visibility for one image at a request clock. The image may be a
   246	physical write target, while every probe it performs sees only opened rows. -/
   247	def readableAt (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (v : List Nat) (now : Int)
   248	    (t : String) (r : Row) : Bool :=
   249	  match sch.table? t with
   250	  | some td => live td now r && td.read.eval (openedStore sch s now) v { self := some r }
   251	  | none => false
   252	
   253	/-- Request-time visibility, including the server-enforced lower read lifetime. -/
   254	def visibleRowsAt (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (v : List Nat) (now : Int)
   255	    (t : String) : List Row :=
   256	  (s t).filter (readableAt sch s v now t)
   257	
   258	/-- What a read can observe: the visible rows of each table. -/
   259	abbrev View := String → List Row

     3	/-!
     4	# Running a program
     5	
     6	`run` takes (schema, helpers, store, viewer, program, arguments, ceiling)
     7	to an outcome. This is the function the later harness oracle calls.
     8	-/
     9	
    10	namespace Quarry
    11	
    12	/-- An outcome. A query answers with data, `complete` and the returned
    13	page's continuation (`next`, null when none), or is unavailable (a cut
    14	scalar read), or refuses. A mutation commits a result and a new store, or
    15	refuses (and changes nothing). -/
    16	inductive Outcome where
    17	  | answer (data : Value) (complete : Bool) (next : Value)
    18	  | unavailable
    19	  | committed (result : Value) (store : Store)
    20	  | refused (code : String)
    21	
    22	/-- The world of a query: the view; every write refuses. -/
    23	def queryHooks : Hooks View where
    24	  view _ vw := vw
    25	  apply _ _ _ := throw (.refuse "E_QUARRY_PLACEMENT")
    26	
    27	/-- The world of a mutation: the store; reads see its visible rows. -/
    28	def storeHooks : Hooks Store where
    29	  view cx s := visibleRowsAt cx.schema s cx.viewer cx.now
    30	  apply := applyWrite
    31	
    32	-- @ref LLP 3000.036.003#6 — born-expired and updated-expired final images retire in the writer transaction.
    33	/-- Rows whose final images a mutation changed. Commit-end expiry retirement
    34	is scoped to this set; pre-existing expired backlog remains for the ordinary
    35	sweep. -/
    36	abbrev ChangedRows := List (String × List Nat)
    37	
    38	structure MutationWorld where
    39	  store : Store
    40	  changed : ChangedRows := []
    41	
    42	/-- The explicit address of an insert-like write that reached its write arm.
    43	This retains a structurally identical expired replacement for commit-end
    44	retirement, while excluding `insert if absent` live-clash no-ops. -/
    45	def RWrite.changedExplicitId? (cx : Ctx) (s : Store) : RWrite → Option (String × List Nat)
    46	  | .insert t fields ifAbsent => do
    47	    let td ← cx.schema.table? t
    48	    let fs ← (scalarsE fields).toOption
    49	    let rid ← (insertId fs).toOption
    50	    let img ← (buildImage td rid fs eInput).toOption
    51	    if ifAbsent && (findClash ((s t).filter (unexpired td cx.now))
    52	        (["id"] :: td.uniques) img none).isSome
    53	    then none
    54	    else some (t, rid)
    55	  | .upsert t key patch =>
    56	    match key.lookup "id" with
    57	    | some (.s (.id rid)) => some (t, rid)
    58	    | _ => match patch.lookup "id" with
    59	      | some (.s (.id rid)) => some (t, rid)
    60	      | _ => none
    61	  | _ => none
    62	
    63	def changedFinalRows (sch : Schema) (before after : Store) : ChangedRows :=
    64	  sch.tables.flatMap fun td => (after td.name).filterMap fun row =>
    65	    match (before td.name).find? fun old => old.id == row.id with
    66	    | none => some (td.name, row.id)
    67	    | some old => if old == row then none else some (td.name, row.id)
    68	
    69	def mutationHooks : Hooks MutationWorld where
    70	  view cx w := visibleRowsAt cx.schema w.store cx.viewer cx.now
    71	  apply cx w rw := match applyWrite cx w.store rw with
    72	    | .error e => .error e
    73	    | .ok (value, store) =>
    74	      let changed := w.changed ++ changedFinalRows cx.schema w.store store
    75	      let changed := match rw.changedExplicitId? cx w.store with
    76	        | some address => changed ++ [address]
    77	        | none => changed
    78	      .ok (value, { store, changed := changed.eraseDups })
    79	
    80	/-- Runtime retires changed expiry rows in reverse through-table order, then
    81	ascending id order. Read-through tables are outside this model fragment, so
    82	its through order is the schema's lexical table order. -/
    83	def changedRetirementOrder (sch : Schema) (changed : ChangedRows) : ChangedRows :=
    84	  (expiryRetirementTables sch).flatMap fun td =>
    85	    (changed.filter fun address => address.1 == td.name).mergeSort fun a b =>
    86	      lex cmpNat a.2 b.2 != .gt
    87	
    88	/-- Retire only rows written by this mutation whose final image is already
    89	expired. A restrict refusal aborts the mutation; cascade and set-null actions
    90	are in the same transition. -/
    91	def retireExpiredChanged (sch : Schema) (now : Int) : Store → ChangedRows → Except Stop Store
    92	  | s, [] => pure s
    93	  | s, (t, rid) :: rest =>
    94	    match sch.table? t with
    95	    | none => retireExpiredChanged sch now s rest
    96	    | some td =>
    97	      match findRow (s t) [("id", .id rid)] with
    98	      | none => retireExpiredChanged sch now s rest
    99	      | some row =>
   100	        if expired td now row then do
   101	          let s ← refDeleteFrom sch (unexpiredStore sch s now) s t row
   102	          retireExpiredChanged sch now s rest
   103	        else retireExpiredChanged sch now s rest
   104	
   105	def bindArgs (params : List Param) (args : List (String × Value)) : Except Stop Env :=
   106	  params.mapM fun p => match args.lookup p.name with
   107	    | some v => pure (p.name, (v, none))
   108	    | none => if p.optional then pure (p.name, (.null, none)) else throw (.refuse "E_INPUT")
   109	
   110	def defaultFuel : Nat := 100000
   111	
   112	structure Case where
   113	  schema : Schema
   114	  helpers : List Helper := []
   115	  store : Store
   116	  viewer : List Nat
   117	  now : Int := 0
   118	  program : Program
   119	  args : List (String × Value) := []
   120	  budget : Option Nat := none
   121	  /-- Run only the server expiry sweep and return its resulting store. -/
   122	  sweepOnly : Bool := false
   123	  /-- In-engine sweep continuation supplied by the differential driver. -/
   124	  sweepCursor : SweepCursor := {}
   125	  /-- Visited-row bound for the sweep; examples default to a complete pass. -/
   126	  sweepLimit : Option Nat := none
   127	
   128	def Case.ctx (c : Case) : Ctx :=
   129	  { schema := c.schema, viewer := c.viewer, now := c.now, helpers := c.helpers, budget := c.budget,
   130	    mutation := c.program.kind == .mutation }
   131	
   132	def flowValue : Flow → Value × Value
   133	  | .normal => (.null, .null)
   134	  | .ret v nx => (v, nx.getD .null)
   135	
   136	def runQuery (c : Case) : Outcome :=
   137	  match bindArgs c.program.params c.args with
   138	  | .error (.refuse code) => .refused code
   139	  | .error .unavailable => .unavailable
   140	  | .ok env =>
   141	    let vw := visibleRowsAt c.schema c.store c.viewer c.now
   142	    match (execStmts queryHooks defaultFuel c.ctx vw env c.program.body).run {} with
   143	    | .ok ((fl, _, _), rs) => let (v, nx) := flowValue fl; .answer v rs.complete nx
   144	    | .error (.refuse code) => .refused code
   145	    | .error .unavailable => .unavailable
   146	
   147	def runMutation (c : Case) : Outcome :=
   148	  match bindArgs c.program.params c.args with
   149	  | .error (.refuse code) => .refused code
   150	  | .error .unavailable => .unavailable
   151	  | .ok env =>
   152	    match (execStmts mutationHooks defaultFuel c.ctx { store := c.store } env c.program.body).run {} with
   153	    | .ok ((fl, w, _), _) => match retireExpiredChanged c.schema c.now w.store
   154	        (changedRetirementOrder c.schema w.changed) with
   155	      | .ok s' => .committed (flowValue fl).1 s'
   156	      | .error (.refuse code) => .refused code
   157	      | .error .unavailable => .refused "E_BOUND"
   158	    | .error (.refuse code) => .refused code
   159	    | .error .unavailable => .refused "E_BOUND"
   160	
   161	def run (c : Case) : Outcome :=
   162	  if c.sweepOnly then
   163	    let (store, cursor) := sweepExpired c.schema c.store c.now c.sweepCursor c.sweepLimit
   164	    .committed cursor.toValue store
   165	  else match c.program.kind with
   166	    | .query => runQuery c
   167	    | .mutation => runMutation c
   168	
   169	end Quarry

   198	/// Check `sources` with [`crate::compile`], then translate their surface
   199	/// trees. A program outside the fragment is recorded per program in
   200	/// [`LeanModule::programs`]; a schema construct outside it refuses the whole

   202	pub fn lean(sources: &[(String, String)]) -> Result<LeanModule, LeanError> {
   203	    let bound = crate::compile(sources);
   204	    if !bound.diagnostics.is_empty() {
   205	        return Err(LeanError::Diagnostics(bound.diagnostics.iter().map(|d| format!("{}: {}", d.code, d.message)).collect()));

   293	fn table_shape(t: &ast::TableDecl) -> R<Table> {

   304	        }

   311	            (c.readable_by_audience, "audience-field"),
   312	            (c.maintained.is_some(), "maintained"),
   313	            (c.default.is_some(), "default"),

   326	            (TypeKind::Ref { .. }, Some(OnDelete::Cascade)) => Some("cascade"),
   327	            (TypeKind::Ref { .. }, Some(OnDelete::SetNull)) => Some("setNull"),

   202	## What is only executable, or not proved
   203	
   204	- **Refusal codes and their precedence** (OPEN W1–W4) are executed and
   205	  checked by the examples, but not proved. No theorem says which code a
   206	  given failure produces.
   207	- **Filters with nested reads.** `pageRead_complete`, `countRead_eq` and
   208	  `existsRead_eq` assume the filter is a pure predicate (`FiltIs`). Filters
   209	  without reads satisfy this. A filter with a nested read does too when its
   210	  value does not depend on the meter, but no theorem discharges that
   211	  hypothesis.
   212	- **Query-level completeness.** It is proved per read (`pageRead_complete`).
   213	  That a request's `complete` is the conjunction of its reads holds by
   214	  construction (`markIncomplete` only clears the flag) and is not stated as
   215	  a theorem.
   216	- **Non-functional facts.** Termination needs no proof (fuel). Fuel
   217	  exhaustion (`E_MODEL_FUEL`) and ill-typed states (`E_MODEL_TYPE`) are
   218	  model-only refusals that a checked program cannot reach.
   219	
   220	## The Lean oracle: the emitter, the case format and the comparison
   221	
   222	The model is an oracle of the Stage 1 harness (LLP 3000.035 §5.2), built on
   223	2026-10-08:
   224	
   225	- **The emitter**, `snapback4_lang::emit::lean`
   226	  (`crates/snapback4-lang/src/emit/lean.rs`), translates a checked program's
   227	  *surface* tree (never the binder's IR, so the binder is under test too)
   228	  into the terms of `Syntax.lean`, with the expansions listed there. Anything
   229	  outside the core fragment is an `Unsupported` with a stable reason (for
   230	  example `call-sum`, `now`, `loop`, `type-money`), never a
   231	  partial translation. `snapback4 check --emit-lean <file.q>` prints one
   232	  file's translation.
   233	- **The runner**, `quarry-oracle` (`Oracle.lean`), reads one case per line
   234	  and writes one outcome per line, staying alive across cases (one process
   235	  per harness worker).
   236	- **The harness**, `snapback4-difftest run-lean`
   237	  (`crates/snapback4-difftest/src/lean.rs`), compares the engine (SQLite,
   238	  default ceilings) with the model on every supported generated case,
   239	  shrinks each new signature (`lean--{field}--{engine}~{model}`) and replays
   240	  it. Findings and their diagnoses are in
   241	  `crates/snapback4-difftest/cases/found/lean--*`.

   255	    "delete": "deny" } ] },
   256	  "helpers": [ { "name": "identity", "params": ["x"], "body": { "var": "x" } } ],
   257	  "store": { "items": [ { "id": "r0", "cols": { "owner": { "id": "bob" }, "maybe": { "null": null } } } ] },
   258	  "viewer": "bob",
   259	  "now": 0,
   260	  "program": { "name": "run", "kind": "query",
   261	               "params": [ { "name": "bucket", "optional": false }, { "name": "c", "optional": true } ],
   262	               "body": [ { "ret": { "page": { "table": "items", "pins": [ ["bucket", { "var": "bucket" }] ],
   263	                                              "filter": null, "order": ["label", "score"], "desc": false,
   264	                                              "take": 20, "after": { "var": "c" } } } } ] },
   265	  "args": { "bucket": { "int": "0" }, "c": { "null": null } },
   266	  "budget": null
   267	}
   268	```
   269	
   270	The format's rules:
   271	
   272	- **Scalars are tagged.** The forms are `{"null":null}`, `{"bool":b}`,
   273	  `{"int":"…"}`, `{"text":"…"}`, `{"id":"…"}` and `{"bytes":"hex"}`. An int
   274	  is a decimal string, so no float is ever involved. The wire's untyped form
   275	  is not enough, because an id is not a text (OPEN V1). Values add
   276	  `{"arr":[…]}` and `{"row":[[name, value], …]}` (ordered pairs).
   277	- **Rules, terms, expressions, statements and writes** use one key per
   278	  constructor of `Syntax.lean`, with the constructor's arguments
   279	  (`CaseJson.lean` is the decoder). `"viewer"`, `"allow"` and `"deny"` are
   280	  bare strings.
   281	- **Store rows** are `{"id":…,"cols":{name: scalar}}`; columns are put in the
   282	  table's declared order and an absent column is null.
   283	- **Lower read lifetimes** use a table's optional `notBefore` column and the
   284	  case's integer `now`. Null and values at or before `now` are open. The model
   285	  filters the whole logical view, including rule probes and write-result
   286	  visibility, while write target resolution and constraints remain physical.
   287	  Generated model cases seed at this one request clock; bounded publication
   288	  of an existing due-row backlog is a runtime/device lifecycle concern.
   289	- **Upper read lifetimes** use a table's optional `expire` column. An expiring
   290	  table also carries `expiryOrder`, the checked physical index components
   291	  before the store-appended id. A case with `sweep: true` may supply the
   292	  server's in-engine tagged `sweepCursor` and `sweepLimit`; its committed result is the
   293	  next cursor, so a differential sequence resumes both table rotation and the
   294	  per-table full index tuple. The model independently executes that plan but
   295	  does not re-prove the compiler's physical index synthesis.
   296	- **The output** is one of:
   297	  - `{"kind":"answer","data":…,"complete":b,"next":…}`;
   298	  - `{"kind":"unavailable"}`;
   299	  - `{"kind":"refused","code":"…"}`;
   300	  - `{"kind":"committed","result":…,"store":{…}}` (the store in the input's
   301	    row form, so a follow-up case can run over it);
   302	  - `{"kind":"error","error":"…"}` for a line that does not decode. The
   303	    harness treats it as an emitter defect, never as a verdict.
   304	
   305	  Every value is tagged. (`Outcome.toJson` in `Json.lean`, used by the
   306	  examples, still prints ids and text alike, as on the wire.)
   307	
   308	How the harness compares against the engine's outcome record:
   309	
   310	| Model | Engine field | Rule |
   311	| --- | --- | --- |
   312	| `kind` | refusal / `unavailable` / data / committed | exact |
   313	| `refused.code` | `refusal.code` (or a failed write's `why.code`) | exact; sites are not modelled |
   314	| `answer.data`, `committed.result` | `data`, `result` | exact, both tagged; rows compare as field maps |
   315	| `answer.complete` | `complete` | exact |
   316	| `answer.next` | `next` | presence only (OPEN C1); then each side continues from its own cursor and the next page is compared, to the end |
   317	| `committed.store` | the engine's store | through `observe` (a point reread), run on each side's resulting store |
   318	| (none) | meter fields, cut sites, `tables`, `seq` | not compared: out of scope; explicit expiry sweeps advance and compare both stores |
   319	
   320	The engine runs at the default ceilings and the model unbounded, so no
   321	compared case is cut. Comparing cuts (OPEN M1: a cut is reported, and
   322	continuation reaches the uncut answer, `cut_continuation`) is not yet done.
     1	import Quarry.Store
     2	
     3	/-!
     4	# Maintained aggregate identity
     5	
     6	The executable engine uses SHA-256 over a domain-separated canonical group
     7	tuple. This independent model deliberately does not reproduce that
     8	cryptographic implementation. It models the properties the language and
     9	store protocols rely on: versioned domain separation, a 64-character
    10	lowercase-hex identity for every logical group (including the empty tuple),
    11	and adoption as one state transition that replaces every legacy physical
    12	identity while publishing the new version.
    13	-/
    14	
    15	namespace Quarry
    16	
    17	/-- The protocol domain whose change requires another store capability and
    18	migration. -/
    19	def maintainedIdDomainV1 : List Nat := cps "snapback4-maintained-id/sha256-v1"
    20	
    21	/-- A small independent digest abstraction. Its contents are intentionally
    22	not the engine's SHA-256; only its versioned input and fixed hex shape belong
    23	to this logical model. -/
    24	def maintainedIdV1 (key : Key) : List Nat :=
    25	  (List.range 64).map fun i =>
    26	    let nibble := (maintainedIdDomainV1.length + (encKey key).length + i) % 16
    27	    if nibble < 10 then 48 + nibble else 87 + nibble
    28	
    29	theorem maintainedIdV1_length (key : Key) : (maintainedIdV1 key).length = 64 := by
    30	  simp [maintainedIdV1]
    31	
    32	/-- The canonical tagged-id overhead is nine bytes and lowercase ASCII is one
    33	byte per character, so every maintained identity fits the 144-byte id bound. -/
    34	theorem maintainedIdV1_fits (key : Key) : 9 + (maintainedIdV1 key).length ≤ 144 := by
    35	  rw [maintainedIdV1_length]
    36	  omega
    37	
    38	def maintainedRowV1 (key : Key) (cols : List (String × Scalar)) : Row :=
    39	  { id := maintainedIdV1 key, cols }
    40	
    41	structure MaintainedState where
    42	  version : Nat
    43	  rows : List Row
    44	
    45	/-- Adoption rebuilds all reconstructible aggregate rows and publishes the
    46	identity version in the same pure state result. `old` is an input so the model
    47	states explicitly that legacy physical ids are never retained. -/
    48	def adoptMaintainedV1 (_old : MaintainedState)
    49	    (groups : List (Key × List (String × Scalar))) : MaintainedState :=
    50	  { version := 1, rows := groups.map fun group => maintainedRowV1 group.1 group.2 }
    51	
    52	theorem adoptMaintainedV1_version (old : MaintainedState) (groups) :
    53	    (adoptMaintainedV1 old groups).version = 1 := rfl
    54	
    55	theorem adoptMaintainedV1_ids (old : MaintainedState) (groups) :
    56	    (adoptMaintainedV1 old groups).rows.map Row.id = groups.map fun group => maintainedIdV1 group.1 := by
    57	  simp [adoptMaintainedV1, maintainedRowV1]
    58	
    59	theorem adoptMaintainedV1_values (old : MaintainedState) (groups) :
    60	    (adoptMaintainedV1 old groups).rows.map Row.cols = groups.map Prod.snd := by
    61	  simp [adoptMaintainedV1, maintainedRowV1]
    62	
    63	example : (maintainedIdV1 []).length = 64 := maintainedIdV1_length []
    64	example : (maintainedIdV1 [.id (List.replicate 64 97), .text (List.replicate 64 120)]).length = 64 :=
    65	  maintainedIdV1_length _
    66	
    67	end Quarry

   469	## 7. Formal and generated semantics
   470	
   471	The Lean table schema carries optional lower and upper lifetime fields. Its
   472	`live` projection filters every logical row lookup, scan, probe and write result
   473	at the case clock. Physical write-target lookup can still resolve an unopened,
   474	unexpired row, but an expired target is `NOT_FOUND`; an ordinary insert or
   475	upsert evaluates insert authority against the pre-retirement logical store,
   476	retires an expired same-id predecessor with its referential actions, then checks
   477	the new image's remaining unique keys against live occupants. `insert if absent`
   478	preflights all of those live unique-key collisions before same-id retirement; a
   479	collision is a no-op and preserves the expired predecessor and its children.
   480	The emitter includes both lifetime fields and independently selects the first
   481	eligible plain expiry index from the checked physical index catalog. This
   482	qualifies sweep execution for the selected physical plan; it does not
   483	independently re-prove the compiler's index synthesis. The model's explicit physical sweep
   484	uses the same cascade/restrict/set-null closure as delete, retains a restricted
   485	root and continues to later due rows. It eagerly rematerializes the declared
   486	table snapshot after each retirement; this is extensionally the same sequential
   487	store update while avoiding an exponential functional-update expression tree.
   488	The formal sweep carries the same in-engine, across-call continuation as the server: the
   489	last visited table rotates the next call even after a complete scan, and a
   490	call stopped at its visited-row bound retains each table's last
   491	`(selected index components,id)` key until the following call scans its tail
   492	and wrapped head.
   493	The Lean difftest generator preserves
   494	seeded expiry values and requested prelude/final sweeps, advances the formal
   495	store with each engine sweep, then compares the following program outcome.
   496	
   497	The difftest AST and generator produce null/past/future/equal-boundary openings,
   498	opening plus expiry, membership witnesses and caps. Its first formal fragment
   499	has no prelude or separately seeded clock: rows are seeded and evaluated under

   501	clock-plus-one. That fragment proves the pure `live(now)` projection without
   502	claiming to model the durable pending ledger or its bounded publication loop.
   503	Native runtime, simulator and both device-store lifecycle suites cover
   504	lower/upper composition, publication, rescheduling, restart, hostile device

   132	### 3.0 Aggregate target identity and migration
   133	
   134	Every ordinary maintained aggregate row has one internal identity function:
   135	64 lowercase hexadecimal characters from SHA-256 over the domain
   136	`snapback4-maintained-id/sha256-v1` and the typed canonical group-key vector.
   137	The checker therefore admits the largest legal group key against a fixed-size
   138	identity, and synthetic check rows, incremental writes, point reads and
   139	adoption rebuilds all call the same function. The group key remains the public
   140	address; programs do not read or supply this internal id.
   141	
   142	The intrinsic `byId` order of aggregate rows is consequently opaque digest
   143	order. It is stable for one identity version but has no relationship to the
   144	lexical or numeric order of group fields, and migration may change it. A query
   145	whose result needs group-key order declares that order explicitly (for example,
   146	`first 50 by .emoji`) rather than relying on an unqualified aggregate scan.
   147	
   148	The SQLite metadata and evaluation-PostgreSQL backend marker
   149	`maintained_id_version = sha256-v1` bind persisted aggregate targets to that
   150	function. Opening or adopting either store without the marker — including a
   151	0.4.28 store whose ids were the unbounded canonical JSON of the group key —
   152	atomically clears and rebuilds every ordinary aggregate target from its source
   153	rows, writes the marker, and publishes a new semantic generation. A failure
   154	rolls back old rows, rebuilt rows, marker and generation together. Adoption
   155	advice counts the SQLite rebuild even when schema/program bytes are unchanged;
   156	the evaluation adapter performs the corresponding rebuild under its opening
   157	writer/head fence. Before clearing targets, adoption derives each target's
   158	legacy-id-to-digest map to a fixed point over typed reference dependencies,
   159	then rewrites every surviving typed reference through those maps. Thus an
   160	aggregate grouped by a reference to another aggregate uses that referenced
   161	aggregate's new digest when deriving its own digest, and a table that refers
   162	to either rebuilt target does not dangle. A legacy id with no matching stored
   163	target stays opaque, preserving the existing dangling-reference contract.
   164	Reference rewrites, index updates, target rebuilds, marker and generation share
   165	the same transaction. The fixed-point bound counts stored aggregate identities,
   166	not aggregate declarations, because one target can hold a legal acyclic chain
   167	of references to other rows in that same target. SQLite captures newly recorded
   168	path values while predecessor targets still exist, then derives and applies all
   169	legacy maps before any recorded-path rebuild can remove those targets. Schemas
   170	with ordinary maintains require device capability
   171	`maintained-id-sha256-v1`; an older device is refused at the handshake before
   172	it can compute a legacy id and silently read a digest-addressed aggregate as
   173	zero. Conversely, a current device refuses to execute backend bytes from an
   174	old server that omit this capability. The shared codec records the omission so
   175	the server can adopt and republish a persisted schema; a device may decode the
   176	same bytes only as an inactive kept predecessor that it atomically replaces
   177	with a current backend, preserving queued writes. Offline reuse and adoption
   178	of the old backend refuse before interpretation.

   212	   identities; no image outlives its page.
   213	4. **Restrict.** For every row `s` in `S` and every `restrict` reference

   215	   itself in `S`**: the probe streams past the rows of `S` that name `s` —
   216	   `p` included, which may name itself — to the first live row outside `S`

   224	   `E_REFERENCED: projects at <site> is still referenced through comments.task (on delete restrict); delete or retarget those rows first, or declare the reference's action (guide writes)`

   227	   transaction counts; one deleted earlier in it does not. Because rows in

   260	
   261	Every step is inside the mutation's transaction: a refusal anywhere (a
   262	`restrict`, a read-through child, the meter) aborts the whole mutation, and
   263	nothing commits.
   264	
   265	An ordinary authored delete derives its closure and action witnesses from the
   266	logical unexpired store, then applies the resulting actions to the physical
   267	store. An expired child therefore neither blocks a `restrict` nor receives a
   268	`cascade` or `set null` action merely because cleanup has not removed its
   269	image yet.
   270	
   271	**Expiry is a referential-action trigger.** A parent whose `expire at` passes
   272	is logically absent at that instant, independent of whether physical cleanup
   273	can retire it. Every path that physically retires an expired image — scheduled
   274	sweep, an already-expired birth at commit, and same-id replacement of an
   275	expired predecessor — applies steps 3–6 above in the same transaction. It
   276	bypasses only the expired root's authored read/delete authorization; it does
   277	not bypass `cascade`, `set null`, `restrict`, read-through retention,
   278	constraints, maintains or partition events on affected rows.
   279	
   280	For an insert or upsert that reuses an expired predecessor's id, insert
   281	authority is evaluated against the pre-retirement logical store. The engine
   282	then retires the predecessor through the action path before the remaining
   283	uniqueness checks and physical insertion. At mutation commit, every row born
   284	or updated into an expired final image is retired through that same path. A
   285	refusal in any of these retirements aborts the whole mutation, including
   286	earlier cascade and set-null writes.
   287	
   288	This commit-end rule also covers a source of a row-keyed maintained view. The
   289	source's final image first reaches normal maintenance, then its expired image
   290	is retired through the common action path in the same transaction. No derived
   291	maintenance shortcut may physically remove that source before closure
   292	preflight: doing so would bypass a live `restrict` child and could orphan a
   293	`cascade` or `set null` child. The source contribution and its retirement
   294	cancel within the transaction, so an already-expired birth never enters a
   295	committed count basis. The execution retains at most one retirement key per
   296	changed source row; its allocation is charged when first retained and the
   297	program's existing rows-written ceiling bounds the commit-end walk.
   298	
   299	Seed commits preserve ordinary expired fixture images for the later sweep,
   300	but sources of row-keyed views keep the established count-basis exception.
   301	After normal maintenance, the seed filters its commit-end expiry tracker to
   302	those sources and retires them through this same common action path. The
   303	retirement uses the engine-owned, unbounded meter after the authored seed
   304	work has been charged; applies `restrict`, `cascade`, and `set null`; and
   305	defers the resulting maintained deltas until the retirement pass completes.
   306	This prevents a born-expired source from reviving under a later clock
   307	rollback without broadening retirement to unrelated fixture or raw-load
   308	rows. The SQLite and evaluation Postgres seed adapters share this ordering;
   309	the wasm interpreter has no server seed API or physical expiry-retirement
   310	path.
   311	
   312	A live `restrict` child, or a physically retained read-through child outside
   313	the cascade closure but below a row in it, keeps the expired root physically
   314	stored and the sweep continues to later due keys. A read-through child inside
   315	the closure is removed first and is not a blocker. The action walk preflights
   316	both kinds of blocker before its first set-null or cascade write. The retained
   317	root remains logically unreadable.
   318	Short sweeps preserve both a per-table row continuation and a rotating table
   319	continuation. Repeated bounded calls therefore cannot restart forever at the
   320	same restricted or read-through-retained roots, and a blocked earlier table
   321	cannot starve due rows in a later table. After reaching a table's end its row
   322	cursor wraps for roots whose blockers were removed.
   323	Expired children are not live restrict witnesses, as in step 4. A read-through
   324	child remains the stricter physical exception because its stored image depends
   325	on its parent. Other errors after an earlier cascade or set-null write roll
   400	    bypasses caller rules, and another parent's cascade may still reach the
   401	    same child. Proving otherwise would require a whole-schema deleting-path
   402	    proof and a fixed maintenance bound; until both exist, the refusal is the
   403	    sound result. "Feeds" needs no
   404	    transitive closure: a maintain's source is an application table and its
   405	    target is engine-owned, so maintains never chain;
   406	  - *partition events* reach only devices that hold the affected rows, as
   407	    every event does: a device receives a `del` or `put` only for a row
   408	    already in its partitions.
   409	- **Timing is out of scope**, as it is for the whole engine (the meter counts
   410	  work, never time): a larger cascade takes longer.
   411	
   412	`check` states the restrict bit in `why E_REFERENCED` and the writes card. A
   413	schema that must not disclose it declares `cascade`, `set null` or `keep`,
   414	or makes the child readable through its parent.
   415	
   416	### 4.3 Who can pin a parent
   417	
   418	Under `restrict`, anyone whose insert rule admits a child row naming `p` can
   419	block `p`'s delete: a stranger's bookmark of a public post pins the post.
   420	That is the price of the default, stated plainly:
   421	
   422	- `check`'s note at each parent delete site names every undeclared reference
   423	  that can now refuse it (§7), so the author decides per relation;
   424	- the writes card's rule of thumb: **a reference that other principals create
   425	  to your rows (likes, bookmarks, follows, RSVPs) is `cascade`**; a
   426	  reference that is part of the row's meaning to its own author (an
   427	  invoice's customer) is `restrict`; history that must outlive its subject
   428	  (an audit entry, a recorded contribution) is `keep`; an optional filing
   429	  pointer is `set null`.
   430	
   431	### 4.4 Dangling references stay legal
   432	
   433	Because writes do not check existence (§1), a row can still name an id that
   434	does not exist; and a parent created later with that id (an id supplied by a
   435	program argument) acquires those rows as its children: under `cascade` its
   436	delete then deletes them, under `restrict` they pin it. That is a destructive
   437	consequence of declaring `cascade` together with caller-chosen ids, not an
   438	undeclared authority, and the writes card says so: **a cascading parent
   439	should be inserted with a minted id, and a child whose rows must name a live
   440	parent writes `insert <- … and exists parents[.parent]`** (or uses `read
   441	through`, which checks it). Such a guard reads the reference, so a reference
   442	it guards cannot also be `set null` (§2.2): it chooses `cascade`, `restrict`
   443	or `keep`.
   444	
   445	## 5. Bounds
   446	
   447	### 5.1 The reservation
   448	
   449	For each writing reference, define `b(C, col)`, its **effective bound**,
   450	piecewise: the exact `cap N by col` when that is the only proof; one when a
   451	plain unique index whose complete column list is exactly `[col]` is the only
   452	proof; the smaller of `N` and one when both proofs exist; and undefined when
   453	neither exists. This definition is identical on every host. For an optional
   454	unique reference, `b = 1` applies to each non-null parent id and says nothing
   455	about the null group.
   456	
   457	The reservation is built from **closure bounds**: `N(P) = 1` for the root's
   458	table, and for each `cascade` edge `C.col → T` reachable from it,
   459	`N(C) += b(C, col) × N(T)` (the cascade graph is acyclic and every edge is

   465	`unit(C)`, the fixed price of one engine write of a `C` row, is

   467	| meter | `unit(C)` |
   468	|---|---|
   469	| steps | `4 + 2e(C)` plus the exported plan's steps |
   470	| index entries | `2e(C)` plus the plan's index entries |
   471	| examined | `1` plus the plan's examined |
   472	| rows written | `1` plus the plan's rows written |
   473	| rule probes, output | the plan's |
   474	| heap | `4 ×` the row's copy ceiling plus every plan phase's heap (a write holds its phases' reservations together until it ends) |

   478	scratch and one `C` row for device verification. These overlap source-write

    91	        )?.first() {

   114	            return Err(RuntimeError::Store("not this Postgres evaluation store version".into()));

+#[test]
+fn legacy_semantic_backend_is_server_adoptable_but_device_refused() {
+    for (capability, source) in [
+        ("maintained-id-sha256-v1", "table entries:\n  group: text <=64\n  public\nview totals: count entries by .group\n  public\n"),
+        ("expiry-reference-actions-v1", "table parents:\n  until: time ?\n  expire at .until\n  public\ntable children:\n  parent: parents on delete cascade\n  cap 1 by parent\n  public\n"),
+    ] {
+        let bound = snapback4_lang::compile(&[("schema.q".into(), source.into())]);
+        assert!(bound.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:#?}", bound.diagnostics);
+        let backend = Backend { generation: 1, schema: bound.schema, programs: bound.programs.into_iter().map(|program| program.program).collect() };
+        let mut legacy = serde_json::to_value(&backend).unwrap();
+        for table in legacy["schema"]["tables"].as_object_mut().unwrap().values_mut() {
+            for constraint in table["constraints"].as_array_mut().unwrap() {
+                if let Some(names) = constraint.get_mut("Capabilities").and_then(|value| value.as_array_mut()) {
+                    names.retain(|value| value != capability);
+                }
+            }
+        }
+        let adopted: Schema = serde_json::from_value(legacy["schema"].clone()).unwrap();
+        assert!(adopted.legacy_semantic_capabilities.contains(capability));
+        assert!(serde_json::to_string(&adopted).unwrap().contains(capability));
+        let opening = Opening::parse(Some(&legacy.to_string())).expect("legacy bytes remain decodable for store migration");
+        let error = match opening.open(MemoryStore::new()) {
+            Err(error) => error,
+            Ok(_) => panic!("device executed backend missing {capability}"),
+        };
+        assert_eq!(error.code(), "E_SCHEMA_CAPABILITY");
+        assert!(error.to_string().contains(capability), "{error}");
+    }
+}

+fn legacy_digest_store<S: DeviceStore>(store: &mut S) -> Backend {
+    let source = "table entries:\n  group: text <=64\n  public\nview totals: count entries by .group\n  public\n";
+    let bound = snapback4_lang::compile(&[("schema.q".into(), source.into())]);
+    assert!(bound.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:#?}", bound.diagnostics);
+    let mut current = Backend { generation: 2, schema: bound.schema, programs: bound.programs.into_iter().map(|program| program.program).collect() };
+    let mut legacy = serde_json::to_value(&current).unwrap();
+    legacy["generation"] = json!(1);
+    for table in legacy["schema"]["tables"].as_object_mut().unwrap().values_mut() {
+        for constraint in table["constraints"].as_array_mut().unwrap() {
+            if let Some(names) = constraint.get_mut("Capabilities").and_then(|value| value.as_array_mut()) {
+                names.retain(|value| value != "maintained-id-sha256-v1");
+            }
+        }
+    }
+    let old: Backend = serde_json::from_value(legacy.clone()).unwrap();
+    store.install(&old.schema, &BTreeMap::from([
+        ("device:backend".into(), legacy.to_string()),
+        ("device:generation".into(), "1".into()),
+    ]), false).unwrap();
+    let tx = store.transaction().unwrap();
+    tx.outbox_insert(1, "pending", r#"{"id":"pending","seq":1,"op":"write","args":{},"new_ids":[]}"#).unwrap();
+    tx.commit().unwrap();
+    current.generation = 2;
+    current
+}
+
+fn legacy_digest_recovery<S: DeviceStore>(store: &mut S, initial: bool) {
+    let current = legacy_digest_store(store);
+    let error = match Opening::Kept.open(Borrowed(store)) {
+        Err(error) => error,
+        Ok(_) => panic!("offline device executed a kept pre-digest backend"),
+    };
+    assert_eq!(error.code(), "E_SCHEMA_CAPABILITY");
+    let tx = store.transaction().unwrap();
+    let before = tx.outbox_entries().unwrap();
+    tx.commit().unwrap();
+    let opening = if initial { Opening::Initial(current) } else { Opening::Install(current) };
+    drop(opening.open(Borrowed(store)).expect("a current backend must recover a kept legacy backend"));
+    let tx = store.transaction().unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(tx.outbox_entries().unwrap(), before, "semantic upgrade preserves queued writes");
+    assert_eq!(tx.meta("device:generation").unwrap().as_deref(), Some("2"));
+    tx.commit().unwrap();
+}

    13	pub(super) type Identity = (Option<String>, Option<String>, Option<String>, Option<String>,
    14	);

    16	pub(super) fn identity(conn: &Connection) -> Result<Identity, RuntimeError> {
    17	    let mut statement = conn.prepare_cached("SELECT value FROM _meta WHERE key = ?1")?;
    18	    let mut get = |key| statement.query_row([key], |row| row.get(0)).optional();
    19	    Ok((get("schema_hash")?, get("activation_hash")?, get("generation")?, get("device:generation")?,
    20	    ))
    21	}

    23	impl Store {
    24	    /// Install a device's schema. Server engines also supply their programs
    25	    /// and derived-state builder through `activate` below.
    26	    pub fn install(&mut self, schema: &Schema) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    27	        self.activate(schema, None, false, |_, _| Ok(())).map(|_| ())
    28	    }
    29	
    30	    /// A device can discard an obsolete partition while atomically caching
    31	    /// its replacement backend and reset watermark. It never migrates rows
    32	    /// whose authority belongs to a previous server generation.
    33	    pub fn install_device(&mut self, schema: &Schema, metadata: &BTreeMap<String, String>, reset: bool) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    34	        self.install_device_checked(schema, metadata, reset, &BTreeMap::new())
    35	    }
    36	
    37	    pub fn install_device_checked(&mut self, schema: &Schema, metadata: &BTreeMap<String, String>, reset: bool, expected: &BTreeMap<String, Option<String>>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    38	        self.install_device_checked_with(schema, metadata, reset, expected, |_| Ok(()))
    39	    }
    40	
    41	    /// Device-owned sidecar changes share the schema installation transaction.
    42	    pub fn install_device_checked_with(&mut self, schema: &Schema, metadata: &BTreeMap<String, String>, reset: bool, expected: &BTreeMap<String, Option<String>>, prepare: impl FnOnce(&Tx<'_>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    43	        self.install_device_checked_with_finish(schema, metadata, reset, expected, prepare, |_| {
    44	            Ok(())
    45	        })
    46	    }
    47	
    48	    /// Opening recovery and its final reads must finish before installation commits.
    49	    pub fn install_device_checked_with_finish<R>(&mut self, schema: &Schema, metadata: &BTreeMap<String, String>, reset: bool, expected: &BTreeMap<String, Option<String>>, prepare: impl FnOnce(&Tx<'_>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError>, finish: impl FnOnce(&Tx<'_>) -> Result<R, RuntimeError>,
    50	    ) -> Result<R, RuntimeError> {
    51	        let mut result = None;
    52	        self.activate(schema, None, reset, |tx, _| {
    53	            for (key, value) in expected {
    54	                let held: Option<String> = tx.conn().query_row("SELECT value FROM _meta WHERE key = ?1", [key], |row| {
    55	                        row.get(0)
    56	                    }).optional()?;
    57	                if &held != value { return Err(RuntimeError::Generation("the backend adoption capture is obsolete; retry sync".into())); }
    58	            }
    59	            prepare(tx)?;
    60	            for (key, value) in metadata {
    61	                // A device metadata namespace reset shares backend installation's transaction.
    62	                if key.ends_with(':') {
    63	                    tx.conn().execute("DELETE FROM _meta WHERE key >= ?1 AND key < ?2", params![key, format!("{key}\u{10ffff}")])?;
    64	                } else { tx.set_meta(key, value)?; }
    65	            }
    66	            if reset { tx.conn().execute_batch("DELETE FROM _device_base; DELETE FROM _device_snapshot;")?; }
    67	            result = Some(finish(tx)?);
    68	            Ok(())
    69	        })?;
    70	        Ok(result.expect("activation ran opening recovery"))
    71	    }

    73	    pub(crate) fn activate(&mut self, schema: &Schema, programs: Option<&BTreeMap<String, Program>>, reset: bool, build: impl FnOnce(&Tx<'_>, bool) -> Result<(), RuntimeError>) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
    74	        self.activate_at(schema, programs, reset, crate::now_ms(), |tx, changed, _| build(tx, changed))
    75	    }
    76	
    77	    pub(crate) fn activate_at(&mut self, schema: &Schema, programs: Option<&BTreeMap<String, Program>>, reset: bool, now: i64, build: impl FnOnce(&Tx<'_>, bool, &mut super::adoption_report::AdoptionReport) -> Result<(), RuntimeError>) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
    78	        // One-shot device preparation is never retried or given a larger cache.
    79	        self.activate_transaction(schema, programs, reset, now, true, build)
    80	    }
    81	
    82	    pub(crate) fn activate_at_with_launch<R>(&mut self, schema: &Schema, programs: Option<&BTreeMap<String, Program>>, reset: bool, now: i64, allow_launch: bool, check: impl Fn(&Connection) -> Result<(), RuntimeError>, mut build: impl FnMut(&Tx<'_>, bool, &mut super::adoption_report::AdoptionReport) -> Result<(), RuntimeError>, finish: impl Fn(&Tx<'_>) -> Result<R, RuntimeError>,
    83	    ) -> Result<(u64, R), RuntimeError> {
    84	        let budget = if programs.is_some() { super::activation_cache::configured_mib()? } else { 0 };
    85	        // The server builder owns only transaction-local work. Recreate all of
    86	        // it on retry, with the same schema/programs/activation time.
    87	        self.with_activation_cache(budget, |store| {
    88	            store.activate_transaction_with(schema, programs, reset, now, allow_launch, &check, &mut build, &finish)
    89	        })
    90	    }
    91	
    92	    pub(super) fn activate_transaction(&mut self, schema: &Schema, programs: Option<&BTreeMap<String, Program>>, reset: bool, now: i64, allow_launch: bool, build: impl FnOnce(&Tx<'_>, bool, &mut super::adoption_report::AdoptionReport) -> Result<(), RuntimeError>) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
    93	        self.activate_transaction_with(schema, programs, reset, now, allow_launch, |_| Ok(()), build, |_| Ok(())).map(|(generation, ())| generation)
    94	    }

   595	    /// The backend changed (a new generation from `/schema`): adopt it and
   596	    /// keep it. A changed generation replaces base images and requests a fresh snapshot.
   597	    pub fn adopt(&mut self, backend: Backend) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   598	        self.adopt_captured(backend, BTreeMap::new())
   599	    }
   600	
   601	    pub fn adopt_captured(&mut self, mut backend: Backend, mut expected: BTreeMap<String, Option<String>>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   602	        check_version(&backend.schema)?;
   603	        backend.require_current_semantics()?;
   604	        backend.schema.check_row_view_audiences()?;
   605	        #[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]
   606	        {
   607	            if let Some(issue) = snapback4_core::schema::columns::validate(&backend.schema).into_iter().find(|i| i.message.contains("E_VIEW_KEY")) {
   608	                return Err(RuntimeError::Structural { code: "E_VIEW_KEY", message: issue.message });
   609	            }
   610	            for program in &backend.programs { snapback4_core::engine::admission::check_state_predicates(&backend.schema, program)?; }
   611	        }
   612	        backend.schema.prepare_contribution_indexes();
   613	        let required = self.store.meta(BACKEND_REQUIRED)?;
   614	        expected.entry(BACKEND_REQUIRED.into()).or_insert(required.clone());
   615	        expected.entry(STORE_ID.into()).or_insert(self.store.meta(STORE_ID)?);
   616	        expected.entry(SEND_REVISION.into()).or_insert(self.store.meta(SEND_REVISION)?);
   617	        let adopted_store = expected.get(STORE_ID).cloned().flatten();
   618	        let cached_native = self.store.meta(NATIVE_DIGEST)?;
   619	        expected.entry(NATIVE_DIGEST.into()).or_insert(cached_native.clone());
   620	        let obsolete_native = adopted_store != self.store_identity || cached_native.filter(|s| !s.is_empty()).as_deref() != self.native_digest.as_deref();
   621	        let replacement = required.as_ref().is_some_and(|value| !value.is_empty());
   622	        let reset = backend.generation != self.generation;
   623	        // @ref LLP 3000.000.000#91-per-row-narrowed-value-dormancy — schema shape alone cannot certify the release's active population.
   624	        let keep_images = false;
   625	        // @ref LLP 3000.000.000#91-per-row-narrowed-value-dormancy — a release can hide restored data even when its added columns have literal defaults.
   626	        let keep_acquired = false;
   627	        let backend_identity = store_identity::backend_identity(&backend);
   628	        let mut metadata = BTreeMap::from([(BACKEND.to_owned(), encoded(&backend)?), (GENERATION.to_owned(), backend.generation.to_string()), (BACKEND_IDENTITY.to_owned(), backend_identity.clone())]);
   629	        metadata.insert(BACKEND_REQUIRED.to_owned(), String::new());
   630	        if reset {
   631	            metadata.insert(WATERMARK.to_owned(), "0".into());
   632	            metadata.insert(ACQUIRED.to_owned(), if keep_acquired { backend.generation.to_string() } else { String::new() });
   633	            invalidate_native(&mut metadata);
   634	            metadata.insert(history::GROUPS.to_owned(), "{}".into());
   635	            metadata.insert(history::STAGED_GROUPS.to_owned(), "{}".into());
   636	            metadata.insert(boundary::STAGED.to_owned(), "{}".into());
   637	            if !keep_acquired { metadata.insert(boundary::BOUNDARIES.to_owned(), "{}".into()); }
   638	        }
   639	        if replacement { invalidate_native(&mut metadata); }
   640	        self.store.install_checked(&backend.schema, &metadata, reset && !keep_images, &expected)?;
   641	        if reset || replacement || obsolete_native {
   642	            #[cfg(feature = "wasm-host")]
   643	            {
   644	                self.native = None;
   645	            }
   646	            self.native_digest = None;
   647	        }
   648	        self.schema = backend.schema;
   649	        self.programs = snapback4_core::small_map::collect(backend.programs.into_iter().map(|p| (p.name.clone(), p)));
   650	        self.generation = backend.generation;
   651	        self.backend_identity = backend_identity;
   652	        self.store_identity = adopted_store;
   653	        self.snapshot_owner = None;
   654	        Ok(())
   655	    }
   656	
   657	    /// The watermark the device has applied through, and its generation.
   658	    pub fn state(&self) -> Result<(u64, u64), RuntimeError> {
   659	        Ok((self.store.meta(WATERMARK)?.and_then(|v| v.parse().ok()).unwrap_or(0), self.generation))
   660	    }
   661	
   662	    /// Persist before starting a POST, so another owner of the store
   663	    /// cannot apply an older sync response that omitted the write being sent.
   664	    pub fn begin_send(&mut self) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
   665	        self.begin_send_for(None)
   666	    }
   667	
   668	    pub fn begin_send_for(&mut self, id: Option<&str>) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
   669	        let tx = self.store.transaction()?;
   670	        store_identity::require_healthy(&tx)?;
   671	        if id.is_none(){for data in tx.outbox_entries()?{upload::require_ready(&decoded::<Queued>(&data)?)?;}}
   672	        if let Some(id) = id {
   673	            if let Some(data) = tx.outbox_get(id)? {
   674	                let entry: Queued = decoded(&data)?;
   675	                upload::require_ready(&entry)?;
   676	                if entry.upload.as_ref().is_some_and(|u| u.get("store_id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) != tx.meta(STORE_ID).ok().flatten().as_deref()) {
   677	                    return Err(RuntimeError::Structural {code:"E_STORE_REPLACED",message:"upload belongs to another backend store".into()});
   678	                }
   679	            }
   680	            predictions::dispatch(&tx, id, "")?;

codex
The capability checks distinguish legacy schemas that a server can migrate from backends a device may execute. The migration code also derives reference maps before clearing aggregate targets. I’m checking the remaining edge cases in that ordering and in the formal sweep model.

+  public

+        e
+    };
+    let context = || Context::new("dev:alice", BTreeMap::from([("id".into(), id("p"))])).at(100);
+    let mut complete = world();
+    let sent = complete.mutate("drop", None, context()).unwrap();
+    assert!(matches!(sent.state, WriteState::Sent { .. }), "{:?}", sent.state);
+
+    let mut cut = world();
+    let mut ceilings = cut.ceilings();
+    ceilings.examined = sent.metered.examined - 1;
+    cut.set_ceilings(ceilings);
+    let refused = cut.mutate("drop", None, context()).unwrap();
+    assert!(matches!(refused.state, WriteState::Failed { ref why, .. } if why.code == "E_BOUND"), "{:?}", refused.state);
+    assert_eq!(cut.store().rows("roots").unwrap().len(), 1);
+    assert_eq!(cut.store().rows("children").unwrap().len(), 1);
+    assert_eq!(cut.store().rows("grandchildren").unwrap().len(), 1);
+}

@@ -166,6 +209,38 @@ mutation replaceExpired():

+#[test]
+fn same_id_replacement_reloads_maintained_columns_after_cascade_retirement() {
+    let source = r#"
+table roots:
+  expiresAt: time ?
+  by byExpiry: expiresAt
+  expire at .expiresAt
+  childCount: count children by root
+  public
+  insert <- allow
+table children:
+  root: roots on delete cascade
+  cap 4 by root
+  public
+mutation replace():
+  insert roots {id: 'same', expiresAt: null}
+"#;
+    let mut e = engine(source);
+    e.seed_at([
+        ("roots".into(), object([("id", id("same")), ("expiresAt", Value::Int(10))])),
+        ("children".into(), object([("id", id("child")), ("root", id("same"))])),
+    ], 0).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("roots").unwrap()[0].field("childCount").unwrap(), &Value::Int(1));
+
+    let replaced = e.mutate("replace", None, Context::new("dev:alice", BTreeMap::new()).at(100)).unwrap();
+    assert!(matches!(replaced.state, WriteState::Sent { .. }), "{:?}", replaced.state);
+    let roots = e.store().rows("roots").unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(roots.len(), 1);
+    assert_eq!(roots[0].field("childCount").unwrap(), &Value::Int(0));
+    assert!(e.store().rows("children").unwrap().is_empty());
+}

@@ -148,7 +148,15 @@ rows, writes the marker, and publishes a new semantic generation. A failure
 rolls back old rows, rebuilt rows, marker and generation together. Adoption
 advice counts the SQLite rebuild even when schema/program bytes are unchanged;
 the evaluation adapter performs the corresponding rebuild under its opening
-writer/head fence. Schemas with ordinary maintains require device capability
+writer/head fence. Before clearing targets, adoption derives each target's
+legacy-id-to-digest map to a fixed point over typed reference dependencies,
+then rewrites every surviving typed reference through those maps. Thus an
+aggregate grouped by a reference to another aggregate uses that referenced
+aggregate's new digest when deriving its own digest, and a table that refers
+to either rebuilt target does not dangle. A legacy id with no matching stored
+target stays opaque, preserving the existing dangling-reference contract.
+Reference rewrites, index updates, target rebuilds, marker and generation share
+the same transaction. Schemas with ordinary maintains require device capability
 `maintained-id-sha256-v1`; an older device is refused at the handshake before
 it can compute a legacy id and silently read a digest-addressed aggregate as
 zero.

+An ordinary authored delete derives its closure and action witnesses from the
+logical unexpired store, then applies the resulting actions to the physical
+store. An expired child therefore neither blocks a `restrict` nor receives a
+`cascade` or `set null` action merely because cleanup has not removed its
+image yet.
+
 **Expiry is a referential-action trigger.** A parent whose `expire at` passes
 is logically absent at that instant, independent of whether physical cleanup
 can retire it. Every path that physically retires an expired image — scheduled
@@ -271,6 +277,14 @@ bypasses only the expired root's authored read/delete authorization; it does
 not bypass `cascade`, `set null`, `restrict`, read-through retention,
 constraints, maintains or partition events on affected rows.
 
+For an insert or upsert that reuses an expired predecessor's id, insert
+authority is evaluated against the pre-retirement logical store. The engine
+then retires the predecessor through the action path before the remaining
+uniqueness checks and physical insertion. At mutation commit, every row born
+or updated into an expired final image is retired through that same path. A
+refusal in any of these retirements aborts the whole mutation, including
+earlier cascade and set-null writes.
+

+#[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
+fn has_legacy_maintained_reference(
+    kind: &crate::schema::ColumnType,
+    ids: &BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>>,
+) -> bool {
+    match kind {
+        crate::schema::ColumnType::Ref { table } => ids.get(table).is_some_and(|ids| !ids.is_empty()),
+        crate::schema::ColumnType::Optional(inner)
+        | crate::schema::ColumnType::List { of: inner, .. }
+        | crate::schema::ColumnType::ListRange { of: inner, .. } => has_legacy_maintained_reference(inner, ids),
+        _ => false,
+    }

+
+#[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
+fn rewrite_legacy_maintained_reference(
+    kind: &crate::schema::ColumnType,
+    value: &mut Value,
+    ids: &BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>>,
+) -> bool {
+    match (kind, value) {
+        (crate::schema::ColumnType::Ref { table }, Value::Id(id)) => {
+            let Some(next) = ids.get(table).and_then(|ids| ids.get(id)) else { return false };
+            *id = next.clone();
+            true
+        }
+        (crate::schema::ColumnType::Optional(inner), value) => rewrite_legacy_maintained_reference(inner, value, ids),
+        (crate::schema::ColumnType::List { of, .. } | crate::schema::ColumnType::ListRange { of, .. }, Value::Array(values)) =>
+            values.iter_mut().fold(false, |changed, value| rewrite_legacy_maintained_reference(of, value, ids) || changed),
+        _ => false,
+    }
+}

+#[test]
+fn expiry_reference_actions_upgrade_legacy_wire_and_fence_old_devices() {
+    let source = "table parents:\n  until: time ?\n  expire at .until\n  public\ntable children:\n  parent: parents on delete cascade\n  cap 1 by parent\n  public\n";
+    let schema = compile(source);
+    assert!(schema.required_capabilities().contains("reference-actions"));
+    assert!(schema.required_capabilities().contains("expiry-reference-actions-v1"));
+
+    let reference_only = compile(&source.replace("  until: time ?\n  expire at .until\n", ""));
+    assert!(reference_only.required_capabilities().contains("reference-actions"));
+    assert!(!reference_only.required_capabilities().contains("expiry-reference-actions-v1"));
+    let expiry_only = compile("table parents:\n  until: time ?\n  expire at .until\n  public\n");
+    assert!(!expiry_only.required_capabilities().contains("expiry-reference-actions-v1"));
+
+    // A kept pre-Wave-12 schema decodes for server adoption, then its next
+    // projection stamps the new device requirement.
+    let mut legacy = serde_json::to_value(&schema).unwrap();
+    for table in legacy["tables"].as_object_mut().unwrap().values_mut() {
+        for constraint in table["constraints"].as_array_mut().unwrap() {
+            if let Some(names) = constraint.get_mut("Capabilities").and_then(|value| value.as_array_mut()) {
+                names.retain(|value| value != "expiry-reference-actions-v1");
+            }
+        }
+    }
+    let upgraded: Schema = serde_json::from_value(legacy).unwrap();
+    assert!(serde_json::to_string(&upgraded).unwrap().contains("expiry-reference-actions-v1"));
+
+    let required = snapback4_core::device_protocol::compatibility(&upgraded.public_projection());
+    let mut old = snapback4_core::device_protocol::DeviceEngine::current();
+    old.version = "0.4.28".into();
+    old.capabilities.retain(|capability| capability != "expiry-reference-actions-v1");
+    let refusal = snapback4_core::device_protocol::check(Some(&old), &required).unwrap_err();
+    assert_eq!(refusal.code, "E_DEVICE_VERSION");
+    assert!(refusal.message.contains("expiry-reference-actions-v1"), "{refusal:?}");
+}

+    assert_eq!(write(&mut e, "replace", "bob", &[("id", id("p"))]), "ok");
+    d.apply(&stream_page(&mut e, "bob", from), false).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(d.store().raw_rows("parents").len(), 1);
+    assert!(d.store().raw_rows("children").is_empty());
+    host.close("expiry-same-id-replacement", d);

     // An expiring row-keyed-view source follows the same server action path;

+#[test]
+fn same_id_replacement_rechecks_an_unchanged_secondary_unique_key() {
+    let source = r#"
+table records:
+  expiresAt: time ?
+  name: text <=20
+  unique name
+  expire at .expiresAt
+  read <- allow
+  insert <- allow
+mutation add(id: id, name: text <=20, expiresAt: time ?):
+  insert records { id, name, expiresAt }
+"#;
+    let mut e = engine(source);
+    e.seed_at([row("records", &[
+        ("id", id("p")),
+        ("name", Value::String("taken".into())),
+        ("expiresAt", Value::Int(900)),
+    ])], 500).unwrap();
+
+    let live = e.mutate("add", None, ctx("alice", &[
+        ("id", id("q")),
+        ("name", Value::String("taken".into())),
+        ("expiresAt", Value::Null),
+    ])).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(refusal(&live), None, "an expired image releases its key: {live:?}");
+
+    let replace = e.mutate("add", None, ctx("alice", &[
+        ("id", id("p")),
+        ("name", Value::String("taken".into())),
+        ("expiresAt", Value::Null),
+    ])).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(refusal(&replace).as_deref(), Some("E_UNIQUE"), "the replacement must see q's live key: {replace:?}");
+    let rows = e.store().rows("records").unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(rows.len(), 2, "the retirement rolls back with the refused replacement");
+    assert!(rows.iter().any(|r| r.field("id").is_ok_and(|v| *v == id("p"))
+        && r.field("expiresAt").is_ok_and(|v| *v == Value::Int(900))), "{rows:?}");
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn commit_end_expiry_precedes_final_exists_checks() {
+    let source = r#"
+table roots:
+  expiresAt: time ?
+  expire at .expiresAt
+  read <- allow
+  insert <- allow
+table children:
+  root: roots on delete cascade
+  cap 2 by root
+  read <- allow
+  insert <- allow
+table markers:
+  child: children on delete cascade
+  cap 2 by child
+  read <- allow
+  insert <- allow
+  after insert <- exists children[.child]
+mutation create(expiresAt: time):
+  insert roots { id: 'r', expiresAt }
+  insert children { id: 'c', root: 'r' }
+  insert markers { id: 'm', child: 'c' }
+"#;
+    let mut e = engine(source);
+    let out = e.mutate("create", None, ctx("alice", &[("expiresAt", Value::Int(900))])).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(refusal(&out).as_deref(), Some("E_CONSTRAINT"), "the cascade removes the final witness: {out:?}");
+    assert_eq!((count(&e, "roots"), count(&e, "children"), count(&e, "markers")), (0, 0, 0),
+        "the failed postcondition rolls back the whole mutation");
+}
+

+}

     1	//! The engine against the Lean model (LLP 3000.035 §5.2).
     2	//!
     3	//! **The model side.** Each case's surface program goes through
     4	//! `snapback4_lang::emit::lean` (the parsed tree, never the binder's IR) to
     5	//! the model's case JSON, and through `quarry-oracle` (`snapback4/lean`,
     6	//! `lake build`), one long-lived process per worker that answers one tagged
     7	//! outcome per line. A case the emitter cannot translate is `Unsupported`
     8	//! under the emitter's named reason, never a pass.
     9	//!
    10	//! **The engine side.** The engine over SQLite (the ordinary in-memory
    11	//! server store) at `Ceilings::default()`, the ceilings a production server
    12	//! runs, not the case's stored budget; the model runs unbounded (its meter is
    13	//! abstract, OPEN M1).
    14	//!
    15	//! **Compared fields** (README, "How the harness compares"):
    16	//!
    17	//! - `kind`: answer, unavailable, refused, committed;
    18	//! - `code`: the refusal code (sites are not modelled);
    19	//! - `data` / `result`: exact, both sides as tagged values, so an id never
    20	//!   compares equal to a text (OPEN V1); rows compare as field maps;
    21	//! - `complete`: exact;
    22	//! - `next`: presence only (OPEN C1). When both carry one, each side
    23	//!   continues from its own cursor and the next page is compared
    24	//!   (`continuation-*`), until both are exhausted;
    25	//! - a mutation then runs `observe` on each side's resulting store
    26	//!   (`post-*`): the engine's store, and the model's committed store (or the
    27	//!   original store after a refusal).
    28	//!
    29	//! Meter fields, cut sites, `tables` and `seq` are not compared. Expiry
    30	//! sweeps advance both stores before the following program is compared.
    31	//!
    32	//! **Signatures** are `lean--{field}--{engine}~{model}`, each side's stable
    33	//! class (a refusal code, `unavailable`, `committed`, or the data's shape).
    34	//! The finding's `left` is the engine's raw record, `right` the model's raw
    35	//! outcome; the canonical forms compared are its `continuation`.

    65	/// Bring this checkout's `quarry-oracle` up to date with its model sources
    66	/// (`lake build quarry-oracle`, under a second when current). A merge or
    67	/// checkout that changes `lean/` leaves the previous executable in `.lake`,
    68	/// and the harness would report that older model's choices as disagreements
    69	/// (2026-10-12: a stale pre-guard oracle on the merged `sb4-loop` tree showed

    71	/// `SNAPBACK4_LEAN_ORACLE` names the oracle (the caller vouches for it; a
    72	/// campaign's workers inherit the refreshed path that way) or when `lake` is
    73	/// not installed (a missing oracle still refuses at `LeanProcess::spawn`).
    74	pub fn refresh() -> Result<(), String> {
    75	    if std::env::var_os("SNAPBACK4_LEAN_ORACLE").is_some() {
    76	        return Ok(());
    77	    }
    78	    let dir = PathBuf::from(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("../../lean");

    81	    match Command::new("lake").arg("--version").current_dir(&dir).stdin(Stdio::null()).output() {
    82	        Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {
    83	            eprintln!("lake not found: using the Lean oracle as built at {}", oracle_path().display());

    90	    let cache = dir.join(".lake");
    91	    fs::create_dir_all(&cache).map_err(|e| format!("Lean refresh cache: {e}"))?;
    92	    let refresh_lock = OpenOptions::new().create(true).truncate(false).read(true).write(true)
    93	        .open(cache.join("snapback4-refresh.lock")).map_err(|e| format!("Lean refresh lock: {e}"))?;
    94	    refresh_lock.lock().map_err(|e| format!("Lean refresh lock: {e}"))?;
    95	    match Command::new("lake").args(["build", "quarry-oracle"]).current_dir(&dir).stdin(Stdio::null()).output() {
    96	        Ok(output) if output.status.success() => Ok(()),
    97	        Ok(output) => Err(format!(
    98	            "`lake build quarry-oracle` failed in {}: {}{}",
    99	            dir.display(),
   100	            String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout),
   101	            String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr)
   102	        )),
   103	        Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {
   104	            eprintln!("lake not found: using the Lean oracle as built at {}", oracle_path().display());
   105	            Ok(())
   106	        }
   107	        Err(e) => Err(format!("lake: {e}")),
   108	    }
   109	}
