   111	/// One `quarry-oracle` process: a JSON case per line in, an outcome per line out.
   112	pub struct LeanProcess {
   113	    child: Child,
   114	    stdin: ChildStdin,
   115	    stdout: BufReader<ChildStdout>,
   116	}
   117	impl LeanProcess {
   118	    pub fn spawn() -> Result<Self, String> {
   119	        let path = oracle_path();
   120	        if !path.is_file() {
   121	            return Err(format!(
   122	                "Lean oracle missing: {} (run `cd snapback4/lean && lake build`, or set SNAPBACK4_LEAN_ORACLE)",
   123	                path.display()
   124	            ));
   125	        }
   126	        let mut child = Command::new(&path)
   127	            .stdin(Stdio::piped())
   128	            .stdout(Stdio::piped())
   129	            .stderr(Stdio::inherit())
   130	            .spawn()
   131	            .map_err(|e| format!("Lean oracle {}: {e}", path.display()))?;
   132	        let stdin = child.stdin.take().unwrap();
   133	        let stdout = BufReader::new(child.stdout.take().unwrap());
   134	        Ok(Self { child, stdin, stdout })
   135	    }
   136	    pub fn ask(&mut self, case: &Json) -> Result<Json, String> {
   137	        writeln!(self.stdin, "{case}").map_err(|e| format!("Lean oracle write: {e}"))?;
   138	        self.stdin.flush().map_err(|e| format!("Lean oracle flush: {e}"))?;
   139	        let mut line = String::new();
   140	        let n = self.stdout.read_line(&mut line).map_err(|e| format!("Lean oracle read: {e}"))?;
   141	        if n == 0 {
   142	            return Err("Lean oracle exited".into());
   143	        }
   144	        let answer: Json = serde_json::from_str(&line).map_err(|e| format!("Lean oracle answer {line:?}: {e}"))?;
   145	        if answer["kind"] == "error" {
   146	            // A case the model cannot decode is an emitter defect, never a verdict.
   147	            return Err(format!("Lean oracle refused the case: {}", answer["error"]));
   148	        }
   149	        Ok(answer)
   150	    }
   151	}
   152	impl Drop for LeanProcess {
   153	    fn drop(&mut self) {
   154	        let _ = self.child.kill();
   155	        let _ = self.child.wait();
   156	    }
   157	}
   158	
   159	thread_local! {
   160	    static PROCESS: RefCell<Option<LeanProcess>> = const { RefCell::new(None) };
   161	}
   162	
   163	/// Ask this thread's oracle process, starting it on first use and once
   164	/// more if it has died.
   165	pub fn ask(case: &Json) -> Result<Json, String> {
   166	    PROCESS.with(|cell| {
   167	        let mut slot = cell.borrow_mut();
   168	        if slot.is_none() {
   169	            *slot = Some(LeanProcess::spawn()?);
   170	        }
   171	        match slot.as_mut().unwrap().ask(case) {
   172	            Err(e) if e == "Lean oracle exited" => {
   173	                *slot = Some(LeanProcess::spawn()?);
   174	                slot.as_mut().unwrap().ask(case)
   175	            }
   176	            other => other,
   177	        }
   178	    })
   179	}
   180	
   181	/// The engine's value as the model's tagged value; rows as field maps.
   182	pub fn engine_value(v: &snapback4_core::Value) -> Json {
   183	    use snapback4_core::Value as V;
   184	    match v {
   185	        V::Null => json!({"null": null}),
   186	        V::Bool(b) => json!({"bool": b}),
   187	        V::Int(n) => json!({"int": n.to_string()}),
   188	        V::String(s) => json!({"text": s}),
   189	        V::Id(s) => json!({"id": s}),
   190	        V::Bytes(b) => json!({"bytes": b.iter().map(|x| format!("{x:02x}")).collect::<String>()}),
   191	        V::Row(fs) | V::Map(fs) => json!({"row": fs.iter().map(|(k, x)| (k.clone(), engine_value(x))).collect::<Map<_, _>>()}),
   192	        V::Array(xs) => json!({"arr": xs.iter().map(engine_value).collect::<Vec<_>>()}),
   193	    }
   194	}
   195	
   196	/// The model's tagged value with rows as field maps (its rows are ordered pairs).
   197	pub fn model_value(v: &Json) -> Json {
   198	    if let Some(xs) = v.get("arr").and_then(Json::as_array) {
   199	        return json!({"arr": xs.iter().map(model_value).collect::<Vec<_>>()});
   200	    }
   201	    if let Some(fs) = v.get("row").and_then(Json::as_array) {
   202	        let mut m = Map::new();
   203	        for p in fs {
   204	            m.insert(p[0].as_str().unwrap_or_default().to_owned(), model_value(&p[1]));
   205	        }
   206	        return json!({"row": m});
   207	    }
   208	    v.clone()
   209	}
   210	
   211	fn shape(v: &Json) -> String {
   212	    v.as_object().and_then(|o| o.keys().next().cloned()).unwrap_or_else(|| "value".into())
   213	}

   215	/// One side's comparable record: `kind`, then `code` or `data`/`complete`/`next`.
   216	#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
   217	pub struct Canon {
   218	    pub kind: String,
   219	    pub code: Option<String>,
   220	    pub data: Option<Json>,
   221	    pub complete: Option<bool>,
   222	    pub next: bool,
   223	}
   224	impl Canon {
   225	    /// The side's stable class for a differing `field`: the field's own
   226	    /// value where it is a flag, else a code, kind or data shape.
   227	    pub fn class(&self, field: &str) -> String {
   228	        if field.ends_with("complete") {
   229	            return if self.complete == Some(true) { "complete" } else { "incomplete" }.into();
   230	        }
   335	}

   337	/// Compare one case whose source compiles. `Err` is a harness or emitter
   338	/// defect (never a verdict).
   339	pub fn compare(case: &Case, source: &str) -> Result<Checked, String> {
   340	    let unsupported = |reason: String| Ok(Checked { verdict: Verdict::Unsupported(reason), executed: 0, pages: 0, mutation: false, class: String::new() });
   341	    let module = match module(source) {
   342	        Ok(m) => m,
   343	        Err(reason) => return unsupported(reason),
   344	    };
   345	    let mutation = case.program.mutation();
   346	    if let Err(u) = module.program("run") {
   347	        return unsupported(u.reason);
   348	    }
   349	    if mutation {
   350	        if let Err(u) = module.program("observe") {
   351	            return unsupported(format!("observe-{}", u.reason));
   352	        }
   353	    }
   354	    let store = match module.store(&case.rows) {
   355	        Ok(s) => s,
   356	        Err(u) => return unsupported(u.reason),
   357	    };
   358	    let mut m_args = match module.tag_args("run", &case.args) {
   359	        Ok(a) => a,
   360	        Err(u) => return unsupported(u.reason),
   361	    };
   362	    // The prelude: each step on the engine and on the model's store, in order.
   363	    for i in 0..case.steps.len() {
   364	        if let Err(u) = module.program(&format!("prep{i}")) {
   365	            return unsupported(format!("prelude-{}", u.reason));
   366	        }
   367	        if let Err(u) = module.tag_args(&format!("prep{i}"), &case.steps[i].args) {
   368	            return unsupported(format!("prelude-{}", u.reason));
   369	        }
   370	    }
   371	    let (mut engine, prelude) = execute::world(case, source)?;
   372	    engine.set_ceilings(Ceilings::default());
   373	    let mut executed = 0;
   374	    let mut pages = 0;
   375	    let mut store = store;
   376	    let mut sweep_cursor: Option<Json> = None;
   377	    let mut steps = prelude.iter();
   378	    let mut trail = vec![];
   379	    for (i, step) in case.steps.iter().enumerate() {
   380	        let name = format!("prep{i}");
   381	        if step.sweep {
   382	            let e_sweep = steps.next().ok_or("prelude sweep outcome missing")?;
   383	            if e_sweep.kind != "sweep" || e_sweep.value.get("error").is_some() {
   384	                return Err(format!("engine prelude sweep failed: {:?}", e_sweep.value));
   385	            }
   386	            let args = module.tag_args(&name, &step.args).map_err(|u| u.to_string())?;
   387	            let viewer = step.viewer.as_deref().unwrap_or(&case.principal);
   388	            let mut sweep_case = module.case_at_sweep(&name, store.clone(), viewer, args, None, step.at, true).map_err(|u| u.to_string())?;
   389	            sweep_case["sweepLimit"] = json!(10_000);
   390	            if let Some(cursor) = &sweep_cursor { sweep_case["sweepCursor"] = cursor.clone(); }
   391	            let swept = ask(&sweep_case)?;
   392	            executed += 1;
   393	            if swept["kind"] != "committed" { return Err(format!("Lean prelude sweep failed: {swept}")); }
   394	            store = swept["store"].clone();
   395	            sweep_cursor = Some(swept["result"].clone());
   396	        }
   397	        let e_raw = steps.next().ok_or("prelude outcome missing")?.clone();
   398	        let args = module.tag_args(&name, &step.args).map_err(|u| u.to_string())?;
   399	        let viewer = step.viewer.as_deref().unwrap_or(&case.principal);
   400	        let m_raw = ask(&module.case_at(&name, store.clone(), viewer, args, None, step.at).map_err(|u| u.to_string())?)?;
   401	        executed += 2;
   402	        let (e, m) = (engine_canon(&e_raw), model_canon(&m_raw));
   403	        trail.push(trail_entry(&e, &m));
   404	        if let Some(f) = differ(&e, &m) {
   405	            return Ok(Checked { verdict: finding(&format!("prelude-{f}"), &e, &m, e_raw, &m_raw, trail), executed, pages, mutation, class: String::new() });
   406	        }
   407	        if m.kind == "committed" {
   408	            store = m_raw["store"].clone();
   409	        }
   410	    }
   411	    if case.sweep {
   412	        let e_sweep = steps.next().ok_or("final sweep outcome missing")?;
   413	        if e_sweep.kind != "sweep" || e_sweep.value.get("error").is_some() {
   414	            return Err(format!("engine final sweep failed: {:?}", e_sweep.value));
   415	        }
   416	        let mut sweep_case = module.case_at_sweep("run", store.clone(), &case.principal, m_args.clone(), None, case.clock, true).map_err(|u| u.to_string())?;
   417	        sweep_case["sweepLimit"] = json!(10_000);
   418	        if let Some(cursor) = &sweep_cursor { sweep_case["sweepCursor"] = cursor.clone(); }
   419	        let swept = ask(&sweep_case)?;
   420	        executed += 1;
   421	        if swept["kind"] != "committed" { return Err(format!("Lean final sweep failed: {swept}")); }
   422	        store = swept["store"].clone();
   423	    }
   424	    if mutation {
   425	        let e_raw = execute::execute(&mut engine, case, "run", &case.args);
   426	        let m_raw = ask(&module.case_at("run", store.clone(), &case.principal, m_args, None, case.clock).map_err(|u| u.to_string())?)?;
   427	        executed += 2;
   428	        let (e, m) = (engine_canon(&e_raw), model_canon(&m_raw));
   429	        let first_class = e.class("kind");
   430	        let mut trail = vec![trail_entry(&e, &m)];
   431	        if let Some(f) = differ(&e, &m) {
   432	            return Ok(Checked { verdict: finding(f, &e, &m, e_raw, &m_raw, trail), executed, pages, mutation, class: String::new() });
   433	        }
   434	        // The resulting stores, seen through `observe`.
   435	        let after = if m.kind == "committed" { m_raw["store"].clone() } else { store };
   436	        let o_args = module.tag_args("observe", &case.args).map_err(|u| u.to_string())?;
   437	        let eo_raw = execute::execute(&mut engine, case, "observe", &case.args);
   438	        let mo_raw = ask(&module.case_at("observe", after, &case.principal, o_args, None, case.clock).map_err(|u| u.to_string())?)?;
   439	        executed += 2;
   440	        let (eo, mo) = (engine_canon(&eo_raw), model_canon(&mo_raw));
   441	        trail.push(trail_entry(&eo, &mo));
   442	        if let Some(f) = differ(&eo, &mo) {
   443	            return Ok(Checked { verdict: finding(&format!("post-{f}"), &eo, &mo, eo_raw, &mo_raw, trail), executed, pages, mutation, class: String::new() });
   444	        }
   445	        return Ok(Checked { verdict: Verdict::Pass, executed, pages, mutation, class: format!("{}-{}", if mutation { "mutation" } else { "query" }, first_class) });
   446	    }
   447	    let mut e_args = case.args.clone();
   448	    let mut trail = Vec::new();
   449	    let mut seen = BTreeSet::new();
   450	    let mut first_class = String::new();
   451	    loop {
   452	        let e_raw = execute::execute(&mut engine, case, "run", &e_args);
   453	        let m_raw = ask(&module.case_at("run", store.clone(), &case.principal, m_args.clone(), None, case.clock).map_err(|u| u.to_string())?)?;
   454	        executed += 2;
   455	        pages += 1;
   456	        let (e, m) = (engine_canon(&e_raw), model_canon(&m_raw));
   457	        if pages == 1 {
   458	            first_class = e.class("kind");
   459	        }
   460	        trail.push(trail_entry(&e, &m));
   461	        let phase = if pages > 1 { "continuation-" } else { "" };
   462	        if let Some(f) = differ(&e, &m) {
   463	            return Ok(Checked { verdict: finding(&format!("{phase}{f}"), &e, &m, e_raw, &m_raw, trail), executed, pages, mutation, class: String::new() });
   464	        }
   465	        if !e.next {
   466	            break;
   467	        }
   468	        let next = e_raw.next().unwrap().to_owned();
   469	        if !seen.insert(next.clone()) || seen.len() > case.rows.len() + 2 {
   470	            return Ok(Checked { verdict: finding("cursor-cycle", &e, &m, e_raw, &m_raw, trail), executed, pages, mutation, class: String::new() });
   471	        }
   472	        e_args["c"] = json!(next);
   473	        m_args.insert("c".into(), m_raw["next"].clone());
   474	    }
   475	    Ok(Checked { verdict: Verdict::Pass, executed, pages, mutation, class: format!("query-{first_class}") })
   476	}

   484	    out.extend(crate::generate::page5_features(case));

   539	            .flat_map(|b| b.all()).any(|s| matches!(s, crate::ast::Stmt::Write { kind: Write::Delete, .. }));

   577	    if rules[0] == Rule::OwnerOrGrant {

   592	        let uniform = match rules[0] {

   594	            // The witness disjunct is pinned by `.bucket`: decided per caller (§16.3).
   595	            Rule::OwnerOrWitness | Rule::OwnerOrIdWitness => *owner,
   596	            _ => true,
   597	        };
   598	        if matches!(rules[0], Rule::OwnerOrWitness | Rule::OwnerOrIdWitness) && !*owner && matches!(kind, Read::Page | Read::Bounded | Read::Exists) {
   599	            out.push(format!("parent-pinned-grant-{kind:?}").to_lowercase());
   600	        }
   601	        if matches!(kind, Read::Exists) {
   602	            out.push(format!("search-exists-{}", if uniform { "decided" } else { "undecided" }));
   603	        }
   604	        if matches!(kind, Read::Page | Read::Bounded) {
   605	            out.push(format!("{}-{kind:?}", if uniform { "uniform" } else { "non-uniform" }).to_lowercase());
   606	            if uniform && matches!(kind, Read::Page) {
   607	                // C2: whether the binder may keep a residual filter on the scan.
   608	                out.push(format!("uniform-page-{}", if case.program.residual.is_some() { "with-residual" } else { "without-residual" }));
   609	            }
   610	        }
   611	        if let Some(order) = &case.program.order {
   612	            out.push(format!("order-{}", order.join("-")));
   613	        }
   614	        if let Some(residual) = &case.program.residual {
   615	            out.push(format!("residual-{}", residual_name(residual)));
   616	        }
   617	    }
   618	    out
   619	}

   621	/// A stable feature name for a residual conjunct of `generate`.
   622	fn residual_name(residual: &str) -> &'static str {
   623	    match residual {
   624	        ".score >= 0" => "score-ge",
   625	        ".label != ''" => "label-ne",
   626	        ".maybe = null" => "nullable-eq-null",
   627	        ".maybe = n" => "nullable-eq-arg",
   628	        "(.score > 0 or .flag = false)" => "disjunction",
   629	        _ => "other",
   630	    }
   631	}
   632	
   633	/// One case, counted into `report`.
   634	pub fn check(case: &Case, report: &mut Report, mut found: impl FnMut(crate::oracle::Finding)) -> Result<(), String> {
   635	    report.generated += 1;
   636	    for feature in crate::coverage::features(case) {
   637	        *report.coverage.entry(feature).or_default() += 1;
   638	    }
   639	    let source = case.program.source();
   640	    if let Err(e) = execute::compile(&source) {
   641	        report.binder_refused_unexpected += 1;
   642	        return Err(format!("binder: {e}"));
   643	    }
   644	    report.compiled += 1;
   645	    let checked = compare(case, &source)?;
   646	    report.executed += checked.executed;
   647	    if let Verdict::Pass = &checked.verdict {
   648	        // What agreed, by outcome class: evidence for the open points.
   649	        *report.store_stats.entry(format!("lean-agreed/{}", checked.class)).or_default() += 1;
   650	    }
   651	    let stats = &mut report.store_stats;
   652	    // @ref LLP 3000.040#25-the-lean-model — calendar evidence is counted where it is compared.
   653	    if case.program.time_arg {
   654	        *stats.entry("lean-calendar-generated".into()).or_default() += 1;
   655	        let class = match &checked.verdict { Verdict::Unsupported(_) => "unsupported", Verdict::Pass => "agreed", Verdict::Disagree(_) => "disagreeing", _ => "other" };
   656	        *stats.entry(format!("lean-calendar-{class}")).or_default() += 1;
   657	    }
   658	    match &checked.verdict {
   659	        Verdict::Unsupported(_) => *stats.entry("lean-unsupported".into()).or_default() += 1,
   660	        _ => {
   661	            *stats.entry("lean-supported".into()).or_default() += 1;
   662	            *stats.entry(format!("lean-supported-{}", if checked.mutation { "mutation" } else { "query" })).or_default() += 1;
   663	            *stats.entry("lean-pages-compared".into()).or_default() += checked.pages;
   664	            if checked.pages > 1 {
   665	                *stats.entry("lean-continued-reads".into()).or_default() += 1;
   666	            }
   667	        }
   668	    }
   669	    if !matches!(checked.verdict, Verdict::Unsupported(_)) {
   670	        let disagreed = matches!(checked.verdict, Verdict::Disagree(_));
   671	        for feature in features(case) {
   672	            *stats.entry(format!("lean-feature/{feature}/compared")).or_default() += 1;
   673	            if disagreed {
   674	                *stats.entry(format!("lean-feature/{feature}/disagreeing")).or_default() += 1;
   675	            }
   676	        }
   677	    }
   678	    report.by_oracle.entry("lean".into()).or_default().record(&checked.verdict);
   679	    if let Verdict::Disagree(f) = checked.verdict {
   680	        found(f);
   681	    }
   682	    Ok(())
   683	}

   685	pub fn reproduce(case: &Case, source: &str) -> Result<Verdict, String> {
   686	    execute::compile(source).map_err(|e| format!("binder: {e}"))?;
   687	    compare(case, source).map(|c| c.verdict)
   688	}

   690	/// The Lean campaign's case for `seed`: the Stage 1 generator's case, and
   691	/// for about half the seeds a variant aimed at the model's open points
   692	/// (`snapback4/lean/OPEN.md`), from an independent stream so the base case
   693	/// is unchanged:
   694	///
   695	/// - per-effect rules on `items` (R2's named and unnamed update rules, W1–W4
   696	///   precedence between rules, readability and clashes, C8's non-uniform
   697	///   reads), with `online only` so any read rule is admissible;
   698	/// - `access` unreadable to everyone (R1: whether a rule probe sees a row its
   699	///   table hides);
   700	/// - page orders over a nullable, a boolean or a unique id column (V2, V3);
   701	/// - a further domain conjunct: residual filters (C2's lookahead) and a
   702	///   null-valued equality (V5).
   703	///
   704	/// A third independent stream (so the draws above are unchanged) adds the
   705	/// forms the engine decides per caller (OPEN C5, C8):
   706	///
   707	/// - half the unpaged totals become a search `exists` over the same domain
   708	///   (LLP 3000.036 §15.12), which needs no decided rule and so draws every
   709	///   read rule;
   710	/// - a third of `Owner`/`OwnerOrWitness` read rules become
   711	///   `.owner = viewer or exists access[0, viewer]`, a readable grant (§12.1);
   712	///   `OwnerOrWitness` under the always-pinned `.bucket` is the parent-pinned
   713	///   grant (§16.3);
   714	/// - a third of pages and `exists` reads end their domain with a test that
   715	///   reads no row (`exists access[bucket, viewer]`, its negation, `a < b`),
   716	///   which the compiler lowers to an `if` around a returned page (§15.4).
   717	pub fn generate(seed: u64) -> Case {
   718	    use crate::ast::{Read, Rule};
   719	    let mut case = crate::generate::generate(seed);
   720	    unbound(&mut case);
   721	    // Half the widened cases the model cannot run (projections, expiry) are
   722	    // narrowed back into its fragment; the other half stay named unsupported.
   723	    if crate::generate::Rng::new(seed ^ 0x4c45_414e_4e41_5257).next() % 2 == 0 {
   724	        narrow(&mut case);
   725	    }
   726	    let mut extra = crate::generate::Rng::new(seed ^ 0x4c45_414e_4558_5354);
   727	    if let Body::Read { kind: kind @ (Read::Count | Read::Sum | Read::Min | Read::Max), .. } = &mut case.program.body {
   728	        if extra.pick(2) == 0 {
   729	            *kind = Read::Exists;
   730	        }
   731	    }
   732	    variants(&mut case, seed);
   733	    if let Some(effects) = &mut case.program.tables[0].effects {
   734	        if matches!(effects[0], Rule::Owner | Rule::OwnerOrWitness) && extra.pick(3) == 0 {
   735	            effects[0] = Rule::OwnerOrGrant;
   736	        }
   737	    }
   738	    if matches!(case.program.body, Body::Read { kind: Read::Page | Read::Bounded | Read::Exists, .. }) && extra.pick(3) == 0 {
   739	        let guards = ["exists access[bucket, viewer]", "not exists access[bucket, viewer]", "a < b"];
   740	        case.program.guard = Some(guards[extra.pick(3) as usize].to_owned());
   741	    }
   742	    membership_page(&mut case, seed);
   743	    boolean_grant_page(&mut case, seed);
   744	    crate::generate::page3(&mut case);
   745	    crate::generate::page4(&mut case);
   746	    case
   747	}

   750	/// fixed principal; half rely on the total unique membership point. Both use
   751	/// the inverse `(principal, bucket)` index for metered discovery before merge.

   759	    if inherited_id || inherited_discovery {
   760	        let read = if inherited_id { Rule::OwnerOrIdWitness } else { Rule::OwnerOrWitness };

     3	/-!
     4	# Write authority
     5	
     6	**No write succeeds unless the corresponding rule holds.** A successful write
     7	either leaves the store unchanged (`insert … if absent` on a visible clash)
     8	or is one authorized `Step`: an insert whose insert rule admits the new
     9	image, an update whose update rule admits (old, next) for a row that exists,
    10	or a delete whose delete rule admits the row. Rules are evaluated in the
    11	opened projection of the store as it stood immediately before that write
    12	(`applyWrite_authorized`).
    13	
    14	A whole mutation's store transition is a chain of such steps
    15	(`mutation_authorized`).
    16	-/
    17	
    18	namespace Quarry
    19	
    20	inductive Step (sch : Schema) (v : List Nat) (now : Int) : Store → Store → Prop
    21	  | insert {s : Store} {t : String} {td : TableDecl} {r : Row} :
    22	      sch.table? t = some td → td.insert.eval (openedStore sch s now) v { self := some r } = true →
    23	      Step sch v now s (s.insertRow t r)
    24	  | update {s : Store} {t : String} {td : TableDecl} {old nw : Row} :
    25	      sch.table? t = some td → old ∈ s t →
    26	      td.update.eval (openedStore sch s now) v { old := some old, next := some nw } = true →
    27	      Step sch v now s (s.replaceRow t old nw)
    28	  /-- A delete whose delete rule admits the row, with the referential
    29	  actions the schema declares on the rows naming it (LLP 3000.039 §4.1: the
    30	  parent's delete authorizes a declared cascade or set null). -/
    31	  | delete {s s' : Store} {t : String} {td : TableDecl} {old : Row} :
    32	      sch.table? t = some td → old ∈ s t →
    33	      td.delete.eval (openedStore sch s now) v { self := some old } = true →
    34	      refDeleteFrom sch (unexpiredStore sch s now) s t old = .ok s' →
    35	      Step sch v now s s'
    36	  /-- An expired same-id row is retired inside an insert transaction before
    37	  the replacement image's remaining constraints are checked. -/
    38	  | retire {s s' : Store} {t : String} {td : TableDecl} {old : Row} :
    39	      sch.table? t = some td → old ∈ s t → expired td now old = true →
    40	      refDeleteFrom sch (unexpiredStore sch s now) s t old = .ok s' →
    41	      Step sch v now s s'
    42	  /-- A same-id replacement is one authorized transition: its insert rule is
    43	  checked against the pre-retirement store, then the expired predecessor's
    44	  actions run, then the new image is inserted. -/
    45	  | replaceExpired {s retired : Store} {t : String} {td : TableDecl} {old img : Row} :
    46	      sch.table? t = some td → old ∈ s t → expired td now old = true →
    47	      td.insert.eval (openedStore sch s now) v { self := some img } = true →
    48	      refDeleteFrom sch (unexpiredStore sch s now) s t old = .ok retired →
    49	      Step sch v now s (retired.insertRow t img)
    50	
    51	inductive Steps (sch : Schema) (v : List Nat) (now : Int) : Store → Store → Prop
    52	  | refl (s : Store) : Steps sch v now s s
    53	  | step {s s' s'' : Store} : Step sch v now s s' → Steps sch v now s' s'' → Steps sch v now s s''

    55	theorem Steps.trans {sch v now} {a b d : Store} (h1 : Steps sch v now a b) (h2 : Steps sch v now b d) :
    56	    Steps sch v now a d := by
    57	  induction h1 with
    58	  | refl => exact h2
    59	  | step h _ ih => exact .step h (ih h2)

    61	theorem Steps.of_step_or_eq {sch v now} {a b : Store} (h : b = a ∨ Step sch v now a b) : Steps sch v now a b := by

    64	  · exact .step h (.refl _)

    68	  cases x with

    76	  unfold findRow at h

 fn run<H: Host>(host: &mut H) {
+    // Digest-addressed maintained rows use the same fixed identity on the
+    // server and each device store, even for the largest composite values in
+    // this generated family.
+    let aggregate = r#"
+table groups:
+  public
+  sync public
+table entries:
+  owner: principal
+  parent: groups
+  token: text <=64
+  amount: int
+  public
+  sync public
+view totals: sum entries of .amount by .owner, .parent, .token
+  public
+"#;
+    let (mut e, b) = compile(aggregate);
+    let principal = "p".repeat(64);
+    let parent = "r".repeat(64);
+    let token = "x".repeat(64);
+    e.seed_at([
+        ("groups".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id(&parent))])),
+        ("entries".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([
+            ("id", id("entry")), ("owner", id(&principal)), ("parent", id(&parent)),
+            ("token", snapback4_core::Value::String(token.clone())),
+            ("amount", snapback4_core::Value::Int(7)),
+        ])),
+    ], 0).unwrap();
+    let expected = snapback4_core::schema::maintained_id(&[
+        id(&principal), id(&parent), snapback4_core::Value::String(token),
+    ]);
+    assert_eq!(expected.len(), 64);
+    let mut d = host.open("aggregate-digest", Some(b)).unwrap();
+    acquire(&mut e, &mut d, &principal, 0);
+    let rows = d.store().raw_rows("totals");
+    assert_eq!(rows.len(), 1);
+    assert_eq!(rows[0].field("id").unwrap(), &id(&expected));
+    host.close("aggregate-digest", d);
+
     // Server expiry is a physical retirement with the schema's declared
     // referential effects. Devices receive that one committed closure just as
     // they receive an authored parent delete.
@@ -88,10 +128,12 @@ table parents:
   sync public
 table cascadeChildren:
   parent: parents on delete cascade
+  cap 1 by parent
   public 'cascadeChildren'
   sync public
 table nullableChildren:
   parent: parents ? on delete set null
+  cap 1 by parent
   public 'nullableChildren'
   sync public
 "#;

+/-- An eager snapshot of the declared table rows used while sweeping. A
+`Store` update is a functional closure over the previous store; repeatedly
+retiring rows through that representation retains an exponentially growing
+evaluation tree. Snapshotting after each successful retirement changes only
+the representation, while preserving table order and action sequencing. -/
+abbrev MaterialStore := Array (String × List Row)
+
+def materialRows (tables : List String) (s : Store) : MaterialStore :=
+  tables.toArray.map fun t => (t, s t)
+
+def MaterialStore.store (rows : MaterialStore) (fallback : Store) : Store := fun t =>
+  match rows.find? fun p => p.1 == t with
+  | some (_, rs) => rs
+  | none => fallback t
+
+-- @ref LLP 3000.036.003#6 — sweep each due root transactionally in table order.
 /-- Retire every due physical row. `restrict` retains that root but never
 stops later due keys; cascade and set-null are committed with the root. The
 model has no read-through retained-history rows, so every non-restricted due
 root can be retired immediately. -/
 def sweepExpired (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (now : Int) : Store :=
-  sch.tables.foldl (fun s td => (s td.name).foldl (fun s r =>
-    if expired td now r && stored s td.name r then
-      match refDeleteFrom sch (unexpiredStore sch s now) s td.name r with
-      | .ok next => next
-      | .error (.refuse "E_REFERENCED") => s
-      | .error _ => s
-    else s) s) s
+  let tables := sch.tables.map (·.name)
+  let rows := sch.tables.foldl (fun rows td =>
+    let physical := rows.store s
+    (physical td.name).foldl (fun rows r =>
+      let physical := rows.store s
+      if expired td now r && stored physical td.name r then
+        match refDeleteFrom sch (unexpiredStore sch physical now) physical td.name r with
+        | .ok next => materialRows tables next
+        | .error (.refuse "E_REFERENCED") => rows
+        | .error _ => rows
+      else rows) rows) (materialRows tables s)
+  rows.store s

+This commit-end rule also covers a source of a row-keyed maintained view. The
+source's final image first reaches normal maintenance, then its expired image
+is retired through the common action path in the same transaction. No derived
+maintenance shortcut may physically remove that source before closure
+preflight: doing so would bypass a live `restrict` child and could orphan a
+`cascade` or `set null` child. The source contribution and its retirement
+cancel within the transaction, so an already-expired birth never enters a
+committed count basis. The execution retains at most one retirement key per
+changed source row; its allocation is charged when first retained and the
+program's existing rows-written ceiling bounds the commit-end walk.
+
 A live `restrict` child, or a physically retained read-through child outside
 the cascade closure but below a row in it, keeps the expired root physically
 stored and the sweep continues to later due keys. A read-through child inside

+#[test]
+fn row_keyed_view_source_expiry_retires_through_reference_actions() {
+    let source = r#"
+table conversations:
+  public
+table members:
+  conversation: conversations
+  principal: principal
+  cap 4 by conversation
+  public
+table messages:
+  conversation: conversations
+  ordinal: int
+  sender: principal
+  until: time ?
+  expire at .until
+  public
+  update <- allow
+view unread: count messages by members m
+  where .conversation = m.conversation and .sender != m.principal
+table cascadeKids:
+  message: messages on delete cascade
+  cap 1 by message
+  public
+table nullableKids:
+  message: messages ? on delete set null
+  cap 1 by message
+  public
+table blockers:
+  message: messages
+  public
+mutation expire(message: messages):
+  update messages[message] { until: now }
+"#;
+    let mut e = engine(source);
+    e.seed_at([
+        ("conversations".into(), object([("id", id("c"))])),
+        ("members".into(), object([("id", id("member")), ("conversation", id("c")), ("principal", id("alice"))])),
+        ("messages".into(), object([("id", id("message")), ("conversation", id("c")), ("ordinal", Value::Int(1)), ("sender", id("bob")), ("until", Value::Null)])),
+        ("cascadeKids".into(), object([("id", id("cascade")), ("message", id("message"))])),
+        ("nullableKids".into(), object([("id", id("nullable")), ("message", id("message"))])),
+        ("blockers".into(), object([("id", id("blocker")), ("message", id("message"))])),
+    ], 0).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("unread").unwrap()[0].field("value").unwrap(), &Value::Int(1));
+
+    let context = || Context::new("dev:alice", BTreeMap::from([("message".into(), id("message"))])).at(100);
+    let refused = e.mutate("expire", None, context()).unwrap();
+    assert!(matches!(refused.state, WriteState::Failed { ref why, .. } if why.code == "E_REFERENCED"), "{:?}", refused.state);
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("messages").unwrap()[0].field("until").unwrap(), &Value::Null);
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("unread").unwrap()[0].field("value").unwrap(), &Value::Int(1));
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("cascadeKids").unwrap().len(), 1, "a refused commit rolls its cascade back");
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("nullableKids").unwrap()[0].field("message").unwrap(), &id("message"));
+
+    e.seed_delete("blockers", "blocker").unwrap();
+    let sent = e.mutate("expire", None, context()).unwrap();
+    assert!(matches!(sent.state, WriteState::Sent { .. }), "{:?}", sent.state);
+    assert!(e.store().rows("messages").unwrap().is_empty());
+    assert!(e.store().rows("cascadeKids").unwrap().is_empty());
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("nullableKids").unwrap()[0].field("message").unwrap(), &Value::Null);
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("unread").unwrap()[0].field("value").unwrap(), &Value::Int(0));
+}

   176	fn expiring_rank_rewrite_routes_by_window_intent() {
   177	    let source = SOURCE.replace("  at: time", "  until: time\n  by byUntil: until\n  expire at .until\n  at: time");
   178	    let bound = snapback4_lang::compile(&[("expiry.q".into(), format!("{source}\nmaintain totals: count posts by author\n  read <- allow\n  by byCount: value, id\n"))]);
   179	    let diagnostic = bound.diagnostics.iter().find(|d| d.code == "E_QUARRY_MAINTAIN_EXPIRE").unwrap();
   180	    println!("{diagnostic}");
   181	    assert_eq!(diagnostic.message, "maintain totals cannot order by value because source posts expires: stored order is stale before the physical sweep, so taking stored top-N can miss a live winner; a count upper-bound threshold scan is not built");
   182	    assert_eq!(diagnostic.guide, "feeds");
   183	    assert_eq!(diagnostic.rewrite, "for an entity-time window over a non-expiring source, use the Trending predicate in guide feeds; for expiring contributions, stream each candidate's live count and rank only a complete candidate domain; a meter cut makes the ranking incomplete");
   184	}

+    // from the final wire image for this pre-P2 compatibility corpus.
+    strip_maintained_identity_capability(wire)
+}
+
+fn strip_maintained_identity_capability(mut wire: String) -> String {
+    let capability = "maintained-id-sha256-v1";
+    wire = wire.replace(&format!("\"{capability}\","), "")
+        .replace(&format!(",\"{capability}\""), "")
+        .replace(&format!("[{{\"Capabilities\":[\"{capability}\"]}}]"), "[]")
+        .replace(&format!("{{\"Capabilities\":[\"{capability}\"]}},"), "")
+        .replace(&format!(",{{\"Capabilities\":[\"{capability}\"]}}"), "");
+    assert!(!wire.contains(capability));
+    wire
 }

+fn expiry_is_emitted_as_a_modeled_table_lifecycle() {
+    let source = "table t:\n  n: int\n  expiresAt: time ?\n  expire at .expiresAt\n  read <- allow\n  online only\nquery witness():\n  return 1\n";

+    let case = m.case_at_sweep("witness", m.store(&[]).unwrap(), "alice", Default::default(), None, 10, true).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(case["sweep"], true);
+}

   365	fn read_packed<'a>(store: &mut wasmi::Store<Host<'a>>, packed: i64) -> Result<String, RuntimeError> {
   366	    let Some(memory) = store.data().memory else { return Err(structural("no memory".into())) };
   367	    let range = checked_range((packed >> 32) as u32, packed as u32, memory.data_size(&*store), store.data().output_limit, MeterKind::OutputBytes, "native module answer")?;
   368	    let mut bytes = vec![0u8; range.len()];
   369	    memory.read(&*store, range.start, &mut bytes).map_err(|e| structural(format!("the module's answer is out of bounds: {e}")))?;
   370	    String::from_utf8(bytes).map_err(|_| structural("the module's answer is not UTF-8".into()))
   371	}
   372	
   373	fn write_bytes<'a>(store: &mut wasmi::Store<Host<'a>>, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(i32, i32), RuntimeError> {
   374	    let (Some(memory), Some(alloc)) = (store.data().memory, store.data().alloc.clone()) else { return Err(structural("the module is not instantiated".into())) };
   375	    if bytes.len() > store.data().heap_limit {
   376	        return Err(bound(MeterKind::HeapBytes, bytes.len(), store.data().heap_limit, "native module request"));
   377	    }
   378	    let len = i32::try_from(bytes.len()).map_err(|_| bound(MeterKind::HeapBytes, bytes.len(), store.data().heap_limit, "native module request"))?;
   379	    let ptr = match alloc.call(&mut *store, len) {
   380	        Ok(ptr) => ptr,
   381	        Err(error) => return Err(resource_bound(store.data(), &error).unwrap_or_else(|| structural(format!("sb4_alloc trapped: {error}")))),
   382	    };
   383	    let range = checked_range(ptr as u32, len as u32, memory.data_size(&*store), store.data().heap_limit, MeterKind::HeapBytes, "native module request")?;
   384	    memory.write(&mut *store, range.start, bytes).map_err(|e| structural(format!("cannot write the request into the module: {e}")))?;
   385	    Ok((ptr, len))
   386	}

   449	        rows_written: runner.rows_written,

   451	    }
   452	}

+#[test]
+fn maintained_identity_is_fixed_size_and_domain_separated() {
+    let short = maintained_id(&[Value::String("x".into())]);

   101	fn refused(why: snapback4_core::Refusal, mutation: bool) -> Actual {
   102	    // The source exporter distinguishes application require/check outcomes
   103	    // from engine refusals. The card carries that distinction in the rule
   104	    // field or E_CONFLICT, rather than in a second write-state vocabulary.
   105	    let application = why.rule.is_some() || why.code == "E_CONFLICT";
   106	    let admission = matches!(why.code.as_str(), "E_STRUCTURAL_FANOUT" | "E_UNBOUND_SCAN");
   107	    Actual { result: None, error: Some(format!("{} ({})", why.code, why.message)), state: if admission { LocalState::CertificationRefused } else if application { if mutation { LocalState::Rejected } else { LocalState::Denied } } else { LocalState::Refused }, next: None }
   108	}

   582	fn scan_limit(scan: &snapback4_core::ir::Scan, expected: &Expected, owned: bool, owners: &BTreeSet<String>) -> bool {
   583	    // @ref LLP 3000.027#1 — a cursorless limit is the answer, not lost coverage.
   584	    ((scan.opaque_cursor && !owned) && expected.range_stops.get(&scan.site).is_some_and(|stops| stops.iter().any(|stop| stop == "limit")))
   585	        || scan.prefix.iter().filter_map(|key| key.scalar()).any(|value| expression_page_limit(value, expected, owners))
   586	        || [scan.after.as_deref(), scan.before.as_deref()].into_iter().flatten().any(|value| expression_page_limit(value, expected, owners))
   587	        || scan.range.as_ref().is_some_and(|range| [range.gt.as_deref(), range.gte.as_deref(), range.lt.as_deref(), range.lte.as_deref()].into_iter().flatten().any(|value| expression_page_limit(value, expected, owners)))
   588	        || scan.filter.as_ref().is_some_and(|value| expression_page_limit(value, expected, owners))
   589	}
   590	
   591	fn expression_page_limit(expr: &snapback4_core::ir::Expr, expected: &Expected, owners: &BTreeSet<String>) -> bool {
   592	    use snapback4_core::ir::Expr;
   593	    match expr {
   594	        Expr::Literal(_) | Expr::Variable(_) | Expr::Input(_) => false,
   595	        Expr::Field { base, .. } | Expr::Unary { value: base, .. } => expression_page_limit(base, expected, owners),
   596	        Expr::Array(values) | Expr::Builtin { args: values, .. } => values.iter().any(|value| expression_page_limit(value, expected, owners)),
   597	        Expr::Object(fields) => fields.values().any(|value| expression_page_limit(value, expected, owners)),
   598	        Expr::Shape { base, fields } => expression_page_limit(base, expected, owners) || fields.values().any(|value| expression_page_limit(value, expected, owners)),
   599	        Expr::Block { body, value } => outer_page_limit(body, expected, owners) || expression_page_limit(value, expected, owners),
   600	        Expr::Binary { left, right, .. } => expression_page_limit(left, expected, owners) || expression_page_limit(right, expected, owners),
   601	        Expr::Get(read) | Expr::Exists(read) => read.key.iter().any(|value| expression_page_limit(value, expected, owners)),
   602	        Expr::Scan(scan) => scan_limit(scan, expected, owners.contains(&scan.site), owners),
   603	        // Lane stops describe the emitted union's cut; source stops describe
   604	        // the bounded set of lanes the author explicitly selected.
   605	        Expr::Merge(merge) => merge.lanes.iter().any(|lane| outer_page_limit(&lane.setup, expected, owners) || scan_limit(&lane.scan, expected, owners.contains(&merge.site), owners)),
   606	    }
   607	}

   609	fn compare(expected: &Expected, expected_state: LocalState, actual: Actual) -> Verdict {
   610	    let mut failures = Vec::new();
   611	    if actual.state != expected_state {
   612	        failures.push(format!("expected card state {expected_state:?} (corpus {:?}), got {:?}", expected.local_state, actual.state));
   613	    }
   614	    if actual.next != expected.next {
   615	        failures.push(format!("expected next {:?}, got {:?}", expected.next, actual.next));
   616	    }
   617	    match (&expected.error_code, actual.error) {
   618	        (Some(expected), Some(actual)) => {
   619	            let code = actual.split(' ').next().unwrap_or(&actual);
   620	            if expected != code {
   621	                failures.push(format!("expected refusal {expected}, got {actual}"));
   622	            }
   623	        }
   624	        (Some(expected), None) => failures.push(format!("expected refusal {expected}, got a result {}", actual.result.map(|v| snapback4_core::value::canonical_json(&v)).unwrap_or_default())),
   625	        (None, Some(actual)) => failures.push(format!("expected a result, got refusal {actual}")),
   626	        (None, None) => {
   627	            let actual = snapback4_core::value::canonical_json(&actual.result.unwrap_or(Value::Null));
   628	            let expected = expected.canonical_result.clone().unwrap_or_default();
   629	            if actual != expected {
   630	                failures.push(format!("result differs\n    expected {expected}\n    actual   {actual}"));
   631	            }
   632	        }
   633	    }
   634	    if failures.is_empty() { Verdict::Pass } else { Verdict::Fail(failures.join("; ")) }
   635	}

   353	fn card_expected(case: &Case, schema: &Schema, program: &Program) -> Result<Expected, String> {
   354	    use snapback4_core::cursor::{CursorPosition, decode_cursor, encode_cursor};

   358	    for descriptor in pages.values() {
   359	        let page: LegacyResultPage = serde_json::from_value(descriptor.clone()).map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;
   360	        if !descriptors.contains(&page) { descriptors.push(page); }
   361	    }
   362	    let Some(canonical) = &expected.canonical_result else { return Ok(expected) };
   363	    if expected.error_code.is_some() { return Ok(expected); }
   364	    let result: Value = serde_json::from_str(canonical).map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;
   365	    if expected.local_state == LocalState::Fresh && case.certificate["completeness"] == "Page"

   367	    {
   368	        let position = decode_cursor(schema, token).map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;

+    /// Whether a read-through child remains outside a delete's cascade
+    /// closure. Children in `deleting` are removed first by deletion_order and
+    /// therefore do not physically retain their parent.

+        &mut self,
+        parent: &str,
+        id: &Value,
+        deleting: &BTreeSet<(String, String)>,
     ) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
         let children: Vec<_> = self
             .schema
             .children(parent)
             .map(|(n, _, _)| n.clone())
             .collect();
+        // At most `deleting.len()` matching rows can be skipped across a
+        // table: row ids are unique. One more row decides outside occupancy.
+        let limit = deleting.len().saturating_add(1);

+        let heap = children.iter().map(|name| super::write_target::row_copy_ceiling(&self.schema.tables[name]).saturating_mul(limit as u64)).fold(0_u64, u64::saturating_add);
+        let probes = (children.len() as u64).saturating_mul(limit as u64);
+        self.authorized_scan(&[(MeterKind::Examined, probes), (MeterKind::Steps, probes), (MeterKind::HeapBytes, heap)], |runner, scope| {
             let mut occupied = false;
             for name in &children {
-                occupied |= !runner.tx.scan(scope, name, CHILDREN, &[id.clone()], &Bounds::default(), Dir::Asc, 1)?.is_empty();
+                let rows = runner.tx.scan(scope, name, CHILDREN, &[id.clone()], &Bounds::default(), Dir::Asc, limit)?;
+                occupied |= rows.into_iter().any(|(row, _)| row.field("id").ok().and_then(|id| id.as_str().ok())
+                    .is_none_or(|child| !deleting.contains(&(name.clone(), child.to_owned()))));
             }
             Ok(occupied)
         })

+/// The copied corpus is a frozen image of the pre-digest store. Translate
+/// maintained target identities at the adapter boundary so its logical values
+/// remain an oracle for the current address function. Other row ids retain
+/// their exact frozen spelling.
+fn legacy_maintained_ids(schema: &Schema, rows: &[ReceiptRow]) -> Result<BTreeMap<String, String>, String> {
+    let mut ids = BTreeMap::new();
+    for receipt in rows {
+        let Some(maintain) = schema.maintains.iter().find(|maintain| maintain.target == receipt.table && maintain.row_key.is_none()) else { continue };
+        let old = match receipt.row.field("id") {
+            Ok(Value::Id(id)) => id,
+            Ok(_) => return Err(format!("{}.id is not an id", receipt.table)),
+            Err(error) => return Err(format!("{}.id: {error}", receipt.table)),
+        };
+        let key = maintain.by.iter().map(|field| receipt.row.field(field).cloned().map_err(|error| format!("{}.{}: {error}", receipt.table, field))).collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()?;
+        let new = snapback4_core::schema::maintained_id(&key);
+        if let Some(prior) = ids.insert(old.clone(), new.clone())
+            && prior != new
+        {
+            return Err(format!("legacy id {old} names more than one maintained group"));
+        }
+    }
+    Ok(ids)

     5	pub(super) struct Plan {
     6	    pub project: bool,
     7	    pub indexes: BTreeSet<String>,
     8	}
     9	
    10	// @ref LLP 3000.019#3.6 — an added view must not reconstruct unrelated rows and indexes.
    11	// Compare the whole table except indexes. This intentionally keeps the old
    12	// exhaustive validation for defaults, captures, rules, lifetimes and constraints.
    13	// An index can survive an unrelated column change only when each interpreted
    14	// dependency (including calendar, words and contribution predicates) is equal.
    15	// Device installations have no persisted server predecessor and keep that path.
    16	pub(super) fn plans(next: &Schema, previous: Option<&Schema>) -> BTreeMap<String, Plan> {
    17	    next.tables
    18	        .iter()
    19	        .map(|(name, table)| {
    20	            let old = previous.and_then(|schema| schema.table(name));
    21	            let project = old.is_none_or(|old| {
    22	                let mut comparable = table.clone();
    23	                comparable.indexes = old.indexes.clone();
    24	                &comparable != old
    25	            });
    26	            let indexes = table
    27	                .indexes
    28	                .iter()
    29	                .filter(|(index_name, index)| {
    30	                    old.is_none_or(|old| {
    31	                        old.indexes.get(*index_name) != Some(*index)
    32	                            || old.through != table.through
    33	                            || old.columns.keys().chain(table.columns.keys()).any(|field| {
    34	                                index.uses_column(field)
    35	                                    && (crate::successor::interpretation(
    36	                                        previous.unwrap(),
    37	                                        name,
    38	                                        field,
    39	                                    ) != crate::successor::interpretation(next, name, field)
    40	                                        || old.maintained.get(field) != table.maintained.get(field))
    41	                            })
    42	                    })
    43	                })
    44	                .map(|(name, _)| name.clone())
    45	                .collect();
    46	            (name.clone(), Plan { project, indexes })
    47	        })
    48	        .collect()
    49	}
    50	
    51	/// Historical catalog numbers remain, but inactive names lose their rows/keys.
    52	pub(super) fn active_names(schema: &Schema) -> BTreeSet<String> {
    53	    schema.tables.iter().filter(|(_, t)| t.ephemeral.is_none())
    54	        .flat_map(|(name, table)| std::iter::once(name.clone())
    55	            .chain(table.indexes.keys().map(move |index| format!("{name}.{index}"))))
    56	        .collect()
    57	}

codex
I found a migration edge case: legacy ID translation reads group fields from the candidate schema, after activation may have projected the old target rows. I’m checking whether an otherwise supported grouping change can therefore block an upgrade.

codex
NOT READY

- **Legacy migration blocks a supported grouping change.** [maintains.rs:207](/home/ccheever/projects/sb4-w12-lang/snapback4/crates/snapback4-core/src/engine/maintains.rs:207) derives legacy keys from the candidate maintain declaration and requires those fields in each old target row at line 219. Activation has already destructively projected those rows using the candidate columns ([store/activation.rs:315](/home/ccheever/projects/sb4-w12-lang/snapback4/crates/snapback4-core/src/store/activation.rs:315)). Consequently, upgrading a populated 0.4.28 store while changing `view totals: count entries by .n` to `by .bucket` fails on the missing `bucket` field and rolls back, even when both source columns already exist and no references need translation. Migration must preserve or account for the predecessor representation before candidate projection.

Activation has already destructively projected those rows using the candidate columns ([store/activation.rs:315](/home/ccheever/projects/sb4-w12-lang/snapback4/crates/snapback4-core/src/store/activation.rs:315)). Consequently, upgrading a populated 0.4.28 store while changing `view totals: count entries by .n` to `by .bucket` fails on the missing `bucket` field and rolls back, even when both source columns already exist and no references need translation. Migration must preserve or account for the predecessor representation before candidate projection.
